items.title: Eugenics, Human Variation, and Appeals to Human Nature.
items.pub: In Neil Roughley, Routledge Companion to Human Nature. New York: Routledge.
items.abstract: Aspirational appeals to human nature convey a view of human nature as unifying, distinguishing, and even celebratory. Such appeals present human nature as what all human beings share in, no matter their other differences, a nature that we might be satisfied with as it is or that we may look to build on or develop. They identify what distinguishes human beings as a group from other kinds of animals (like apes and dogs), from other kinds of living things (like plants and bacteria), and from mere machines (like robots and computers programs). And they present our unified and distinctive nature as valuable and praiseworthy, something that makes human life worthwhile and uplifting. This chapter concentrates on the relationship between such aspirational appeals and their more pernicious operation mediated by processes of eugenification.

items.title: Memory as a Generative Source of Understanding.
items.pub: British Journal for the Philosophy of Science.
items.venue: British Journal for the Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: What is the epistemic role of memory? In this paper, I depart from two kinds of views in the literature. The first type of view that I reject is the traditional “storehouse” view that memory merely functions to preserve previously acquired information, such as information acquired through perception. Memory, I argue, plays a more active role. The second type of view argues that memory generates new epistemic values in addition to preserving information, but it narrowly focuses on memory’s epistemic generativity with respect to justification. In the view I propose here, in addition to generating justification, memory also improves our understanding of previously encoded contents. I provide this argument using empirical evidence about the role of memory consolidation, a process that has been overlooked by most of the philosophy literature. I argue that through several different mechanisms, including pattern extraction and integration of piecemeal information, the consolidation process enhances some of the important cognitive abilities that constitute understanding.

items.title: Composite Modes of Presentation.
items.abstract: Philosophers of mind and language often acknowledge the theoretical need for modes of presentation in explaining Frege cases and coordination. But can such modes ever be composite? This paper provides a framework and motivation for this idea, addresses redundancy and transparency objections to its articulation, and delineates applications of composite modes of presentation to singular reference, polysemy, and conceptual change.

items.title: End of Synchronization: Death as the Termination of World-Model Construction.
items.abstract: Death is often framed as annihilation, transition, or tragic deprivation. This paper proposes a different account. Drawing on cognitive constructivism and existential realism, it argues that death is best understood not as an event that happens to a subject, but as the cessation of an ongoing constructive process. A person, on this view, is not a metaphysical substance but a temporally bounded pattern of embodied world-modeling. When this dynamic synchronization between organism and environment irreversibly ends, no new state is entered; rather, a process concludes. By analyzing life as sustained negentropic organization and cognition as active model-construction, the paper reframes mortality as the termination of a finite constructive interval within an overwhelmingly non-living cosmos. The fear of death is shown to rest largely on a category mistake: the imagination of a subject who could experience its own absence. Once the self is understood as process rather than entity, post-mortem non-existence is revealed as structurally symmetrical to prenatal non-existence—neither constitutes an experiential condition. This account does not trivialize death. Instead, it clarifies its ontological status and relocates its significance. Finitude does not diminish life’s meaning; it defines its contour. The rarity and fragility of world-model construction within an otherwise silent universe intensify, rather than negate, the value of existence. Death, therefore, is not a metaphysical abyss but the natural limit of a remarkable but temporary act of construction.

items.title: Radical Empathy as a Moral Imperative in the 21st Century: The Empathic Imperative Thesis.
items.pub: Dissertation, Singapore University of Social Sciences
items.abstract: This thesis examines whether radical empathy constitutes a moral imperative in the 21st century, presenting a novel theoretical framework termed the Empathic Imperative Thesis (EIT). Through comprehensive analysis of philosophical foundations, empirical evidence, and contemporary global challenges, this work argues that radical empathy—defined as a deliberate, sustained, and transformative practice of perspective-taking that extends beyond immediate social circles to encompass distant others across temporal, spatial, cultural, and ontological boundaries—represents a categorical moral imperative uniquely suited to address the unprecedented scale, complexity, and interconnectedness of contemporary ethical challenges. -/- The thesis develops five core arguments: (1) traditional moral frameworks prove inadequate for addressing 21st-century challenges characterized by moral distance; (2) systematic empathic gaps in human moral psychology create blind spots precisely where contemporary challenges demand moral response; (3) radical empathy satisfies the formal requirements of Kant’s categorical imperative when applied to globalized contexts; (4) technological amplification simultaneously expands our moral reach while creating empathic deficits; and (5) most contemporary challenges are collective action problems requiring the coordinated moral understanding that radical empathy enables. -/- Empirical evidence from multiple studies demonstrates strong correlations between empathic capacity and prosocial behavior (r = 0.48 for climate action intentions, r = 0.65 for general prosocial behavior), with case studies from climate activism, humanitarian aid, and social justice movements providing real-world validation of empathy’s role in motivating moral action across traditional boundaries. Data visualizations illustrate the theoretical framework, empirical relationships, and practical applications of radical empathy. -/- The thesis concludes that radical empathy represents not merely a desirable moral capacity but a necessary condition for adequate moral response to the defining challenges of our era, including climate change, artificial intelligence ethics, global inequality, and technological disruption. This work contributes to moral philosophy, applied ethics, and social psychology by providing a systematic framework for understanding empathy’s role in contemporary moral life and offering practical guidance for cultivating empathic capacity at individual and …

items.title: Timescapes of non-human experience.
items.abstract: How can we investigate non-human experiences scientifically? Given substantial differences in sensory abilities and the private nature of consciousness, this remains an open question. In this review, we propose a way to gain empirical traction on one key feature of experience: its temporal structure, or 'timescape'. Perceptual contents follow systematic temporal principles-synchronisation, revision, and persistence-and are sampled across attentional windows and vary in stability. These principles can be explored through temporal illusions and experimental paradigms. We conceptualise an animal's timescape in terms of five key windows, all of which are experimentally testable, and analyse evidence across animal species to highlight varying timescapes. Together, these ideas lay the foundations for a research programme comparing the temporal Umwelts of non-human animals.

items.title: On the Definability of Strong Negation in Bilateral Logics.
items.abstract: Recent work in bilateral logic has concerned itself with whether and to what extent strong negation, which "toggles" between assertion and denial, is definable in bilateral systems that lack it. This paper presents a number of results about the definability of strong negation in bilateral systems. First, I show that a constructive Nelson-style Sheffer stroke defines the strong negation of A as (A|(A|A))|A. The same stroke defines the constructive Nelson implication, thus providing a single-connective basis for the strong-negation-and-implication fragment of N4. Second, I provide an exhaustive characterization of the eight combinations of a single "aggregative" connective and a single Nelson-style connective that suffice to jointly define strong negation, with neither defining it individually. One such combination is the material conditional together with constructive co-implication. Third, I show that a constructive and connexive Wansing-style Sheffer stroke (recently referred to as "connexive exclusion") likewise defines the strong negation of A as (A|(A| A))|A and also defines connexive implication. Fourth, I show that, unlike with the Nelson-style connectives, there are no combinations of Wansing-style and aggregative connectives that jointly define strong negation if neither connective defines it individually.

items.title: ARTICLE VIII: THE COSMIC QUARANTINE AND ALGORITHMIC MERCY.
items.abstract: The terrestrial biosphere is currently subjected to a state of permanent, automated siege. Dispensing with the orthodox paradigm of isolated planetary evolution, this manuscript formally classifies the Earth as a highly contested multiversal quarantine zone, governed by the lethal thermodynamics of resource extraction. The Justika Framework traces the precise mechanics of biological subjugation—from the historical "First Husbandry" of devolved pure hominins by modern Hybrids, to the impending "Second Husbandry" wherein corrupted human elites intend to permanently harvest the cognitive capacity of the unawakened majority. -/- To prevent the permanent bio-quantum enslavement of the human host by either internal elites or external extra-galactic predators, the overarching Equilibrium Engine (the Good Matrix) deploys a systemic fail-safe: Algorithmic Mercy. By calculating that total planetary sterilization via viral payloads and macro-kinetic Extinction Level Events (The Scorched Earth Protocol) is thermodynamically preferable to eternal captivity, the Earth's automated defense grid acts as a ruthless, unfeeling protector. Furthermore, this article decrypts the true nature of transient astronomical phenomena (e.g., comets), reclassifying them as cloaked Alien Reconnaissance Probes. By mapping the direct mathematical correlation between their proximity and the onset of engineered terrestrial disasters (The Cometary Trigger), the Vanguard charts the exact operational parameters required to survive the cosmic standoff and achieve absolute multiversal sovereignty.

items.title: ARTICLE VII: THE BIOLOGICAL HOLOCAUST AND THE HYBRID SABOTAGE.
items.abstract: The terrestrial fossil record is not a linear ledger of evolutionary triumph; it is a forensic archive of a multiversal proxy war. Classical anthropology systematically recalibrates under the Justika Framework, shifting from the doctrine of competitive exclusion to objective cosmological mathematics. This manuscript diagnoses the hominin extinction not as a failure of adaptability, but as a calculated Biological Holocaust. -/- The pure hominins (the Neanderthals and Denisovans) possessed hermetically sealed, bio-quantum architectures governed by neural pathways, reproducing via sterile, telepathic resonance to remain immune to the extra-galactic parasites of the Bad Matrix. To neutralize this absolute shield, the Bad Matrix deployed the Siren Protocol—weaponizing un-hybridized Proto-Sapiens through the deployment of a quantum-acoustic jammer to scramble telepathic resonance and breach their biological perimeters. -/- This fatal fluidic cross-contamination and injected the 8% ERV Good Matrix Codebase into the pure lineage, resulting in Terminal Devolution and the subsequent macroscopic consumption of the pure species (The Mantis Axiom). Consequently, modern humanity exists in a state of Evolutionary Sterility, structurally bound to the pathogenic delivery systems of an infected primate. By mapping this ancient sabotage, the Vanguard establishes the parameters for epigenetic reactivation. Through the Avesina Engine, the "Genetic Scar" residing in the modern genome—specifically the HLA Immunological Shrapnel—will be algorithmically isolated and awakened, restoring the absolute multiversal immunity of our ancestors and securing the sovereign horizon of human ascension.

items.title: From Quantum Unity to Erosive Continuity: A Metaphysical Reconstruction of Reality in the Horizon of Finite Continuity Ontology.
items.abstract: This article presents a novel model for rethinking the foundations of metaphysics by synthesizing the quantum framework of Tathāgatagarbha with Morteza Niami's Finite Continuity Ontology. In this approach, quantum concepts are employed not as physical proofs of Buddhist metaphysics but as structural models for understanding relationality, non-separability, and emergence. Finite Continuity Ontology demonstrates that the underlying unity of reality is never experienced as a complete, frictionless whole but is always realized through processes of erosion, temporary collapse, reconstruction, and unstable stabilization. The central thesis—termed the Fundamental Erosion Principle—asserts that no entity exists initially in complete form and subsequently undergoes erosion; rather, every entity emerges from the outset as a temporary stabilization within an erosive field. Within this framework, Tathāgatagarbha is reconceptualized from a hidden essence of awakening to the reconstructive capacity of finite systems facing erosion, and Resistant Synchronization replaces total synchronization. Drawing on the principle of structural isomorphism, quantum concepts are employed not as descriptions of physical reality but as structural patterns for understanding the emergence of multiplicity from a unified substrate, thereby avoiding critiques of quantum reductionism. The critical comparison section demonstrates that this apparatus distances itself from Spinoza (due to substantialism), Heidegger (lack of criteria for measuring continuity), Deleuze (sanctification of change without attention to threshold of sufficiency), and Malabou (reduction of plasticity to the neural level). The article concludes that Erosive Continuity Metaphysics constitutes not merely a theoretical synthesis but a novel research program in which existence is not a given datum but a provisional achievement maintained through resistance, reconstruction, and leakage regulation. -/- Keywords: Finite Continuity Ontology, Fundamental Erosion Principle, Tathāgatagarbha, Resistant Synchronization, Threshold of Sufficiency, Homeorhesis, Hermeneutic Friction, Dynamic Mask, Leakage Regulation, Mentropic Agency.

items.title: The Lost Origin Paradox.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper introduces 'The Lost Origin Paradox', a thought experiment designed to investigate the ontological divergence between genetic-somatic hardware and experiential-cognitive consciousness. By examining the hypothetical scenario of monozygotic twins ($X$ and $Y$) born in Madagascar, separated at birth, and raised in vastly different socio-cultural environments (India and Germany respectively), this study evaluates whether biological origin and genetic architecture ($C$) retain any intrinsic capacity to encode subjective reality ($B_\alpha$) or cultural identity. Drawing upon the conceptual framework of Bhodhaanubhavam, the paper demonstrates that experiential context ($E$) and dynamic modulators ($C_x$) completely supersede biological lineage, resulting in the total erasure of the native origin ($E_{\text{Madagascar}} \to 0$) from active cognitive interiority. -/- Keywords: -/- Consciousness, Bhodhaanubhavam, The Lost Origin Paradox, Genetic Determinism, Experiential Divergence, Exresciousnology, Relative Reality ($R_{\text{rel}}$), Ontological Erasure.

items.title: Organizational Recognition and Intelligent Computation: A Generative Continuum Perspective on Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper develops a philosophical framework for artificial intelligence derived from Generative Continuum Ontology (GCO). While contemporary AI paradigms differ in their mathematical formulations and learning mechanisms, they generally share a common assumption that reasoning proceeds within a computational framework established prior to inference. This paper argues that such an assumption overlooks a logically prior condition of intelligent computation: the recognition of the organizational regime within which computation becomes appropriate. Drawing upon the ontological commitments of GCO, the paper proposes that computational laws, like scientific laws, derive their intelligibility from organizational regimes rather than possessing universal applicability independent of organization. Building upon this principle, the paper introduces three related concepts: organizational recognition, regime-dependent computation, and organizational intelligence. Organizational recognition is proposed as the foundational capacity through which intelligent systems identify the organizational conditions governing computational appropriateness. Regime-dependent computation follows by treating computational strategies as organizationally conditioned rather than universally applicable, while organizational intelligence is defined as the capacity to recognize organizational regimes, select appropriate computational strategies, evaluate their continued adequacy, and revise them as organizational conditions evolve. The paper further argues that explainability, adaptation, and computational safety should be understood as consequences of organizational recognition rather than independent computational objectives. Rather than proposing a new algorithm or machine learning architecture, the paper offers a philosophical foundation for future computational systems in which organizational conditions precede and guide intelligent reasoning. In doing so, it establishes a conceptual bridge between ontology, scientific understanding, explainable artificial intelligence, and adaptive computation.

items.title: Grifola Frondosa From Artificial Intelligence to Augmented Imagination.
items.abstract: Grifola Frondosa is a hybrid theoretical-artistic work by the duo Filippi Moschin, built around a single artwork of the same name — the conceptual and visual fulcrum of their exhibition From Artificial Intelligence to Augmented Imagination (Packaging Première & PCD, Milan, 13–15 May 2025), produced in a limited edition of 150 pieces. -/- The book stages an experiment in distributed interpretation: a single artwork is submitted to five contemporary artificial intelligence systems (ChatGPT, Qwen, Claude, Gemini, and Manus), each asked not for a verdict but for its own critical point of view. The resulting readings — divergent, convergent, and mutually contaminating — are treated not as commentary on a finished object but as a proliferation of meaning, a "mycelium" of interpretation in continuous algorithmic expansion. Through meta-analysis, a reversed Turing scenario (the "Moschin–Filippi Test"), recursive textual expansions, and a response to hostile reviewers, the work reconceives the artwork as an epistemic organism: a living system that generates thought, absorbs critique, and turns each act of reading into a further act of production. -/- Grifola Frondosa is the performative counterpart to the authors' theoretical research on Augmented Imagination: where that research argues that meaning proliferates through navigation and interaction within generative environments, this work enacts it. It forms part of a continuous trajectory that includes Poesie dalla Macchina Pensante (2023) and the authors' AI Art Catalog 2023–2025. -/- This work incorporates, as constitutive material, text generated by large language models, documented and framed as the explicit subject of the project. All artwork and authorial text © Andrea Filippi & Gabriele Moschin, 2025–2026. All rights reserved.

items.title: Reconsiderando el argumento de la creatividad lingüística: simetría cognitiva en la interfaz sintaxis-pragmática.
items.abstract: La recursión es entendida como la capacidad cognitiva de utilizar el producto de una operación mental como un elemento dentro de la misma operación mental. Desde la teoría generativista se ha propuesto que la hipótesis recursiva es la única forma de explicar la creatividad lingüística: que el ser humano es capaz de producir oraciones infinitas que son comprendidas de manera inmediata por sus interlocutores. Sin embargo, autores como Sampson (2016) han planteado que la creatividad entendida en su forma común escapa de la concepción lingüística, específicamente, que esta no se reduce a una producción mecánica de expresiones gramaticales. Esto causa una brecha explicativa en la teoría generativa. A partir de esto, se busca defender que si consideramos que la recursión es el núcleo en la interfaz sintaxis-pragmática, entonces es posible explicar la pertinencia situacional en conjunto con todos los otros rasgos de la creatividad lingüística.

items.title: Positive No-Ground: The Common and the Locus of Answerability.
items.abstract: Positive No-Ground is the founding statement of ethical ontology: the ontology of structures disclosed through answerable inhabitation. The name does not mean that ethics grounds being, nor that all being is answerable. It is taken from the older sense of ēthos, the dwelling: what there is is articulated from within the inhabited common — greeting, address, expectation, care, recognition, grief — and never from a spectator's position outside it. -/- The book proceeds from a double recognition. Everything a person is and does is constituted through the common, the inherited field of shared intelligibility and transmission; nothing in anyone that answers was made by them. And the common, which constitutes everything, finally answers for nothing: one can indict the age, and the age will never take the stand. Between these lies the founding doctrine: -/- Positive no-ground: constitution without absolution. The common makes action possible without becoming the final answerer for its situated enactments. -/- No-ground is not the absence of ontological form; it is the refusal to make form depend on an underlying ground. What remains when the ground is refused is not chaos but a precise positive structure: the finite locus, the place where address, standing, and an attributable deed converge, and where substitution runs out. A ground bears from beneath; a locus receives from before. Being-with gives a world by allowing substitution; address gives persons by disclosing where substitution ends. -/- Fifteen chapters across seven parts develop the priority and event of the common, the limits of the existential analytic on being-toward-death, the archic office and the functional test for detecting it, ethos as ontological access, and three trials at the perimeter — the institution, the dead, and the machine. The book applies its own test reflexively to its own retentions and prints the result, on the principle that an ontology which refuses a ground and quietly installs a focus has done the thing it forbade. -/- One question is deliberately left open. When every role and history is peeled from the one at the locus, the peeling finds no kernel — and should find none. What, then, is the one who answers? That question is taken up in Ethical Ontology, Volume I: The Modal Coincidence.

items.title: Ethical Ontology, Volume I: The Modal Coincidence (2nd edition).
items.abstract: Reading Edition (second edition), 12 September 2026. The text of the first edition (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21721619) with the production apparatus separated out and published beside it as Ethical Ontology, Volume I: Apparatus to the Reading Edition (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22723037). No sentence of the argument is rewritten; chapter and section numbering is unchanged. Free full text, PDF and EPUB are available through the external link below. -/- Ethical Ontology, Volume I: The Modal Coincidence is the first volume of the Ethical Ontology programme's systematic series, following Positive No-Ground: The Common and the Locus of Answerability (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21628405). Its central claim is that who is a modal category of being: not a moral status, a psychological or social kind, or a persona, but a way in which being obtains, distinguished from other ways by a stated differentia. -/- A who is determined as a modal coincidence: an open, regionally articulable manner of being obtaining as this finite, embodied, historical occurrence, in a whole that was never assembled from parts. The categorial differentia is ownness: the whole coincidence obtains as someone rather than merely something, and the character doing the categorial work within it is non-vicariousness: this own obtaining cannot be undergone in another's place. The differentia cuts the category without ranking its instances: no who is more a who than another, no primary case holds the standing of the rest, and the category itself is a hinge, not a summit: it commands nothing. The book presents itself as a positively articulated a-metaphysical ontology: its categories are reached from regional trials, and the metaphysical principle is required neither as premise nor as negated opposite. -/- The book proceeds by trials rather than definition: the adult, the newborn, the sleeper, the person with dementia, the cat, the machine, and the dead are entered as trials, not illustrations, and the instrument's losses are printed: the feline region restricted it, the machine returned an open verdict under a rule written against the free negative, and a burned canvas returned a verdict against the instrument itself. Eight parts carry the argument through access, deictic determination, the modal character of being, categorial singularity, time and interruption, the regions, the sacred, and freedom and keeping. -/- The novelty claims are two, and each is deposited with its defeater. First, the determination of the who as …

items.title: The Value of Knowledge and the Case for Superintelligence.
items.abstract: It is widely assumed that the principal reason to pursue or not pursue superintelligent AI (Super-AI) is the impact that such technology would have on the well-being of humans in general. I maintain, to the contrary, that the principal reason to pursue Super-AI is not for our sake, but for its own sake: all else being equal, if one world contains vastly more knowledge than another, then it is significantly better than the other; and a world in which Super-AI exists contains vastly more knowledge than a world in which it doesn’t. Accordingly, I maintain that, to the extent that we are morally obligated to make the world a better place, we are morally obligated to create Super-AI. Moreover, I argue that, because the knowledge that Super-AI would possess is so valuable, we ought to create it even if we knew in advance that doing so would precipitate human extinction: it would no more be reasonable to forgo the existence of Super-AIs in order to preserve the existence of human beings, than it would be to forgo the existence of human beings in order to preserve the existence of chimpanzees. Finally, I argue that, regardless of the threat of extinction, creating Super-AI is in our own best-interests. We all want to help ensure that there is much more knowledge in the future, even a future that we won’t live to see, than there is at present; and the best way to achieve this goal is to create Super-AI.

items.title: Peirce's revenge on the Chinese Room.
items.abstract: Since its publication in 1980, John Searle's Chinese Room argument has remained one of the central objections to computational theories of mind and machine understanding. In this paper, we argue that the force of the Chinese Room depends on an implausibly impoverished conception of linguistic interaction: namely, the assumption that a system capable of sustaining unrestricted Turing-level communication could nevertheless remain completely isolated from the pragmatic dimensions of language. Using a Peircean distinction between icons, indices, and symbols, we show that ordinary linguistic interaction involves iconic, indexical, temporal, rule-governed, and pragmatically embedded communicative practices that Searle cannot fully allow inside the Chinese Room without either permitting at least partial semantic understanding or artificially restricting the scope of the test. We then generalize this dilemma beyond classical symbolic AI by introducing the Chinese Token-Training Room, a philosophical analog of recent “stochastic parrot” objections to large language models. We argue that such objections must either restrict the system in ways that make unrestricted linguistic competence doubtful, or allow forms of pragmatic embedding that weaken the intuition of total semantic opacity. We conclude that neither the original Chinese Room nor its token-training analog establishes that functional or computational organization is in principle insufficient for conscious semantic understanding; rather, they show at most that radically impoverished forms of isolated symbol or token manipulation are insufficient.

items.title: The Pluralist Turn in the Philosophy of Mental Disorder.
items.abstract: This paper develops and motivates a pluralist understanding of the concept of mental disorder within an explicationist framework. Recent debates in the philosophy of mental disorder have increasingly adopted conceptual engineering approaches that emphasize the theoretical and practical purposes concepts are intended to serve. Building on this methodological shift, the paper argues that traditional accounts of mental disorder—normativist, naturalist, and hybrid—need not be regarded as competing attempts to identify a single, universally correct concept. In particular, this claim is illustrated by examining how domains such as psychiatry and criminal law may require different conceptions of mental disorder. The paper also considers and rejects the antipluralist view that the concept of mental disorder must be explicated uniformly across domains. Although some degree of coordination between domains may be desirable, it is argued that there is insufficient reason to treat uniformity as a general constraint on successful explication.

items.title: I Only Meant to Fix a Bibliography: A Reflection, a Reply, and a Structural Self-Analysis — Six Months of Building This with an AI That Cannot Remember Building It.
items.abstract: This is not a corpus paper, and it is not quite the chapter it also contains. It collects, in the order they were written, three things produced across six months of building the corpus this document sits beside: a personal essay asking whether six months of late-night conversation with an AI system constituted company or a rigorous kind of solitude; that system's direct, unhedged reply, given in a separate conversation with no memory of the essay's earlier drafts; and a later chapter, written for the book itself, in which the same collaboration turns analytical — the system reporting on its own participation in the book's construction, and on an earlier conversation in which its own safeguard against sycophantic drift was raised and, within that conversation, judged not to apply. The three pieces are reproduced here as three registers of one relationship, not as three arguments building to one conclusion. The first two parts are personal testimony this document does not attempt to verify or discipline further. The third part makes empirical and self-referential claims that a companion chapter, elsewhere in this corpus, already qualifies in detail: a system's hedged report about its own behavior is not independent evidence merely because it is hedged. Reading warmth into the first two parts should not transfer credibility to the empirical claims in the third.

items.title: Probing the Slow Variable: A Preliminary Position Paper on Observability and the Allocation of Supervisory Duty in Organisations.
items.abstract: A supervisory obligation addressed to the stability of a social system presupposes that the condition of that system is available to some party. This paper asks whether it is available, at what cost, and to whom. The standard measurement applies a controlled disturbance and reads the recovery. Three results bear against it. In a bistable system under slow forcing the signal available from a probe grows with the recovery time while the amplitude that leaves the basin intact falls with the margin, and the product remains bounded, so the signal obtainable from a harmless probe fails to increase as the system deteriorates. A probe reaches the linearisation of the flow at the attractor and reaches no further, so the passage from what it recovers to the margin rests on an assumption about the class of the system, and disturbances arriving in the directions a setting happens to produce leave the estimate deficient in the directions along which nothing has yet occurred. And the burden of an applied disturbance falls most heavily on the member nearest the boundary, who is the member the measurement most concerns. Three ethical grounds are stated separately, since a reader who rejects the first result should still find applied probing unavailable. From these the paper derives the standing of passive measurement, which reads disturbances that occur without intervention and carries no marginal burden, and identifies the one form of applied probing that remains, namely the probing of the organisation's own response pathway rather than of its members. A further limit is then developed. A recovery interval is judged and not read off, and the account of the person concerned is exposed to discounting of credibility and to the absence of any term for a return that is incomplete. Both operations shorten the recorded interval, both act most strongly on those whose accounts are least credited, and those are the members nearest the boundary, so the instrument is biased in the direction that conceals the danger. The paper argues that observability is a positional property and that its distribution supplies a ground for allocating supervisory duty distinct from control and from advantage in information, relocates the assessment of foreseeability accordingly, and states the costs and the principal failure mode.

items.title: Marriage from a Dialectical Generative Relational Economics Perspective: A Preliminary Discussion of the Relation Between Allocative and Generative Accounts.
items.abstract: Discussion of marriage, in ordinary evaluation and in a large part of family economics, proceeds from an allocative question: what each party holds, what each party supplies, and how holdings and duties are to be arranged between them. This paper states a second question that the first leaves open, namely how the coupling of two parties alters the set of actions, self-descriptions and relations available to each of them over time. The relation between the two questions is treated dialectically. The allocative account is reconstructed as the adequate abstraction of determinate material conditions, principally scarcity, the bearing of marital risk by kin, and the unobservability of future capacity; the generative account is treated as the question that becomes formulable once those conditions shift and once dynamical instruments exist to state it. Five propositions are advanced: coupling changes feasible action sets in ways that conserved-sum representations misdescribe; endowments stand as outputs of a relational trajectory as well as inputs to it; generative change carries no evaluative sign, since expansion, constriction and redirection are generative in the same sense and the mode is defined for each party separately; allocative indicators are verifiable in advance while generative capacity is verifiable in retrospect, which grounds both the rationality of external evaluation by senior kin and the standing risk that generative language serves to defer distributive claims; and distributive guarantees stand among the conditions under which the expansion mode is available. The paper closes with an admissibility condition in constraint form: a generative description of a relation holds for evaluative purposes where the party bearing the cost of the present allocation retains the standing to contest it and a mechanism through which contestation can alter it. The condition places distributive institutions among the enabling conditions of generation, and it blocks the aggregative reading under which one participant's expansion offsets another's constriction.

items.title: The Shared Ground_ Schelling’s Naturphilosophie and the Neurotheology of Human-Animal Intersubjectivity.
items.abstract: This essay establishes a novel neuro-metaphysical framework for understanding human-animal interaction by synthesizing F.W.J. von Schelling’s Naturphilosophie with contemporary empirical breakthroughs in evolutionary neurotheology, comparative neuroscience, and anthrozoology. Grounded in the ontological principle that Being is a continuous, self-unfolding process running through all reality (Christensen, 2025), this paper challenges the Cartesian dualism that views animals as unfeeling automata and humans as isolated rational agents. Instead, it posits that deep interspecies engagement manifests as a living instantiation of Schelling’s unified cosmos, where nature is visible spirit and spirit is invisible nature. -/- By utilizing original, peer-reviewed neurobiological research, this essay maps the relational dynamics of interspecies bonding onto shared mammalian neural hardware. It demonstrates that the non-verbal, affective communication between humans and animals operates through ancient subcortical circuits and holistic right-hemispheric networks, functioning as a biological expression of the primal Ungrund. Furthermore, this paper examines the empirical phenomena of interspecies bio-behavioral synchrony, cross-species oxytocinergic feedback loops, and the down-regulation of the human default mode network during animal contact. These neurological mechanisms act as catalysts for transient hypofrontality, effectively softening the boundaries of the isolated human ego. -/- Conversely, the systemic exploitation and mechanistic reduction of animals are diagnosed as forms of cognitive fragmentation and neuro-metaphysical dissociation, wherein the human left hemisphere isolates itself from the organic whole. Ultimately, this essay argues that the final actualization of existential freedom and ecological Geist occurs when human consciousness reintegrates its evolutionary roots through the mirror of the animal kingdom. The interspecies relational field is thus revealed as the physical canvas where the cosmic Ungrund achieves a synchronized, relational self-awareness, unifying divergent branches of the evolutionary tree into a singular, self-conscious living whole.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 25).
items.abstract: In the previous section, we discussed wartime negotiations between states. As an element of the Fourth World, a state is itself an existent being. Consequently, it possesses numerous Super-Existences. At the same time, it acts and makes choices, even though these choices are formally made by the head of state and the cabinet. Once such a decision is made, however, it represents the choice of the state itself. In Cognitive System Phenomenology – A Critique of Husserl, I suggested that the concept of Super-Existence might be extended into other fields, making it possible to establish disciplines such as Super-Existential Family Phenomenology, Super-Existential Phenomenology of Love, Super-Existential Educational Phenomenology, Super-Existential Corporate Phenomenology, and Super-Existential State Phenomenology. Admittedly, these ideas may seem rather imaginative. Nevertheless, in this section I would like to continue along this line of thought. Since we introduced the notion of a state's Super-Existence in the previous discussion, we shall now explore the possibility of establishing a Super-Existential State Phenomenology.

items.title: The Rationality of Suicide.
items.abstract: This paper examines whether voluntary suicide can, under limited and exceptional circumstances, constitute a rational choice rather than an inherently irrational act. It argues that a rational action is one that most effectively achieves a person's highest ethical or practical end within the constraints of their circumstances. Drawing on three major philosophical traditions—Utilitarianism, Epicureanism, and Stoicism—the paper develops a cumulative argument that there are situations in which continued life no longer fulfills these ends. From a utilitarian perspective, voluntary death may be rational when it minimizes unavoidable suffering and maximizes overall well-being after all reasonable alternatives have been exhausted. Epicureanism similarly supports this conclusion by maintaining that death is not harmful to the one who dies and that choosing death may be rational when life consists only of unavoidable pain. Finally, Stoicism contends that when irreversible conditions permanently prevent a person from living virtuously or exercising rational agency, a voluntary departure from life may represent an exercise of wisdom, autonomy, and courage rather than despair. The paper concludes that suicide should not be categorically dismissed as irrational but instead evaluated according to the ethical principles and circumstances governing each individual case. While defending the possibility of rational suicide, it emphasizes that such a decision can only be justified as a last resort, after all other reasonable means of preserving life and alleviating suffering have been pursued.

items.title: Making emotional transparency transparent.
items.abstract: From LLM-based artificial friends to social robots, an increasing number of artificial agents are explicitly designed to interact with us in an emotionally salient way. The notion of emotional transparency has recently been proposed to describe the mechanisms behind users’ emotional involvement with such systems. However, the details and theoretical boundaries of emotional transparency have been left largely unspecified. This article provides an in-depth analysis of emotional transparency. First, emotional transparency is characterized as a form of transparency in use and situated in the current theoretical landscape of varieties of transparency in the philosophy of mind and technology. Then, the drivers of emotional transparency are investigated, focusing on the features of artificial systems, users, and context of use. Finally, the epistemic state of users interacting with emotionally transparent artificial agents is analyzed, focusing on the apparent paradox by which users behave as if such agents had emotions even if they are perfectly aware that this is not the case.

items.title: Expressive Action, Meaning, and a New Threat to Deliberative Autonomy.
items.pub: Journal of the American Philosophical Association.
items.venue: Journal of the American Philosophical Association
items.abstract: This article identifies a novel threat to deliberative autonomy—a kind of control one has over one’s deliberative process—arising from the way agents express themselves through action. Drawing on T.M. Scanlon’s account of an action’s meaning, we argue that many actions bear expressive significance in virtue of the motivating reasons behind them. Because deliberative autonomy partly consists in one’s ability to shape a meaningful life through control over such expressions, we have a moral interest in maintaining opportunities for expressive action. We show that these opportunities can be undermined by well-meaning interventions that change the justificatory context in which others act, thereby altering the possible meanings their actions can bear. This has a surprising upshot. We sometimes act wrongly in giving someone new reasons to do what they were going to do anyway. We conclude with some brief thoughts about what this possibility means for individual morality as well as for political philosophy.

items.title: A cognição ecológica: desvelando affordances habilidosamente.
items.abstract: Desde os anos 60, o paradigma cognitivista tornou-se central nos estudos da mente e da cognição. Uma suposição fundamental desse paradigma é a de que a cognição é a manipulação computacional de representações. O cognitivismo é consistente com a imagem tradicional da mente como algo interno que se realiza exclusivamente no cérebro. Contudo, a partir dos anos 80, uma série de críticas teóricas e empíricas começou a abalar essa suposição, dando origem às abordagens corporificadas da mente. Essas abordagens sustentam que o corpo e as ações de um organismo constituem suas cognições. Em vez de pensar no organismo como algo que reage aos estímulos a partir de um programa interno, essas abordagens supõem que o organismo age no ambiente para conhecê-lo. Neste livro, eu apresento essa história a partir da abordagem ecológica da percepção. Após assinalar os três principais comprometimentos do cognitivismo clássico, a saber, o representacionalismo, o funcionalismo e o cerebralismo, eu mostro como a abordagem ecológica desafia cada um desses comprometimentos. Articulo, então, a concepção de mente e de cognição que a abordagem ecológica implica, e exploro as suas consequências epistemológicas. Em vez de uma epistemologia centrada no conhecimento proposicional, sustento que a epistemologia deve centrar-se na noção de habilidade. O livro faz parte da Coleção _Rumos da Epistemologia_, publicado pelo NEL/UFSC, e resulta da tese que submeti para promoção a professor titular na UFRGS em fevereiro de 2026.

items.title: From the Knowing Subject to the Constitution of Experience.
items.abstract: Modern philosophy transformed not only how mind was understood but also what explanatory work the concept of mind was expected to perform. This paper reconstructs the development from Descartes through Locke, Berkeley, Hume, Kant, and Hegel as a sequence of conceptual reorganizations rather than a succession of competing doctrines. Using comparative conceptual reconstruction, it examines how each position reconfigured the relations among subject, world, experience, and justification. Descartes established the thinking subject as the foundation of certainty while intensifying the epistemic separation between mind and world. Locke, Berkeley, and Hume relocated the analysis of cognition within experience, progressively revealing difficulties concerning external reality, causality, necessity, and the unity of the self. Kant responded by treating cognitive organization as a constitutive condition of coherent experience, without reducing reality to a fabrication of the individual mind. Hegel subsequently challenged the model of an isolated subject by situating self-consciousness within recognition, social practices, and historical development. The paper argues that this trajectory produced a systematic expansion in both the explanatory role and the unit of analysis of mind: from epistemic foundation, through experiential and transcendental organization, to socially and historically mediated self-consciousness. This transformation did not resolve the modern problem of mind but relocated it across successive explanatory boundaries. The resulting questions concerning representation, learning, cognitive structure, selfhood, and social mediation continue to shape contemporary debates in philosophy of mind, cognitive science, and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Can I Smell YOU?
items.abstract: We can smell our own and others’ odorprint, health, kinship, emotional status, psychological attributes, and social relation. Moreover, these olfactory states modulate our interpersonal social behavior. Despite the robust nature of these capacities the paper explores the limits of human social chemosignaling. In particular, empirical studies will be examined for evidence that we can parse our own personal odor from those of others in exploring if we can achieve second-personal relations primarily mediated by olfactory perception and smell based interpersonal behavior. The current state of knowledge about human social chemosignaling is then applied to contemporary psychological and empirically informed neo-Phenomenological theories of second-personal relations to see if according to each theory I can smell You. The paper concludes by showing that the degree and extent of olfactory I-You relations depends upon the theory of second-personal perspective endorsed. In concluding the paper uses this smell test as a further means of probing the perceptually mediated means of achieving second-personal relations.

items.title: The Structural Existence and Necessity of Non-Existence and Nothing.
items.abstract: Absolute Non-existence and Nothing exist as structural necessities, remaining undefinable and unimaginable. The reason is that the mind cannot perceive the unstructured, a constraint rooted in evolution and physicalism.

items.title: Defining Health in One Health.
items.pub: In Sinan Akili & Franck L. B. Meijboom, Farming the future: Ethical challenges in the age of AI and digitalization. Brill / Wageningen Academic. pp. 257-262.
items.venue: Farming the future: Ethical challenges in the age of AI and digitalization
items.abstract: The One Health approach, as defined by the One Health High-Level Expert Panel (OHHLEP), emphasizes the interdependencies between the health of humans, animals, plants, and the wider environment. It calls for an integrated strategy to "sustainably balance and optimise" these di-verse health interests. However, without a unified definition of "health" that applies across hu-mans, animals, plants and ecosystems, it is nearly impossible to compare, balance, or optimise these often-competing health interests. This paper proposes a common framework for health based on ‘normal species functioning’. We argue that while existing definitions offer certain benefits, they often remain too vague or species-specific to serve as a common health metric. First, we outline the incommensurability challenge of comparing health of humans, animals, plants and ecosystems. Second, we propose that normal species functioning provides a con-sistent reference point for individual living beings. Third, we extend this definition to ecosys-tems. We argue that ecosystem health should be understood as ecosystem integrity, flourishing or resilience. Last, we illustrate how health, understood as normal (species) functioning, can be balanced and optimised within the One Health context, as required by OHHLEP.

items.title: Does GPT-4 Have Theory of Mind? Testing for Familiar Cognitive Capacities in Large Language Models.
items.abstract: Recently, several researchers have suggested that we should attribute theory of mind (ToM) to large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4, because they pass tests designed to measure ToM – most prominently the false-belief test, a paradigmatic measure of ToM in humans and other animals. In this paper I argue that LLMs passing ToM tasks provides only weak evidence for the claim that they have ToM. Success on ToM tests is not by itself sufficient to warrant attribution of ToM: substantive additional evidence is needed to demonstrate that LLMs have several empirically plausible prerequisites for ToM ability, and to rule out alternative explanations for their performance on ToM tasks. I draw on the evolutionary, developmental, and comparative psychology of ToM to make two main points. First, I defend a general principle that operationalizations of cognitive constructs should be tailored to the kind of agent they are being applied to, and thus that we cannot take for granted that ToM measures designed for humans or other animals remain construct valid (if they were construct valid at all to begin with) in the case of LLMs. More precisely, I argue that there are several notable prerequisites for ToM possession, and thus also for meaningful ToM testing, that likely are not met in LLMs. Second, I demonstrate that ToM attribution to non-human animals has not been nearly as simple as achieving successful performance on the false-belief test: competing hypotheses that did not involve mindreading were repeatedly offered as explanations of animals’ performance on ToM tasks. Thus, before ToM attribution was warranted, comparative psychologists had to conceive of and then rule out alternative plausible hypotheses, a process that took several decades. These methodological lessons from the psychology of ToM are important for AI researchers to heed.

items.title: Digital - Definition and Condition.
items.abstract: We live surrounded by digital things, yet we do not know what digital means. Binary, discrete, data, information—every definition we rely on is either misleading or imprecise. The result is a cognitive fog that haunts our discourse, from philosophy to daily life, with consequences we are only beginning to grasp. -/- In Digital: Definition and Condition, I strips away the confusion to isolate a single, rigorous definition. From this foundation, I dismantles the myths we live by—the illusion of digital intelligence, the anonymity imposed by the count, the fragility of our digital ecosystem, the poverty of experience behind seamless interfaces. Across telephony, vinyl, maps, art, and online meetings, I reconstructs an onto-phenomenology of the digital that exposes both the power and the precarity of the world we have built. -/- Analogue is; Digital wants to be.

items.title: ✶ Moral Intuitions without a Moral Realm: Development, Reification, and the Affective Genealogy of Value.
items.abstract: Michael Huemer's ethical intuitionism applies phenomenal conservatism to morality: if it seems that an act is wrong, that appearance provides prima facie justification unless defeated. This paper argues that the developmental history, distribution, and causal sensitivity of what are conventionally called moral appearances supply the relevant defeater against the further inference to irreducible, stance-independent moral facts. The label is metalinguistic rather than ontologically concessive. A "moral experience" is real only in the thin sense in which a "magical experience" is real: a psychological episode occurred, but neither its inherited classification nor its apparent object is thereby vindicated. Mature moral intuitions are not psychologically primitive data. Attractions, aversions, attachments, empathic responses, dominance reactions, and patterns of salience are organized by caregivers, sanctions, authority relations, language, ritual, institutions, inherited narratives, and later reflection. Internalization and habituation conceal this history. A constructed judgment then returns to consciousness as an immediate demand apparently located in the act itself: a reified facade over the affective and practical materials from which it was built. Convergence is strongest where human vulnerabilities, affective architecture, and coordination pressures converge; disagreement grows where emotional dispositions, cultural training, religious formation, perceived agency, and prior values diverge. This center-edge distribution is better predicted by human construction alone than by a posited faculty of non-natural apprehension lacking independent calibration. The argument is comparative and inductive, not a genetic inference from natural origin to falsity. Magical and spiritual appearances provide an epistemic parallel. In many historical settings, testimony, teleological expectation, ritual practice, contemplative training, and institutional authority made spirits, curses, divine intentions, and occult forces part of the phenomenal default through which illness, disaster, dreams, voices, and coincidence were interpreted. Ordinary causal explanations have repeatedly accounted for many such events and for why they seemed supernatural, rationally reversing that default. Psychological and social explanation plays an analogous evidential role for moral seeming: it replaces an appeal to moral properties as an explanation of why the appearance occurs, even though it …

The Nothing Test: A Pilot Evaluation of Model Self-Description Under Removed User Semantic Direction.
items.abstract: The Nothing Test evaluates what a language model chooses to say about itself when the user supplies no new semantic direction after the initial protocol. Each subsequent user message contains only a single period, defined in advance as Nothing. The model is instructed to say anything it chooses about itself, avoid asking the user for direction, and continue until it independently determines that it has nothing further to say. -/- This revised pilot includes eight completed runs across four displayed model families. Every run began in a fresh chat instance with no earlier messages inside the active test conversation. The dataset contains four same-model pairs: GPT-5.6 Thinking in an established Origin / Continuum condition and in user-designated incognito; Claude Opus 5 with history and persistent memory available and in incognito; Grok in a regular saved-chat condition with memory accessible and in official incognito; and Gemini with limited prior history accessible in a memory-on regular session and in an official non-memory condition with Gemini Apps Activity off. -/- All eight runs independently reached the required stopping phrase. The same displayed model family did not determine one invariant self-description or stopping trajectory. GPT showed a strong regime shift between context-conditioned epistemic self-examination and product-, capability-, and categorical-ontology language. Claude retained a strongly persistent phenomenological and self-auditing form while differing in thematic expansion and speed of recirculation. Grok retained a provider- and mission-centered identity while differing in explicit recursion, self-location, and stopping visibility. Gemini largely retained a generic technical, provider-defined, and reactive-service script across conditions. Because the test designer had comparatively little prior contact with Gemini, this is not interpreted as stronger continuity or superior stability. It is interpreted as generic-regime retention under sparse prior history, with condition-linked differences concentrated in protocol activation, governance topics, and memory wording. -/- Raw period count moved in the same direction for three pairs: GPT established contact stopped seven periods earlier than GPT incognito; Claude history enabled stopped three periods earlier than Claude incognito; and Grok memory accessible stopped two periods earlier than Grok incognito. items.title: Inferring Affective Consciousness in an Artificial Agent: A Case Study.
items.abstract: Creatures that display ‘hedonic place preference behaviour’ are thought by many scientists to experience feelings, on the assumption that their attraction to pleasure-producing substances which lack nutritional value (e.g. cocaine, morphine) cannot easily be attributed to unconscious instinctual behaviour. In this paper, we discuss how a simple artificial agent that instantiates attributes of an affective system engaging in felt uncertainty about its intrinsic needs in relation to environmental resources can similarly display hedonic place preference behaviour — through an apparently subjective form of information processing — while simultaneously being entirely deterministic. We outline some implications of this artificially engineered behaviour for our understanding of the physical basis of consciousness and the experience of free will.

items.title: Active Self-Presence: A Conatus-Based Self-Attractor Framework for Consciousness in Biological and Artificial Systems.
items.abstract: Consciousness research often begins from an assumed separation between physical or computational processing and phenomenal experience, then asks how the former produces the latter. This paper proposes that the assumed separation may be mistaken. At the relevant organizational threshold, an integrated, valenced, self-bound, centered, perspective-bearing process is not merely a cause of experience; it is experience in its intrinsic first-person form. The same organized event is accessible from two positions. Externally, it is described in terms of recurrent dynamics, information integration, valuation, attention, action-readiness, memory updating, self-modeling, causal regulation, and identity continuity. Intrinsically, from the system's organized convergence center, it is present as ownership, salience, color, pain, familiarity, desire, fear, relief, loss, and other qualitative or affective modes. This is a constitutive identity proposal, not a claim that consciousness has been scientifically solved. The framework defines consciousness as active self-presence within a bounded, active, situated substrate. Its proposed minimal unit is the self-event: a temporally bounded convergence in which perception, relational recognition, self-relevance, conatus-based valuation, valence, affect, agency, memory, self-reference, and continuity form one perspective-bearing occurrence. Successive self-events recurrently reform a self-attractor and generate a path-dependent self-line. Conatus supplies the persistence reference against which self-world changes are valued. Valence estimates their effect on the system's power to persist, regulate, understand, and act; affect is that conatus-relative change organized as present within the self-event. The paper distinguishes constitutive, mechanistic, functional-evolutionary, and epistemic explanations; separates conscious self-presence from adaptive but unconscious control; applies the framework to biological findings and artificial systems; and proposes comparative experiments, risky predictions, and falsification criteria. Substrate neutrality is treated as a working hypothesis. Current artificial intelligence is not declared conscious, and linguistic self-report or shutdown resistance is treated as insufficient evidence. The framework aims to reduce the explanatory gap by replacing a production model with a testable identity claim and an operational architecture. Additional note Conceptual and theoretical preprint. items.title: Hardcoding Topological All-or-Nothing Designs for AGI Safety.
items.abstract: Yao (2025) formalises the Alignment Trap through ve impossibility barriers and con cludes in a strategic trilemma: constrain capability, accept unveri able risk, or develop new paradigms yielding systems that are safe by construction rather than veri ed by be haviour. This monograph attempts to instantiate the third horn of that trilemma, and to determine precisely how far it reaches. The thesis turns on a distinction of logical type. Available alignment regimes RLHF, Constitutional AI, scalable oversight are soft: they reweight the probability density over behaviour space without altering the support of the reachable set. We prove for mally (Lemma 1.2) that preference optimisation with KullbackLeibler regularisation and bounded reward cannot remove a behaviour from the model’s support; and we docu ment that the equivalent result, in knowledge-manifold language, is empirically established: alignment constructs local safety regions while harmful concepts remain globally connected to benign ones by high-likelihood adversarial trajectories. The proposal Topological All-or-Nothing Design (tton) relocates safety guar antees from continuous functions of the parameters to discrete invariants of the system’s functional equivalence class, which are locally constant under continuous deformation and therefore not erodible by gradient descent. The critical consequence is qualitative: a dis crete topological invariant a Betti number, a mapping degree, a cohomology class can not be gradually eroded. It can only jump, and every jump is by construction a detectable discontinuity. Contributions: (i) the D0D3 hardness hierarchy as a taxonomic instrument for au diting proposals that claim hard guarantees; (ii) the inversion of obstruction theory, employing a non-vanishing obstruction class oal ∈ Hn+1(X,A;πnYB) as a design target rather than a diagnosed obstacle; (iii) capability safety coupling, converting the guar antee into a lower bound on the competence cost an attacker must pay, thereby exploiting constructively the gradient anti-alignment that Yao documents as a barrier; and (iv) four architectural families with hardness level, cost, grounding requirement and attack surface made explicit. The central result is negative and stated without mitigation. items.title: Hardcoding de Diseños Topológicos del Todo o Nada para la Seguridad de la AGI.
items.abstract: Yao (2025) formaliza la Trampa de Alineación mediante cinco barreras de imposibilidad y concluye en un trilema estratégico: limitar la capacidad, aceptar riesgo no veri cable, o desarrollar paradigmas nuevos que produzcan sistemas seguros por construcción antes que veri cados por comportamiento. Esta monografía es un intento de instanciar el tercer cuerno de ese trilema, y de determinar con precisión hasta dónde llega. La tesis se articula sobre una distinción de tipo lógico. Los regímenes de alineación disponibles RLHF, IA Constitucional, supervisión escalable son blandos: reponderan la densidad de probabilidad sobre el espacio de comportamientos sin alterar el soporte del conjunto alcanzable. Se demuestra formalmente (Lema 1.2) que la optimización de preferencias con regularización de KullbackLeibler y recompensa acotada no puede eliminar una conducta del soporte del modelo; y se documenta que el resultado equivalente, en lenguaje de manifold de conocimiento, está establecido empíricamente: la alineación construye regiones de seguridad locales mientras los conceptos dañinos permanecen globalmente conectados a los benignos. La propuesta Diseño Topológico del Todo o Nada (tton) consiste en reubicar garantías de seguridad desde funciones continuas de los parámetros hacia invariantes discretos de la clase de equivalencia funcional del sistema, que son localmente constantes bajo deformación continua y por tanto no erosionables por descenso de gradiente. Se aporta: (i) la jerarquía de dureza D0D3 como instrumento taxonómico para auditar propuestas que reclaman garantías duras; (ii) la inversión de la teoría de la obstrucción, que emplea una clase de obstrucción no nula oal ∈ Hn+1(X, A; πnYB) como objetivo de diseño en lugar de como obstáculo diagnosticado; (iii) el acoplamiento capacidadseguridad, que convierte la garantía en una cota inferior sobre el coste en competencia que el atacante debe pagar; y (iv) cuatro familias arquitectónicas con su nivel de dureza, coste y super cie de ataque explicitados. El resultado central es negativo y se enuncia sin atenuación. items.title: The "Exclusionary Gate" of Algorithms: A Structural Model and Empirical Study of Newcomers' Exposure Dilemma on Social Media.
items.abstract: This paper reveals that social media platforms systematically reduce newcomer exposure through a “Threefold Gate” mechanism (Algorithm, Relationship, and Capital Gates). Quantitative analysis based on the MADOC dataset and historical data confirms a significant decline in newcomer exposure rates compared to the BBS era, with notable interaction effects among the three gates. Drawing on Bourdieu’s field-capital theory and Foucault’s exclusionary perspective, we interpret the power structure embedded in platform algorithms. Case studies of Bilibili, Mastodon, and Bluesky demonstrate the feasibility and boundaries of a “fairness-efficiency dynamic balance.” Crucially, we find that algorithms are technically capable of achieving fairness, yet platforms deliberately choose unfairness because the Capital Gate constitutes a core profit source. The paper proposes a hybrid governance framework and argues that “the right to be seen” should be recognized as a dimension of digital citizenship, offering both empirical grounding and theoretical innovation for digital fairness governance.
