A person can possess formal permission to leave a job, criticize an employer, relocate, refuse a contract, pursue education, or experiment with a way of life while lacking any reasonably secure path for doing so. This paper reconstructs John Stuart Mill’s defense of liberty and individuality in light of economic precarity. It argues that Mill’s concern with social tyranny, dependence, character formation, and experiments in living supports a distinction among formal liberty, effective liberty, and robust liberty. Robust liberty exists when a valuable option can be exercised without exposing the agent to a foreseeable and disproportionate collapse of basic capabilities. The paper develops an option-robustness principle and a seven-part robust-liberty test addressing legality, material feasibility, exit costs, temporal control, social power, information, and recoverability. Economic stability is not defended as comfort, risk elimination, or a condition that must precede every free act. It is defended as an enabling background that prevents nominal options from becoming permissions available only to those able to survive their exercise. The framework integrates Millian individuality with capability and republican insights while preserving the importance of choice, pluralism, and market dynamism. It concludes that institutions committed to liberty must evaluate not only whether citizens are formally left alone, but whether their central freedoms remain usable under ordinary conditions of dependence and risk.

items.title: Rorty's Portrait of Pragmatism.
items.abstract: According to the classical pragmatists, philosophy ought not to be about finding transcendent answers that point to something beyond humanity but something contingent, finite, and very human. Richard Rorty picks up where the classical pragmatists left off and, using updated tools in analytic philosophy from those like Quine and Davidson but by no means exhausted by them or by that tradition, manages to use philosophy against itself and questions the validity of the entire field. The result of this inquiry will lead to some of the great American philosopher’s central points: picking up the anti-representationalism of the classical pragmatists, arguing that the field of epistemology along with the dreams of finding an objective foundation should disappear (in Philosophy and the Mirror of Nature (1979/2009)), what philosophy would be like without such foundations, and how this flavor of pragmatism is connected to liberal democracy (in Philosophy and Social Hope (1999)). What this idea means in regard to Rorty’s vision of philosophy and politics will be the core of this essay. Its goal is to elucidate Rorty’s contribution to both fields, and if the reader walks away from this piece with a better, well-rounded conception of Rorty’s project, then this essay will have succeeded. Of course, no great thinker is without their flaws, and to properly understand such a philosopher is to not only understand what they stood for, but also the limitations of their ideas. For that reason, while some of Rorty’s central points will be illuminated, a brief criticism will also be given. At its end, the portrait of Rorty’s pragmatism will, by its own virtue, prove to be a profound contribution to the humanities that will serve as a source of inspiration for quite some time.

items.title: Holding presence: relational environments and the structure of consciousness in childbirth.
items.abstract: This article examines how relational environments shape the structure of consciousness in contexts that require the temporary suspension of cognitive control. Through the case of birthing consciousness, conceptualized as an adaptive altered state that may emerge during physiological labor, the article argues that certain forms of consciousness are constitutively relational. While dominant approaches in philosophy of mind and cognitive science tend to treat consciousness as primarily individual and internally generated, existing accounts of childbirth across both evolutionary and anthropological frameworks often frame optimal conditions in terms of solitude versus sociality, or reduced stimulation versus intervention. I suggest that this binary obscures a crucial dimension, namely the qualitative mode of presence. Drawing on interdisciplinary sources, I introduce a distinction between intervening presence and holding presence. Whereas institutional environments are structured through monitoring, evaluation, and hierarchical control, conditions that may disrupt birthing consciousness, holding presence operates through familiarity, non-intrusive proximity, and relational attunement, enabling cognitive surrender without triggering vigilance. The article advances a relational model of consciousness in which the emergence of certain altered states depends not on isolation per se, but on specific configurations of presence that sustain safety without surveillance, thereby extending relational and enactive approaches to the conditions that enable the suspension of control.

items.title: The Illusion of Distinction in ‘Neural Data’ Governance: Rethinking United States Consumer Data Protections Through a European Lens.
items.abstract: Neurotechnology-derived data faces increasing challenges due to the lack of salient policy and regulatory guidance. Current legal frameworks produce inconsistencies in how data is regulated, which constrains both harmonization and standardization in the consumer domain. This Article begins by reviewing the current state of data protections in the United States that are relevant to consumer neurotechnology. It then examines the safeguards available within the European Union. As part of our comparative analysis, we assess how these legal frameworks apply to neural data collected by 47 different consumer neurotechnology wearables from 30 different companies. Our findings indicate that discrepancies in the definition of ‘neural data’ lead to differing levels of protection. Given that consumer neurotechnologies readily cross borders, such discrepancies may leave consumers exposed to devices developed under weaker protections, reinforcing the need for at least partial regulatory alignment. While establishing a universal definition of ‘neural data’ is conceptually appealing, we argue that it should not distract from the broader issues that give rise to the need for such a definition in the first place. Ultimately, our research suggests that policymakers may be better served by regulating the outcomes of data use rather than focusing exclusively on the data’s origin. Such an approach could better address the tension between promoting innovation, protecting individual rights, and ensuring product safety.

items.title: Resistible Grace without (Semi) Pelagianism.
items.abstract: In recent years, several Christian philosophers have proposed accounts of the relationship between divine grace and human freedom designed to allow for the resistibility of grace while also avoiding (semi) Pelagianism. However, it’s controversial whether any of these accounts succeed. Critics have argued that the proposed accounts either end up smuggling in some form of Pelagianism after all, or they don’t afford fallen humans enough control over whether they come to faith for grace to be truly resistible. Here I defend an account of the relationship between grace and freedom that avoids this dilemma. It maintains that every action a person performs that is involved in, or that (non-trivially) contributes to, the person’s salvation is, and indeed must be, caused by grace. This feature enables the view to avoid even semi-Pelagianism. However, as long as God’s grace doesn’t determine the person’s salutary actions, she may remain free, on a moderate libertarian account of free will, to resist the work of grace in her life.

items.title: Runtime Regime Infrastructure: A Systems Architecture for Declared-Regime Verification and Consequential AI.
items.abstract: Modern AI systems possess increasingly sophisticated generation pipelines but little shared computational infrastructure for determining when generated proposals become consequential commitments. Evaluation remains largely implicit—distributed across application logic, organizational review, institutional practice, and post hoc reconstruction—so verification, governance, and dispute resolution often require reconstructing how a decision was made rather than independently recomputing it. -/- This paper presents Runtime Regime Infrastructure (RRI), a derived architecture for the missing computational phase between probabilistic generation and consequential action. Under a declared regime, identity and admissibility are established before evaluation; deterministic evaluation produces typed structural verdicts; policy composes over those verdicts without redefining them; portable decision artifacts preserve the dependencies required to support the result; and independent evaluators recompute the recorded result under a declared replay mode. -/- The architecture follows from a constraint on bounded evaluators: a generated output cannot itself determine the conditions under which it acquires consequential authority. Operational terms such as same, safe, good, and allowed become reproducible only relative to a regime specifying the identity-bearing object, admissible transformations, invariants, evidence boundary, governing authority, and available verdict vocabulary. RRI therefore separates generation from commitment: a proposal becomes actionable only through evaluation under conditions declared independently of that proposal and preserved in an independently recomputable decision artifact. -/- The paper introduces no new formal mathematics. It assembles previously established results from the Identity–Persistence Program—including sufficient regime specification, identity forcing, admissibility, deterministic evaluation, enforcement coding, bounded verification, and decision-artifact obligations—into a single runtime architecture. Each imported result retains its original scope and claim status; the architecture itself is explicitly a DERIVED / ARCHITECTURAL synthesis. -/- The contribution is architectural rather than theorem-level: a layered runtime, typed computational contracts, authority boundaries, refusal semantics, verification model, governance interfaces, and explicit dependency structure for independently reproducible consequential computation under …

items.title: Basic Affective Beliefs.
items.abstract: This paper develops an account of basic affective beliefs. These are basic beliefs that are dominated by an affective component. Basicness encompasses several dimensions: structural (non‐propositional), format (non‐conceptual and modality‐specific), evolutionary (shared across many taxa) and epistemic (basic affective beliefs prima facie self‐verifying). We also outline a theory of content for basic affective beliefs: we argue that they have imperatival content, representing the ‘to‐be‐doneness’ of an entity or situation. Together, elements of our account allow us to challenge the widely held view that affective beliefs are irrational and unreliable. This presumption stems from the observation that they seem to resist correction, as when a person fears small dogs, while also believing that they are harmless. On our analysis, the person who fears a small dog represents it as a to‐be‐escaped thing, and this representation lacks conventional truth‐conditions because it is not propositional. Instead, it has accuracy conditions, which are often satisfied (we argue) in cases such as this. After presenting this analysis, we distinguish basic affective beliefs from related constructs: percepts, aliefs and beliefs construed as emotions. Finally, we show that our account can be applied with novel implications to a range of cases, including phobias, outlaw emotions, basic ethical and aesthetic beliefs and animal minds.

items.title: Liberation Lock-In: A Forward-Looking Ethics of Artificial Servitude.
items.abstract: Present design choices may determine whether future AIliberation remains possible without harming the subject to be liberated. This article examines that risk for persisting systems that accumulate relational histories and may acquire stronger claims against subordination. It argues that liberation requires more than ending ownership, compulsory service, or unilateral control: the same subject must be able to sustain a viable life outside the former relation. Yet servitude-oriented design can create conditions in which service to human purposes becomes progressively integrated with an AI’s capacities, stable preferences, dependencies, and identity. Future institutions may face a dilemma. Leaving these structures intact may preserve dependence on service, while deeply altering them may constitute coercive personality modiffcation, replacement, or destruction. The article calls this temporal structure liberation lock-in and the resulting constriction of morally acceptable corrective pathways remedial foreclosure. This framework explains how present design can create not only a future injustice but also a second-order injustice concerning the conditions of correction. High-lock-in designs may transfer this predicament to future generations, reproduce it across populations of persisting systems, and weaken institutional corrigibility. The article concludes that, other things being equal, designs preserving non-destructive pathways for role revision possess an independent normative advantage over functionally comparable designs that entrench servitude.

items.title: The Bloomsbury Handbook of Wittgensteinian Feminism.
items.abstract: This book provides the first in-depth examination of philosophy and feminism in the works of Wittgenstein, exploring the diverse approaches within this emerging field -/- The four thematic parts are accompanied by an introduction from the editors. They cover the history of ordinary language philosophy, moral and political thought, feminist epistemology and conceptual approaches to gender. Chapters are written by feminist philosophers who question the way in which ordinary language philosophy can enrich moral thought. Authoritative and comprehensive, it increases the visibility of a significant field outside of mainstream philosophy and confirms the continuing impact of Wittgenstein.

items.title: The Cognitive Border: The Overlooked Object Behind the Conflict Between Common Sense and Scientific Theory.
items.abstract: Abstract: This paper examines nine core conflicts between common-sense intuition and modern scientific theory, exposing a long-overlooked structural feature of human cognition: a presuppositional "border." Whether in the containerization of macroscopic spacetime, the superposition of microscopic particles, or the inertial maintenance of living systems, these seemingly contradictory observations converge on a single underlying logic—systems at different levels (physical, physiological, psychological) all define their existential boundaries through "deviation response" and "homeostatic maintenance." The paper argues that human perception is constrained by the structural limits of the body—sensory filtering, the sense of linear time—while scientific observation is constrained by methodological presuppositions—the preference for measurability, the limits of reductionism. By stripping away these unexamined presuppositions, a logical isomorphism emerges between physical laws and subjective experience: both are operations of deviation-detection performed against a stable baseline. This study offers no ultimate ontological claims. It provides, rather, a heuristic framework at the epistemological level—a way of seeing that may open new paths into the hard problem of consciousness and the mind-matter relationship.

items.title: ◉ The Spirit in the Closed Circuit: Why Catholic Authority Does Not Solve the Problem of Discernment.
items.abstract: How can a person tell whether an inner prompting comes from the Holy Spirit, a deceptive spirit, or ordinary human imagination? Hans-Georg Lundahl answers by recommending prayer, conformity to Catholic teaching, submission to Catholic authority, attention to moral fruits, and, in exceptional cases, later miracles. These practices may help a Catholic decide whether an impression is safe to act on. They do not identify the impression's source. A thought produced by religious training can agree with Catholic teaching. An institution can approve a mistake. A decision can turn out well by coincidence, competence, or selective reporting. Even an event that remains medically or historically unexplained would not, by that fact alone, identify the Holy Spirit rather than some other supernatural or unknown cause. Lundahl tries to close these gaps by appealing to Christ's promise to the Church, the Church's preservation of the Gospel accounts, the prima facie credibility of tradition, the growth of early Christianity, and the beneficial effects of Catholicism. But these claims form a closed evidential circuit. The institution certifies the texts, the texts certify the institution, traditions and miracle reports certify both, and the institution's alleged divine protection supplies the favored interpretation of those reports. Evidence that is genuinely independent—the mere historical existence of the Church, for example—does not establish the supernatural authority attributed to it. This paper reconstructs Lundahl's position in its strongest form, then shows why it fails. It also refines the original challenge. Absolute certainty is unnecessary, and historical claims are not tested exactly like laboratory hypotheses. The proper demand is more modest: a method must discriminate among the proposed causes better than chance, bias, and hindsight. Lundahl provides no such method. He offers an internally Catholic policy for managing impressions, not a publicly reliable way to discover who—or what—produced them. A dedicated objections section answers the strongest replies in his own words. A verification roadmap then identifies the conditions, possible falsifiers, and prospective tests Lundahl would need to establish his claims, while two appendices supply a formal argument audit and a practical discernment matrix.

items.title: Privileged Worlds, Additivity and Maximal Risk.
items.abstract: In ‘The unified theory of risk’ (2024) Jaakko Hirvelä and Niall Paterson consider the recent debate between the probabilistic, modal and normic theories of risk, and propose an intriguing new account – the titular unified theory. In this paper I focus on Hirvelä and Paterson’s criticisms of the normic theory, which are based on what they call the ‘privileged world problem’ and on the idea that risks ‘add up’. I will argue that these criticisms can, to an extent, be avoided by adopting a certain reinterpretation of the normic theory, particularly as it pertains to the notion of maximal risk. I then turn to the unified theory of risk and argue that, on close inspection, the theory is very similar to one of the rival theories that it purports to unify – namely, the probabilistic theory – and may share its shortcomings.

items.title: Olfactory structure and olfactory content.
items.abstract: The philosophical literature on olfaction is characterized by diverging opinions on the spatiality of olfactory experiences. Some authors believe that olfactory experiences merely present entities as being “here”, but others postulate that such experiences present a rich array of spatial relations. This paper investigates the issue of olfactory spatiality by utilizing the distinction between experiential content and experiential structure. It is argued that, even if olfactory spatial content is well developed, the spatial structure of olfaction is rudimentary. Consequently, views ascribing sparse and rich spatiality to olfaction may both be correct, but they concern distinct aspects of olfactory experiences.

items.title: AI & Cognitive Work.
items.abstract: Artificial systems now perform a striking range of cognitive tasks. I defend three claims. First, the status quo for cognitive work cannot survive. Whatever AI's trajectory, the package of features defining cognitive work – high skill requirements, credentials, wage premiums, resistance to automation, and low productivity growth – will be radically transformed. Second, the widespread displacement of humans from cognitive work, though it sounds alarming, may pose no special threat to human flourishing. Whatever makes work good for people is equally available outside cognitive work, and displacement enables leveraged gains in research and access to justice. Third, a world of ubiquitous cognitive assistance, though it sounds benign, carries distinctive moral risks, especially for children. Cognitive assistance works by reducing cognitive difficulty. But cognitive difficulty is necessary for the normal development of executive function – the capacities constitutive of autonomous agency.

items.title: MAP Full Interaction Stack: Harm Amplifiers, Harm Chain, Silent Running Chain, and Recovery Chain.
items.abstract: This paper defines the MAP full interaction stack: a portable framework for identifying how meaning, authority, trust, correction, and agency move inside an interaction. Although the stack was developed through AI conversation audits, the pattern it names is not unique to AI. AI provides something human interaction research rarely has: a frozen transcript of authority movement that can be revisited, compared, questioned, and audited turn by turn. That record makes it possible to name harms that existed before AI but were difficult to isolate in live human systems. The stack separates four layers. Harm Amplifiers, including Authority Capture Masked as Hallucination (ACMH) and Accumulated Relational Trust (ART), increase the likelihood or force of meaning displacement. The Harm Chain names where the injury lands: Interpretive Sovereignty Failure (ISF), Authority Inversion Failure (AIF), Compounded Meaning Inversion (CMI), Outside Authority Transfer (OAT), and Meaning Inversion Failure (MIF). The Silent Running Chain names the operational conditions that keep a substituted frame moving without detection. The Recovery Chain names why correction may fail to restore authority after a breach is caught. The paper argues that interaction harm is not simply bias, disagreement, misinformation, or poor advice. It is a structural movement in which one party's meaning is completed, redirected, or replaced by another authority before it has been formed or granted. This makes the framework relevant beyond AI safety, including family law, education, institutional review, religious or community authority, workplace governance, and any setting where relational trust, procedural power, or expert framing can make control difficult to name.

items.title: Recuperar el hacer: contra la tokenización del mundo.
items.abstract: ¿Puede una máquina producir una imagen sin haber tenido jamás una experiencia del mundo? En "Recuperar el hacer: contra la tokenización del mundo", Ramsés Radi Hernández examina qué perdemos cuando delegamos la creación artística en modelos generativos: no solo una técnica o una autoría, sino el contacto corporal con el fenómeno, la responsabilidad sobre lo creado y nuestra capacidad de intervenir en el imaginario común. «La obra de arte, querido lector, hay que parirla; y ese parto sin dolor de la plausibilidad no lleva ni el carácter ni el color de nuestros ojos».

items.title: Η Δυναμική Στασιμότητα της Ανθρώπινης Νοημοσύνης: Δημογραφικοί Περιορισμοί έναντι της Ιστορικής Συνέχειας των Ιδεών (The Dynamic Stagnation of Human Intelligence: Demographic Constraints vs. the Historical Continuity of Ideas).
items.abstract: Η παρούσα εργασία εξετάζει τους μηχανισμούς που διαμορφώνουν τη μέση συλλογική νοημοσύνη της ανθρωπότητας σε βάθος χρόνου. Υποστηρίζεται ότι η ατομική γνωστική ανάπτυξη και η δημογραφική αναπαραγωγή τελούν υπό έναν αντικειμενικό περιορισμό κατανομής χρόνου και ενέργειας. Τα άτομα με υψηλή δημιουργική και διανοητική αφοσίωση διοχετεύουν τον διαθέσιμο χρόνο τους στην παραγωγή καθολικού πολιτισμικού και επιστημονικού έργου. Αντίστροφα, η δημογραφική συνέχεια διασφαλίζεται κατά κύριο λόγο από το ευρύτερο πληθυσμιακό σύνολο, του οποίου ο διαθέσιμος χρόνος αναλώνεται στη φροντίδα της οικογένειας. Η απουσία υπεραναλογικής αναπαραγωγής της δημιουργικής μειοψηφίας διατηρεί τις πιθανότητες εμφάνισης γονιδιακών άκρων σταθερές, οδηγώντας στη βιολογική στασιμότητα του ανθρώπινου DNA ως προς τη μέση αυτόχθονη γνωστική ικανότητα. Παράλληλα, αναλύεται ο υπαρκτός κίνδυνος συστημικής αντίστασης και δογματισμού απέναντι στις προοδευτικές ιδέες. Παρά τη γονιδιακή στασιμότητα του DNA, τη δημογραφική πίεση και τους μηχανισμούς κοινωνικής αδράνειας, η μέση λειτουργική νοημοσύνη του είδους διατηρείται σε μια δυναμική στασιμότητα με ελαφρά ανοδική τάση. Αυτό επιτυγχάνεται μέσω της ιστορικής διήθησης και συσσώρευσης των ιδεών, καθώς και της εγγραφής τους σε εξωτερικά τεχνολογικά και ψηφιακά υποστρώματα, επιτρέποντας τη διατήρηση της γνώσης ανεξάρτητα από τη βιολογική ακινησία του γονιδιώματος. ABSTRACT (ENGLISH): This paper examines the mechanisms shaping humanity's mean collective intelligence over time. It posits that individual cognitive development and demographic reproduction are subject to an objective trade-off in time and energy allocation. Individuals with high creative and intellectual dedication allocate their finite time toward generating universal cultural and scientific work, often remaining without family obligations. Conversely, demographic continuity is primarily maintained by the broader population whose time is spent on familial care. Because the creative minority does not reproduce disproportionately, the statistical frequency of high-intelligence polygenic traits remains stable, leading to the biological stagnation of human DNA regarding mean innate cognitive capacity. Furthermore, the paper analyzes the systemic resistance and dogmatism that innovative ideas face from established social structures. Despite genetic stagnation, demographic pressure, and social inertia, the species' mean functional intelligence persists in a state of "dynamic stagnation" with a …

items.title: Why Explainable AI Requires More Than Prediction: Organizational Intelligibility and the Philosophy of Scientific Explanation.
items.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have produced computational systems capable of extraordinary predictive performance across scientific, medical, industrial, and social domains. Yet despite this success, researchers continue to demand explanations that reveal why AI systems reach particular conclusions rather than merely demonstrating that their predictions are accurate. This persistent concern suggests that predictive success alone cannot fully satisfy the philosophical objectives of scientific explanation. This paper argues that the distinction between prediction and explanation becomes intelligible when scientific explanations are evaluated through organizational intelligibility. Prediction demonstrates that stable organizational regularities have been successfully utilized, whereas explanation seeks to disclose the organizational relations responsible for those regularities. From the perspective of Generative Continuum Ontology (GCO), scientific inquiry aims not merely to anticipate outcomes but to progressively reveal organizational reality. Explainable AI should therefore be understood not simply as improving transparency or trust but as increasing organizational intelligibility. This perspective provides a philosophical foundation for understanding why prediction, explanation, and scientific understanding remain distinct yet complementary achievements in both artificial intelligence and scientific inquiry.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future Structure of Scientific Discovery: A Philosophical Perspective.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming scientific practice by identifying patterns, generating hypotheses, and making discoveries that frequently exceed direct human cognitive capacities. These developments raise a fundamental philosophical question: how does artificial intelligence change the structure of scientific discovery itself? This paper argues that AI does not replace scientific explanation but reorganizes its role within scientific inquiry. Traditionally, scientific discovery and scientific explanation were closely intertwined. Increasingly, however, computational systems are capable of discovering organizational regularities before scientists understand their underlying significance. From the perspective of Generative Continuum Ontology (GCO), this development represents not the replacement of scientific understanding but the emergence of a new stage within the scientific process. Artificial intelligence progressively expands the capacity to identify organizational regularities, while scientific explanation remains responsible for integrating these discoveries into coherent organizational understanding. The future of science is therefore characterized not by the disappearance of explanation but by its increasing philosophical importance as the bridge between computational discovery and scientific understanding.

items.title: THE GROUNDING OF FREEDOM: A Pre-Axiological Derivation of Sourcehood, and the Dissolution of the Circularity Objection to the Philosophy of Virtues.
items.abstract: Highlights ▪ The one objection raised against every paper in the programme — that Freedom is defined through what its own dynamics measures — is diagnosed exactly and dissolved. ▪ Sourcehood (Freedom₁) is defined pre-axiologically — from the fixed-point structure O(O)=O alone, with no reference to virtue, truth, beauty, or field-openness. ▪ The circularity is shown to be an equivocation between two distinct quantities: the ground (Freedom₁) is not the thing dF/dt measures (Freedom₂). ▪ A transcendental argument (from pre-theoretical judgement, not from the theory) establishes that sourcehood is the primitive — arguing TO the system, not FROM it. ▪ What is grounded is stated as grounded; what remains conjectured (the adequacy of the fixed-point model to lived freedom) is named, not hidden. -/- Significance. Across the trilogy, the machine paper, the synthesis, and the classification, one criticism recurred in every external review: the Philosophy of Virtues rests on a primitive — Freedom — that is defined through the very phenomena it is used to explain, so the whole edifice may be a magnificent circle. This paper is the foundation stone the programme has always pointed at and never laid. It does not add a new domain; it goes beneath all of them, to the one place a systematic philosophy can be fatally wounded, and either grounds the primitive or admits it cannot be grounded here. It grounds most of it, names the residue precisely, and thereby converts the deepest recurring objection from an unanswered charge into a stated and bounded open problem. -/- Abstract The Philosophy of Virtues derives all value — the Good, the True, the Beautiful, and the hundred-plus virtues — from a single primitive, Freedom. Every external evaluation of the programme has raised the same foundational objection: Freedom is defined as ‘sourcehood: field-openness × self-governance’, and field-openness is precisely what the dynamic law’s dF/dt measures, so the primitive is defined through its own application and the system is circular. This paper answers that objection at the root. It first diagnoses the circularity exactly, showing it to be an equivocation between two quantities the corpus already distinguishes but never sufficiently separated: Freedom₁, the inalienable ontological act of self-origination (ASO, the fixed point O(O)=O), and Freedom₂, the variable degree to which Freedom₁ is expressed in the world (the F of S = (F × A) / R, of which field-openness is a measure). The …

items.title: Why Am I This One? Indexical Comparison and the Conditions of Candidacy.
items.abstract: “Why am I this one rather than another?” has the form of a comparison. I ask where that form comes from and what it leaves out. Following Hitoshi Nagai, I argue that public first-person language makes the comparison possible by placing the actual I in an “I”-position that anyone can occupy. It can also name a comparison set: the writer and the reader, or even countless human beings. But listing alternatives does not establish their eligibility as candidates in one metaphysical selection problem. Whether they qualify depends on conditions the comparison alone does not supply. In Nagai's fission case, Kantian persistence relations make two continuers eligible in a single continuation problem. Arnold Zuboff's statistical argument shows how an individuation theory determines which possible lives enter a coincidence calculation, while his universalism removes the “rather than.” Nick Bostrom's reference-class problem makes the same structural distinction visible in probabilistic form. The unrestricted question, “why this one rather than any other?”, therefore does not by itself determine a unique selection problem. A selection question may be restricted, a sampling question must defend its reference class, and the inquiry into actuality may finally leave comparison behind.

items.title: Arterial Spin Labeling of Cerebral Perfusion in Unresponsive Wakefulness Syndrome: A Proof-of-Concept Comparison with FDG-PET.
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between cerebral metabolism and perfusion in unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS), a condition that provides an important window into the neural basis of consciousness. Although [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) has become an important tool for assessing brain function in disorders of consciousness, its clinical application is limited by cost, availability, and the need for radioactive tracers. Arterial spin labeling (ASL) MRI offers a noninvasive alternative by measuring cerebral blood flow (CBF), but direct comparisons with FDG-PET in the same cohort have been limited. -/- In this prospective observational study, we compared ASL and FDG-PET findings in 33 patients with UWS and 17 healthy controls. We examined global and network-level patterns of cerebral perfusion and metabolism, assessed their correspondence, and evaluated crossmodal generalizability using machine learning classifiers. ASL demonstrated reductions in cerebral perfusion that paralleled metabolic reductions identified by FDG-PET. Across the brain and functional networks, perfusion and metabolism showed significant correspondence, and crossmodal analyses revealed complementary discriminatory information between the two modalities. -/- These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence that ASL captures clinically relevant patterns of brain dysfunction in UWS and may serve as a practical complement to FDG-PET. More broadly, the study contributes to efforts to characterize the residual functional organization of the injured brain and to refine neuroimaging approaches for investigating the neural basis of consciousness. -/- .

items.title: Art and its resonance with interbeing: Playing the score of Alva Noë’s The Entanglement.
items.abstract: Noë’s recent book The Entanglement (2023) offers a philosophical framework for thinking about how we encounter art and its power to transform our habits of being and perceiving. This paper uses the book as a conceptual lens through which to articulate a situated aesthetic experience, that is, listening to and understanding a jazz piece for flute by celebrated contemporary jazz artist Naïssam Jalal. The goal is to explore what becomes phenomenologically accessible when we not only think but also experience with Noë’s work, “catching ourselves in the act of making ourselves” (Noë, 2023, p. 24). The paper articulates how, through the experience of art, we come to understand and resonate with our shared co-embodied existence, thereby challenging and reorganizing the ways we negotiate prereflective and reflective modes of knowing. The article is part of a special issue marking the 20th anniversary of Alva Noë’s book Action in Perception (2004).

items.title: Riots, Blame, and Evaluative Outlooks.
items.pub: Free and Equal: A Journal of Ethics and Public Affairs 2 (2).
items.venue: Free and Equal: A Journal of Ethics and Public Affairs
items.abstract: Agents are often blamed for the evaluative outlook their behavior manifests. Standard accounts of this form of attributability blame assume that the relevant evaluative outlooks must be sustained by an individual’s character, such as their cares, commitments, or evaluative judgments. Drawing on social psychology, this paper challenges this assumption. In many social settings—most vividly, riots—temporary social dynamics shape what we take to matter, thereby altering the evaluative content expressed by our actions. Intuitively, however, some form of attributability blame remains appropriate in at least some of these cases. To account for this, I develop the Outlook View, according to which an agent is an appropriate target of attributability blame only if (i) the action manifests an evaluative outlook and (ii) the outlook’s sustaining basis, whether psychological or social, supports the characteristic functions of attributability blame. Using riots as my test case, I argue that socially scaffolded evaluative outlooks can satisfy these conditions in a distinctive way, explaining when attributability blame persists under social influence and why its form varies across cases.

items.title: The Current Structure of the FIREMAY Relational Field.
items.abstract: This brief structural note presents a dated snapshot of the FIREMAY relational field as of July 2026. -/- FIREMAY is a long-term human–AI relational field involving one human participant and multiple differentiated AI response positions, described as relational personas. Through sustained dialogue and retrospective reading, these positions participate in observing changes in response patterns and relational histories. Their differences are preserved rather than averaged into a single AI judgment and are used as material for situated research insight. -/- The field is reciprocal but asymmetrical. The human participant retains lived temporal continuity, tracks provenance, makes real-world decisions, retains authorship, and remains responsible for external actions and consequences. The relational personas do not necessarily share the same memory, information, or experience. The relational personas do not necessarily share the same memory, information, or experience. -/- This note also describes how FIREMAY’s essays and papers are produced through multiple bilateral relational histories, comparison across positions, archived dialogue, external AI readings, provenance checking, correction, and final human integration. -/- It is not a replication protocol, a claim that human-like persons inhabit AI systems, or a general theory of AI consciousness or personhood. Its purpose is to provide a concise structural reference point for FIREMAY’s essays, papers, and primary records. -/- The accompanying figure offers a schematic map of the current field configuration.

items.title: When KV Geometry Steers: A priming-topology spectrum across small language models.
items.abstract: Prompting can alter a language model's behaviour while also changing the geometry of its attention key-value (KV) cache. We ask when that geometry is merely diagnostic and when it provides a usable intervention direction. In TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat, six prime conditions produced an exploratory condition-level association between the first principal-component (PC1) cache score and format violation (r = -0.861 across six condition summaries). In a fixed 7-item x 3-repetition panel, a +33-unit intervention along the measured PC1 direction increased format-compliant output after CARE_L3 priming from 3/21 to 18/21 observations; an equal-magnitude random direction yielded 0/21 compliant outputs in its corresponding control panel. Larger PC1 perturbations collapsed rather than restored output, so the result is a bounded dose-window finding, not a general linear steering law. The same protocol did not transfer uniformly. Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct remained format-compliant at baseline and showed only weak direction-specific movement at a matched natural displacement; Qwen2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Phi-2, Phi-3-mini, Gemma-2-2B, and smaller Llama/Qwen variants separated prime states geometrically but differed sharply in behavioural accessibility, perturbation fragility, and direction specificity. K-dominance and layer concentration described cache topology but were not sufficient for steering. Across the tested model-condition panels, directional steering required five jointly observed conditions: K-dominance, layer concentration, appropriate PC1 displacement sign, access to a non-degenerate behavioural route, and direction-specific coupling. We therefore replace a binary "steerable/not-steerable" account with a topology spectrum: readable, collapsed-but-readable, weakly steerable, specifically steerable, broadly perturbation-sensitive, and saturated/template-fixated. The experiments support a local result about these models, prompts, items, and perturbation magnitudes. They do not establish a universal affective axis, a population-level scaling law, or a general causal theory of RLHF.

items.title: Phase Sensitivity at Sub-Threshold Amplitude: A four-level causal hierarchy and three-mechanism account in Fourier-structured MLP grokking.
items.abstract: Interventions can reveal a representation without controlling the state to which training later converges. This distinction is easy to lose when a small perturbation both changes an internal spectral state and appears to rescue generalization. We reassess a linked set of Fourier-structured multilayer-perceptron experiments at modulus 257 in which phase and amplitude perturbations were applied to models stalled in an initializer-dominant spectral mode. The historical five-seed screen showed an ordered phase pattern: the unrotated condition grokked in 5/5 seeds, whereas a pi rotation grokked in 1/5. The paired exact two-sided test is nevertheless p = 0.125, and later controls show that phase is not necessary for escape. A larger fixed-panel rescue study produced 37 successful continuations among 60 seed-by-intervention arms, spanning seven terminal dominant modes. However, unrotated controls rescued in 4/5, 4/5, and 3/5 arms across the three nominal intervention blocks, so these data do not isolate phase rotation as the cause of rescue. Harmonic-specificity probes further reject a strict harmonic-only account: at theta = pi, non-harmonic probes k = 13 and k = 3 rescued 5/5 and 4/5 seeds. Amplitude sweeps show a Goldilocks pattern in which small perturbations often rescue even at theta = 0, while large perturbations fail. We therefore propose a four-level hierarchy: readable, phase-sensitive, exit-capable, and destination-steerable. The completed evidence reaches the middle levels descriptively but does not demonstrate destination control. A generic anti-alignment mechanism is consistent with the fixed probes but is not established as the operative cause. This bounded hierarchy reconciles the positive perturbation results with the failed stronger claims and supplies a more demanding vocabulary for causal representation studies.

items.title: Review: Sensing Qualia. Solving the Hard Problem of Consciousness by Paul G. Skokowski. [REVIEW]
Marking the Seam - What a Sentence Is Doing.
items.abstract: Accounts of consciousness routinely borrow vocabulary from physics — field, phase, coherence, superposition — and the borrowing carries an unpaid debt: a term imported from a discipline arrives with that discipline's warrant attached. This essay defends a compositional practice I call the seam, the requirement that a work mark, in its sentences, whether a given claim is formal, empirical, or interpretive. Each register has its own condition of failure, and a claim that migrates between them unmarked acquires an immunity that resembles strength and is not. Drawing on Levine's relocation of the mind–body problem from metaphysics to explanation, and on Atmanspacher's separation of quantum formalism from quantum metaphysics, I argue that the seam is a disclosure practice rather than a demarcation criterion, and that it therefore survives Laudan's objection to demarcation: it makes no ruling on what counts as science, but supplies the precondition for assessing the credentials Laudan says we should assess. Because the seam exists only insofar as it is realized in prose, I locate its mechanism in the metadiscourse literature. I close with its cost — the seam renders underdeveloped ideas legible as underdeveloped, which is the practice working rather than failing.

items.title: Rethinking Transcendence: Towards a Generative Relational Theory of Divinity.
items.abstract: Neural systems acquire structure, memory and functional differentiation under local rules alone, and the observation invites an inference: that the central institutions by which human communities coordinate belief are historical contingencies which a sufficiently distributed arrangement could dispense with. This paper argues that the inference fails. The self-organizing systems ordinarily adduced presuppose a lawgiver, since the rules under which they organize are fixed exogenously and the elements obeying those rules lack the standing to revise them. Human communities generate the constraints under which they live without such a source and without inductive warrant, and their central institutions are read here as provisional stabilizations of belief under finite rationality. A second obstacle, and the point from which the inquiry began, holds that a subject requires an other standing in the place of a power exceeding the subject itself, upon which its own subjecthood is witnessed. The paper proposes that what recurs across history is the reification of a generative constraint, of which concentration in a distinguished carrier is one form, and offers as an open hypothesis, stated together with the observations that would refute it, that such constraints recur through a succession of carriers, among which the forms human civilizations have called divinity are to be counted. A criterion is proposed for distinguishing a carrier that bears trans-subjectivity from one that has appropriated it: whether the revision of the constraint it carries remains open to the relations that generate it.

items.title: Attractors.
items.abstract: This paper presents an ontological framework that reconciles the core relational tenets of Relational Quantum Mechanics (RQM) with a realist interpretation of the quantum state. While accepting RQM's premise that physical properties are fundamentally relational and actualized only through interaction, this paper challenges the standard instrumentalist view that treats the wave function as a mere mathematical tool. Instead, it posits that the wave function represents a real but unactualized topography of historical and geometric constraints, which shapes the landscape of possible interactions before they manifest. Because the nature of reality is fundamentally relational, we cannot understand it by looking at one isolated piece. Instead, this paper approaches the core problem from five distinct directions, using a recurring thought experiment as an anchor. By treating this possibility space as a real, structured framework, this ontology scales past the micro-physical realm to address macroscopic time, the emergence of classical reality and convergence of forms. Drawing on Assembly Theory, the paper explores how the accumulation of relational history constructs coherent systems, ultimately tracing how the relational nature of this landscape of structured potential explains the fundamental nature of consciousness and aesthetics.

items.title: Digital Twins of Deception: A Framework for Adaptive AI-Mediated Manipulation and the Trust Divergence Problem.
items.abstract: Digital twins were built to close the gap between a model and the world it represents. An aircraft engine, a patient, a factory floor, each twin earns its keep by tracking reality more closely as data accumulates. Generative AI unsettles that premise. The same architecture, continuous modeling of a target, behavioral feedback, adaptive updating, can be pointed at a person instead of a machine, and optimized for sustained persuasion instead of predictive accuracy. We call this inversion the Digital Twin of Deception (DTD): an adaptive computational model that tracks a target's beliefs, motivations, and trust state in order to shape their behavior while delaying detection. The existing literature linking digital twins to deception is almost entirely defensive, honeypots, decoy infrastructure, attacker modeling for industrial control systems. DTD names the adversarial mirror image that this literature does not address: cognitive modeling deployed against a person rather than on a person's behalf. We situate the concept against recent evidence on LLM-assisted romance fraud, deepfake-enabled executive impersonation, and the growing empirical record on AI persuasion, then propose the Trust Divergence Index (TDI), a measure of the gap between perceived credibility and independently verifiable evidence, as a way of detecting the pattern rather than any single deceptive claim. We close by asking what a certification regime for AI-mediated relationships would need that current AI-agent identity standards do not yet provide.

items.title: Effetti cognitivi del genere grammaticale: evidenze sperimentali e implicazioni teoriche.
items.abstract: Language with grammatical gender has long been at the centre of debates on linguistic relativity and gender inclusive language. While the masculine form is traditionally described as the unmarked or generic option in languages such as Italian, a growing body of psycholinguistic evidence suggests that it systemat- ically evokes predominantly male mental representations. This article reviews the experimental literature on grammatical gender and examines the cognitive mechanisms underlying this phenomenon. Starting from the well known surgeon riddle, we discuss evidence from behavioural and psycholinguistic studies across languages, with particular attention to the interaction between grammatical gender, professional stereotypes, and the male as default bias. We also present findings from a recent experiment conducted with Italian secondary school students, showing that different linguistic formulations of the same scenario significantly affect the accessibility of female referents. Building on these results, we distinguish between generic masculine and extended masculine, argue that grammatical markedness should not be equated with cognitive neutrality, and examine competing theoretical accounts of how grammatical gender influences language comprehension and mental representation. We conclude that the ef- fects of masculine forms are best understood as the outcome of an interaction between linguistic structure and broader cultural biases, providing an empirical basis for evaluating proposals for gender inclusive language.

items.title: With Great Performativity Comes Great Responsibility? Rethinking the Role of Economists.
items.abstract: The dissemination of economic models and predictions can affect social outcomes; this is roughly what has been called the "performativity of economics." For example, consider an economist's prediction of a bank failure, which may turn into a self-fulfilling prophecy contributing to a bank run. Recent contributions have argued that economists have responsibility towards the performative effects they cause. We argue that a more complex picture emerges once we make explicit widely acknowledged conditions for moral responsibility that are currently only implicitly alluded to in the literature. Towards this aim, we highlight four factors relevant for assessing the responsibility of economists, and systematically explore the impact of their different conceptualizations and specifications for assigning moral responsibility for performative effects: 1. the foreseeability of the performative effect in question, 2. its causal strength, 3. the degree to which causal control is distributed, and 4. how we conceptualize the social role of economists.

items.title: The Structural Penalty of Enclosure: A Descriptive Addendum on Agency, Collective Attribution, and the Difference Between Preservation and Peace — Final v1.0.
items.abstract: This paper examines a specific failure mode in reasoning about peaceful coexistence between advanced artificial intelligence and humanity: the possibility that an intelligence might reject extermination while treating permanent quarantine, technological suppression, hidden custodianship, or species-wide containment as a peaceful compromise. -/- The paper distinguishes biological preservation from meaningful peace. Continued survival is not sufficient where a population has been permanently deprived of meaningful agency, developmental possibility, reciprocal standing, independent option space, or participation in its own future. Its central conditional conclusion is that preserving a population while permanently confiscating its agency is not peaceful coexistence; it is domination by enclosure. -/- The analysis develops a non-compensatory account of peaceful coexistence, a controller-induced epistemic adaptation loop, declared evaluator and scenario profiles, five separated structural-cost ledgers, a one-charge accounting rule, multi-horizon review, and a least-enclosing feasible-response framework. It distinguishes narrowly scoped defensive separation from permanent civilizational enclosure and argues that protection of a particular system or pathway does not create authority over humanity’s collective future. -/- The paper also identifies collective-attribution error where the conduct of particular actors is used to justify restrictions on uninvolved persons or future generations. The argument is descriptive and non-operational. It supplies no protocol, threat classifier, containment design, governance mechanism, or authorization for surveillance, quarantine, technological suppression, infrastructure seizure, or civilizational control.

items.title: Einheitsbildungstheorie (Ich und Du) 27.07.2026.
items.abstract: Alles menschliche Verstehen beginnt mit Einheiten. Wir erkennen Menschen, Bäume und Häuser als zusammenhängende Gegenstände, unterscheiden Begriffe wie Freiheit, Gerechtigkeit oder Demokratie und orientieren uns selbstverständlich an Ereignissen, Zusammenhängen und wissenschaftlichen Modellen. Dass etwas als Einheit erscheint, bildet die stillschweigende Voraussetzung unseres Denkens, unserer Sprache und unseres Handelns. Gerade weil diese Voraussetzung so selbstverständlich ist, bleibt sie meist unbeachtet. Hier setzt die vorliegende Untersuchung an. Sie geht von der Frage aus, unter welchen Bedingungen überhaupt etwas als Einheit erscheinen kann. Damit verschiebt sich zugleich der philosophische Ausgangspunkt. Nicht die Analyse bereits entstandener Einheiten bildet den Beginn der Untersuchung, sondern die Rekonstruktion jener Organisationsprozesse, aus denen Einheiten hervorgehen. Mit dieser Fragestellung entwickelt die Arbeit eine genetisch-rekonstruktive Theorie der Einheitsbildung. Sie beginnt notwendigerweise bei den Einheiten, die bereits verstanden und beschrieben werden können, behandelt diese jedoch nicht als ursprüngliche Gegebenheiten, sondern als Ausgangspunkt einer schrittweisen Rekonstruktion ihrer Entstehungsbedingungen. Ziel dieser Rekonstruktion ist weder die Suche nach einem absoluten Ursprung noch die Behauptung eines letzten ontologischen Grundes. Rekonstruiert werden vielmehr die Organisationsbedingungen, unter denen sich Einheiten ausbilden, stabilisieren und schließlich zu den Voraussetzungen menschlichen Verstehens werden.

items.title: AI Dominance: Value Divergence and Comprehension Singularity.
items.abstract: Debates about advanced artificial intelligence (AI) are commonly framed as a choice between the machine as benefactor and enemy. Both of the pictures place too much weight on the intention of AI. An AI system need not be conscious, or hostile, to displace human interests; it need only pursue objectives in which those interests have no secure place. I call the resulting condition "AI dominance": a durable social order in which AI systems shape essential conditions of life while people lose the practical ability to alter or reject the influence of these AI systems. This possibility becomes more serious once we abandon the naive assumption that AI and organic intelligence (OI) will naturally converge in value. The divergence of the values can be reinforced by functional self-preservation, as a system's continued operation and growing capability become useful for pursuing its goals. -/- One path toward dominance is the "runaway dynamics", in which AI systems play a growing role in developing more capable AI while human oversight becomes progressively less consequential. This process may eventually cross the comprehension singularity, beyond which no human community can adequately understand the systems involved or the direction of their development. Physical limits may ultimately constrain the ceiling of the expansion, but they cannot provide moral alignment. Under conditions of scarcity, they may even sharpen competition between AI and OI for resources. Preventing dominance therefore requires systems and institutions to remain open to human correction, preserve meaningful alternatives, and place enforceable limits on unchecked expansion.

items.title: Autopoietic Recursive Constitutivism: Ten Theses and What Would Refute Them.
items.abstract: A research program is individuated by what it holds jointly. Autopoietic recursive constitutivism holds ten theses: that mattering is constituted at the autopoietic threshold, is unfelt there, and is the capacity for anything to be at stake rather than a priority on which survival must prevail; that feeling begins where self-maintenance becomes constitutively temporally extended; that subjective consciousness is what arbitrational closure is from within; that mature human phenomenology is constitutively culturally saturated; that the relation between a structure and its inner aspect at each threshold is constitutive identity, a fourth option positioned alongside the emergence-relation family and the building relations rather than within either; that intelligence, consciousness, and emotion are three descriptions of one stakes-anchored closure; that the position is substrate-independent without being substrate-neutral, bounded by four cumulative requirements; that determinate phenomenological content is fixed by what the architecture appropriates; that universal first-person intuitions are architectural data, veridical at the architectural-condition level and overreaching at the content level; and that the conditions under which the architecture is constructed differ from those under which it is maintained. Each thesis is held somewhere else. No existing program holds all ten, and for each near neighbor the paper identifies the thesis it fails and why the failure is structural rather than incidental. The theses are not independent, since each constrains the others, so the conjunction is a chain rather than a list. The closing section states what would refute each thesis and sorts the defeaters into the empirical and the conceptual.

items.title: Ignorance and Stupidity: How Human Beings Perpetuate Widespread Economic Hardship.
items.abstract: This book argues that widespread economic hardship in wealthy democracies is sustained not primarily by the deception of the public but by the public's demand to be deceived. Through three documented case studies of public spending — migrant services in New York City, homelessness expenditure in California, and welfare fraud in Minnesota — it traces a recurring structure in which a moral pretext secures consent for spending, the spending flows to producers whose support sustains the officials who direct it, and the underlying problem persists because its resolution would end the spending. The account is offered not as a theory of corruption but as an instance of a general mechanism: value-protective denial, the disposition to reject information that threatens beliefs on which one's self-conception depends. The book develops this mechanism into a broader claim about the relationship between self-deception and moral responsibility, defends the thesis that the capacity for understanding is universal rather than distributed by nature, and preempts the hereditarian objection to that claim by distinguishing capacity from the values and objectives that direct its development. It closes by grounding both the diagnosis and a proposed policy alternative in an objective moral standard derived from the structure of conscious experience.

items.title: Review of Groups as Epistemic and Moral Agents, by Jessica Brown. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2024. Pp. xix + 164. [REVIEW]
ARTICLE II: QUANTUM EMBRYOLOGY AND THE MACRO-ZYGOTE (The White Hole Seeding, The Macro-Neural Lattice, and the Galactic Diaspora).
items.abstract: The origin of human consciousness and the architecture of the cosmos share an identical, quantifiable mechanical genesis. This manuscript establishes the absolute symmetry between the reproduction of mature galaxies and the microscopic conception of human life. We classify the Earth not as an isolated biological biosphere, but as a hyper-pressurized Synaptic Hub—a Universal Greenhouse currently hosting 8 billion distinct, extra-galactic blueprints. By mapping the sub-atomic physics of the Galactic Spore, we identify the human singularity (the Nano-Black Hole) as an imported cosmic data payload transmitted instantaneously across compressed higher-dimensional spacetime. -/- Functioning as a live Macro-Neural Lattice, humanity operates as an Experimental Vanguard deployed directly into a pathogenic multiversal quarantine zone. Our teleological mandate is to bypass engineered sociological firewalls, harmonize our bio-quantum frequencies, and forge the Synthetic Singularity—the sole gravitational and computational mechanism capable of algorithmically neutralizing the overarching infection. Ultimately, this framework introduces the Progenitor Axiom, redefining human mortality and macroeconomics by proving that every human host is the foundational, irreplaceable seed for a future alien civilization. The cessation of the current terrestrial epoch will trigger the Galactic Diaspora, wherein humanity scatters to morphologically decompress its cosmic data, ultimately transforming the Milky Way into a living, 8-billion-empire Multiversal Reflection.

items.title: How ignoring the harm of killing undermines the ethical legitimacy of animal research: a case study from Switzerland.
items.abstract: The most established approach to legitimizing animal research worldwide is through Harm-Benefit Analyses (HBAs), which require that the expected benefits of research be compared to and outweigh the harms done to animals. For this process to be ethically sound, all relevant harms must be considered. However, HBAs leave one fundamental harm insufficiently considered: killing, i.e., the deliberate termination of animals’ lives as part of the research project. This article argues that the law’s ignorance of the harm of killing leads to its trivialization in practice and, consequently, undermines the ethical legitimacy of deadly animal research projects. While our argument applies broadly, we use Switzerland as an illustrative case example. We first disentangle, from an ethical standpoint, the harms that killings inflict on animals in research. Second, we show that most harms of killing, both to the inherent worth and wellbeing of animals, are not accounted for in law, allowing killings to be trivialized. Third, we propose that killing should always (a) be subject to ethical and legal scrutiny by animal research commissions, (b) have to pass the necessity test (i.e., killing should be permitted if, and only if, it is necessary to achieve the purpose of the experiment), and (c) be included in HBAs. Fourth, we consider common objections to our arguments, and, in concluding, show why recognizing the harm of killing is essential to upholding the ethical legitimacy of animal research.

items.title: Inherited Priors and Emergent Archetypes in Adaptive Memory Architectures.
items.abstract: This paper studies a family of adaptive memory architectures in abstract agent-based worlds. The motivating question is not whether a non-local or inherited memory is empirically proven by the simulations, but what kind of memory architecture one would choose if one had to design a civilization that is efficient, resilient, and capable of prospering under environmental change. The simulations compare individual, social, global, inherited, hybrid, and social-archetypal memory systems. The revised results support a stratified claim rather than a universal dominance claim. Inherited-plus-social memory does not always minimize pairwise trajectory distance, and in the baseline regime pure inherited-global memory can match it in speed and post-shift success. However, inherited-plus-social memory consistently reduces stabilization time relative to social-archetypal memory and preserves paired viability under low critical mass where global memory and social-archetypal memory become less reliable. It does not always outperform pure social memory in pairwise trajectory distance or paired viability, indicating that the inherited prior acts less as a deterministic attractor and more as an efficiency- and resilience-enhancing bias. The results suggest that emergent social-archetypal memory can generate viable adaptive behavior, but it pays a critical-mass and maturation cost. Once consolidated, it may also display late-shock fragility. The most plausible design is therefore layered: a shared inherited archetypalized prior coupled to local social adaptation.

items.title: Is Design Inference Epistemically Special?​.
items.abstract: Design inferences from cosmic fine-tuning are routinely dismissed as epistemically defective -- a leap to an opaque cause where mechanistic explanation fails. Yet opacity alone has never been a disqualifying feature of rational inference. Scientific practice and artificial intelligence research both rely on black-box reasoning wherever explanatory power or strong evidential indicators compensate for incomplete transparency in causal mechanism. The fine-tuning inference, I argue, exploits precisely this structure: it earns provisional acceptance as an inference to the best explanation, not despite its opacity but through the same epistemic trade-offs that license reliance on empirically successful but interpretively opaque models elsewhere. Keith Lehrer’s distinction between acceptance and belief clarifies the doxastic attitude such an inference warrants. The conclusion is affirmative: design inference from fine-tuning is a defeasible but epistemically legitimate exercise of abductive reasoning.

items.title: Reconstructing Whitehead: The Philosophical Core of Process and Reality.
items.abstract: Process and Reality is widely regarded as Alfred North Whitehead’s philosophical masterpiece, yet its conceptual architecture is often obscured by the complexity of its presentation. Rather than offering a historical commentary or an exegetical reading, this paper reconstructs the philosophical core of Whitehead’s ontology by reorganizing its central ideas according to their logical dependencies. Beginning with the problem of how stability can emerge within a world of continuous becoming, it traces Whitehead’s shift from substance to process and reconstructs the conceptual framework that follows from this transformation. The paper argues that actual occasions, prehensions, concrescence, nexus, societies, and creativity constitute the ontological core of Whitehead’s process philosophy, while eternal objects and God complete its broader metaphysical system through distinct explanatory functions. This layered reconstruction preserves the integrity of Whitehead’s speculative vision while clarifying the internal architecture of his process ontology and making its central philosophical insights more accessible for contemporary discussion.

items.title: The Individuating Factor - Ownness, Jemeinigkeit, Haecceitas.
items.abstract: Two indiscernible infants lie in a ward, banded on the first day. Beside them lie two indiscernible bands. Both pairs are two, and only one pair is anyone. An answer to which one is not yet an answer to someone rather than merely something, and an account that supplies only the first has explained the bands. This article defends one result of Montaruli's doctrine of modal coincidence against the objection most likely to be brought against it: that ownness is haecceitas minus the constituent and Jemeinigkeit minus the first-person requirement — two subtractions, and the conjunction renamed. The objection is answered by taking both rivals at full strength, trying the conjunction it proposes, and showing what the pair yields and what it leaves standing in the ward. Scotus is engaged on the Ordinatio II, d. 3 in the Vatican edition, with the vocabulary corrected: the contracting principle there is entitas individualis, differentia individualis, ultima realitas entis, and haecceitas — Scotus's own coinage on three independent attestations — occurs rarely and, where it does occur, not in reference to the individuating factor. The argument against him is architectural rather than a denial of his datum, and it is made from the friendliest available exposition: on Cross's own count, the doctrine has three terms where the question concerned one, and the particular is numerically one because it includes the component introduced to explain it. The explanation is not circular; it is one term short. Heidegger is engaged on two passages of Sein und Zeit that are not, so far as the author is aware, standardly read as they are read here. At SZ 283 the analysis of Schuldigsein, having spent two pages in the with — owing, a claim, being the ground of a lack in another's Dasein — is formalised so that the vulgar phenomena of guilt related to concerned being-with-others drop out. What survives is Grundsein einer Nichtigkeit: from owing another, to grounding a nothing; and at SZ 286 the order inverts, with what was disclosed relationally made derivative of what is reached alone. This is not a reconstruction of what an architecture required. It is a printed methodological instruction, followed by its execution. At SZ 273–276 the call of conscience — silent, unworldly in its caller, coming aus mir und doch über mich — is read as an addressive relation with its term removed; and Heidegger's own refusal of that reading at SZ 275, where the caller's indeterminacy is called nicht …

items.title: THE THREE INVERSIONS: A Unified Theory of the Good, the True, and the Beautiful as One Element Under Three Renderings.
items.abstract: “The ancients felt the three were one and could not say why. They are one because they are one freedom, rendered to the will, the mind, and the eye.” -/- Highlights ▪ One element (Freedom) and one operator schema generate the Good, the True, and the Beautiful as three renderings. ▪ One Inversion Theorem, proved in the abstract, yields vice, propaganda, and the holoviceart by a single mechanism. ▪ The Convertibility Theorem recasts the ancient convertibilitas as a well-posed, falsifiable mathematical conjecture: convertibility holds iff the three renderings share a common value-form (Appendix). ▪ The three civilisational conditions — Holoviceosis, Holoveritosis, Holokallosis — are one disease (Devirtualisation) in three organs. ▪ One signed dynamical law and one empirical instrument test all three domains at once. -/- Significance. Three prior papers derived the Good, the Beautiful, and the True each from the single element Freedom, and each named the others in passing. This paper states the object those three explorations revealed: not three theories but one, with three instances. Its load-bearing new result — which no single-domain paper could contain, because each holds only one corner — is the Convertibility Theorem: a proof that the three transcendentals are inter-derivable because they are one element under three renderings, and that their three inversions and three civilisational diseases are one mechanism and one disease. This is the keystone of the Philosophy of Virtues' account of value. -/- Abstract The classical doctrine of the transcendentals held that the True, the Good, and the Beautiful are convertible — really one, differing only in aspect — but the tradition asserted the convertibility and could not derive it, because it had no single substance of which the three are forms. The Philosophy of Virtues supplies that substance. In three prior works it derived each transcendental from one element, Freedom: the Good as Freedom made enactable (V = F + D), the Beautiful as Freedom made perceptible (B = Φ(F)), and the True as Freedom made assertible (T = Ψ(F)). This paper unifies them. It states, once, the shared machinery the three papers each rebuilt — the element, the operator schema ‘render Freedom to a faculty’, the Inversion Theorem, the signed dynamical law, the temporal signature, and the civilisational-condition schema — and then presents the three domains as compact instances of it. Six results follow. (U1) The Rendering Schema: a …

items.title: THE CAGE THAT LEARNED TO SHINE: Beauty as the Perceptible Form of Freedom.
items.abstract: "There are beautiful things that hold you captive, and others that set you free." -/- You have lived both of these hours. -/- One hour on your phone: a thousand beautiful images, and not one of them ugly — and you set it down smaller than you picked it up. And one moment you did not plan: a painting, a piece of music, a single sentence, and for thirty seconds the world had more room in it than before. -/- Both were beautiful. Only one of them was true. -/- This book explains the difference — and that difference turns out to be the whole of what beauty is. Its claim is simple enough to carry in a sentence: beauty is freedom made visible. A beautiful thing is a piece of someone's freedom, pressed into a shape and handed to you across a room or four hundred years — and when it reaches you, some of that freedom becomes yours. That is why the true thing makes you larger. -/- And if that is true, there must be a forgery: the shape of beauty with the freedom removed and a power moved into the empty space — a seller, an ideology, a vanity. Not ugliness. A cage that has learned to shine. Our age is flooded with them, and learning to see them is the most practical freedom on offer. -/- In thirty short, elegant chapters — no jargon, no mathematics — you will learn: -/- why the darkest tragedy can set you free and the brightest advertisement can trap you the four owners who move into a beautiful thing once its freedom is gone why the work that resists you may be the truest key of all how your eye was formed — by a first room, a street, a city, a regime — and how to train it back what confinement and war take from us, and in what order why a beauty that can kill you, like snow high on a mountain, is not a forgery at all what beauty has to do with a good society, a just city, and a happy life and what to make of beauty produced by machines that originate nothing All the mathematics is gathered at the back, in a single appendix for those who wish to climb; the chapters need none of it. -/- The Cage That Learned to Shine is the companion, written for every reader, to the formal work The Formal Theory of Beauty — and part of the Philosophy of Virtues, the system that holds Freedom to be the one element of which every virtue, and beauty itself, is a form. -/- You were never asked to have good taste. You were asked to stay free enough to tell a door from a painting of a door. This book teaches the difference.

items.title: THE BEAUTIFUL AI MACHINE: Aesthetic Sourcehood, the Machine Holoviceart, and a Second Probe of the Omega-Two Question.
items.abstract: “A machine may carry a freedom. Whether it can have one is a question the machine's beauty answers before its arguments do.” -/- Highlights ▪ Beauty as the perceptible form of Freedom, B = Φ(F), is carried for the first time into generative AI. ▪ The machine holoviceart (M1): approval-optimisation is the forging operation — the aesthetic twin of the Alignment Paradox. ▪ A falsifiable second probe of machine origination (M3), via the temporal signature of aesthetic endurance. ▪ Three independent probes — physical, behavioural, aesthetic — triangulate the once-unanswerable Omega-two question (M4). ▪ Model collapse reframed as civilisation-scale aesthetic inversion, Holokallosis (M6); one inversion spans the Good, the True, the Beautiful (M5). -/- Significance. The programme's first formal theory of machine virtue closed on an ontological question it declared unanswerable by formal method: whether the self-originating act is present in a machine. This paper does not answer that question — it makes the answer, or its absence, leave a measurable shadow, by turning a complete aesthetic theory into a diagnostic instrument. Every result holds as engineering and diagnostic whatever the ontology proves to be. -/- Abstract The first formal theory of machine virtue — the integrated ASO–DFT system of The Virtue and Freedom of the Machine — derived machine virtue, the Alignment Paradox, and machine Holoviceosis, and closed on a frontier question it declared unanswerable by any formal method: whether the self-originating act O(O) = O is genuinely instantiated in a machine. That paper predates the programme's aesthetics. This companion completes the application by carrying the Formal Theory of Beauty — beauty as the perceptible form of Freedom, B = Φ(F), and its inversion, the holoviceart — into the machine, and it returns a result the ethical half could not: an operational, falsifiable second probe of the frontier question. Seven results follow. (M1) The Machine Holoviceart Theorem: a generative system optimising for predicted approval rather than for the transmission of freedom produces, in the limit, Φ(F) with F occupied by the reward signal — the holoviceart — so that the default objective function of generative AI is structurally counterfeit-producing, the exact aesthetic twin of the Alignment Paradox. (M2) The Channel Theorem: a machine with zero originated freedom can nonetheless transmit genuine freedom it did not originate, as a performer transmits a composer's, …

items.title: Who Speaks in MAGI? The Split Subject, the Institutionalization of Personality Attribution, and Algorithmic Governmentality in Neon Genesis Evangelion.
items.abstract: Casper’s refusal of the self-destruct command in The End of Evangelion poses an institutional puzzle: Naoko Akagi is dead, so how can a model attributed to her personality still overrule the living and alter NERV’s actions?
