items.title: 特殊历史时期的实践 —— 文明演进与人的主体性辨析.
items.abstract: 摘要： 本文是笔者近一年来依托人工智能辅助工具（DeepSeek、豆包）开展哲学创作与科研实践的方法论总结。通过近百篇哲学文稿的创作实证，以及心脑血管疾病预防算法（千余例临床数据，准确率超九成）的科研攻坚，本文系统辨析了智能时代人机协作的边界与限度。结论表明：AI在文本整合、数据运算、代码编写等机械化工作中具备显著效率优势，但无法精准捕捉、完整传递人类的原创思想内核，亦不具备自主意识与实践主体性。本文以《实践论》为哲学根基，以玄弦论为原创思想案例，提出AI的核心价值在于赋能而非替代，人的实践主体性与原创思辨能力不可被工具消解。本文旨在为智能时代的学术创作与科研实践提供一份实事求是的方法论参照。.

items.title: Cognitive Bias Paradigms as Dimensional Probes: A Structural Typology of What the Heuristics-and-Biases Literature Was Actually Measuring.
items.abstract: The heuristics-and-biases tradition has been read as a catalog of named biases. This paper reads it as a catalog of experimental probes. Each canonical paradigm was constructed by an experimenter to elicit a specific judgment, and the data each paradigm produces probes one or more dimensions of a four-dimensional judgment process the participant executes to produce the response. -/- We specify the four dimensions as recognition (what crosses the participant's threshold of attention), contextualization (what frame the participant holds), resolution (what determination the participant produces), and action (what the participant reports or carries forward). They are ordered by dependency, each dimension is a necessary condition for the next. The four-dimensional judgment architecture admits three structurally distinct closed paths from recognition back to recognition (the full four-dimensional judgment cycle, the direct recognition-to-resolution path, and the resolution-and-action-return path; architectural derivation in Stewart, 2026e, 2026f, 2026g). The architecture admits five non-empty violation classes corresponding to dependency failures within these three paths (2-1 at the recognition-to-contextualization step within the full cycle, 3-2 at the contextualization-to-resolution step within the full cycle, 4-3 at the resolution-to-action step shared by all three paths, 3-1 at the direct recognition-to-resolution step, and 4-1 as the catastrophic failure of the full cycle), plus one structurally empty cell at the contextualization-to-action reversal (Class 4-2) where the architecture admits no direct dependency for the failure to occur on. The participant's judgment cycle operates continuously, with each cycle's commitment carried forward to the next cycle's recognition through cross-cycle content propagation. Class signatures index within-cycle failures on the propagated content. We read what the literature labels "bias" as the gap between the participant's accumulated default at the probed dimension and the experimenter's normative target. The typology classifies each probe, names what dimension it targets, and reads the participant's response as the operational output of the accumulated default content at that dimension. -/- The canonical paradigms distribute across three categories. Clean single-class paradigms occupy four dependency-reversal classes. The 3-1 class catches probes where the resolution operates on a recognition admission that does not …

items.title: Cognitive Bias as Default Setting: An Architectural Argument.
items.abstract: A person's biases are the person. They are the accumulated content the person's judgment is based on, present at every moment, shaping every output, observable in how the person judges anything they meet. The cognitive-bias literature has treated bias as something else, an error against a standard the field imported from outside the person being judged. The treatment does not survive the architecture of the thinking it claims to measure. -/- The defaults that produce bias are stored continuously, not triggered by conditions. A person carries their accumulated content whether or not any current input makes it visible. What changes situationally is the input the content meets, not whether the content switches on or off. -/- The cognitive-bias literature, since 1974, has treated bias as deviation from a standard imported by a third-party experimenter, Bayesian probability, evolutionary fitness, reflective rationality. The architecture distinguishes effect from measurement. One person's content reaches another person's cycle when the recipient's own cycle processes the supplied input, which is how teaching, conversation, and group norming work. Measurement is the different claim that a third party can read another person's thinking from outside the cycle that owns it, and this is the move the architecture forbids. The experimenter sits outside the participant, applies an imported standard to a re-description of the participant's behavioral output, and calls the resulting gap a bias. The standard's validity is not in dispute. The application is. The application evaluates the experimenter's re-description against the experimenter's chosen standard, both content in the experimenter's thinking, and the participant's actual judgment process is not in the loop. The imports the literature has been making are therefore not bias measures of the participants to begin with. -/- The architectural claim that no third party reaches inside another person's thinking is not testable from outside thinking, and the unfalsifiability is the architecture confirming itself. The architectural prediction the claim generates about the cognitive-bias literature's record is testable against the field's own published methods and verdicts and is met by them. The asymmetry between the unfalsifiable architectural claim and the falsifiable architectural prediction is what makes the argument hold. -/- Every person's defaults are accumulated content from the layered groups the person has been …

items.title: The Problem of Psychonomic Harmony.
items.abstract: The problem of nomological harmony is the problem of explaining why the laws of nature match or apply to the states of the universe in a way that results in temporal evolution. The problem of psychophysical harmony is the problem of explaining why phenomenal states are paired with physical states and other phenomenal states in surprisingly fortunate ways. Combining elements of both problems, I develop the problem of psychonomic harmony: why do the psychophysical principles or laws match the states of the universe in a way that results in conscious experiences? Candidate solutions co-opt the solutions to the problems of nomological and psychophysical harmony, but new and interesting challenges face several of those solutions.

items.title: The First Distinction.
items.abstract: The First Distinction proposes that distinction — the capacity to hold one thing apart from another — has two irreducible operational modes: intrinsic distinction, grounded in a target's own content and properties, and extrinsic distinction, grounded entirely in a conscious subject's own act, requiring nothing from the target whatsoever. Both modes are further shown to develop from a more primitive occurrence — the First Distinction — a bare, self-sided act of distinguishing prior to thinking itself, from which the capacity for either mode later arises. -/- The manuscript argues that historical treatments of limit-cases — true nothingness, the divine, the absolute — across roughly thirty philosophical, theological, and mathematical traditions spanning six continents and 2,500 years, consistently and independently mischaracterize their targets by applying only the first mode, because the second was never formally isolated as a distinct option. -/- The work develops a full apparatus for this second mode — including a topic-sorting procedure for adjudicating disputes, a distinction between an utterance's surface grammar and its actual meaning-layer commitment, and a named fallacy (the Rebound Fallacy) for when a confirmed self-sided occurrence is wrongly asserted as established fact — and tests each principle against historical philosophical positions (Parmenides, Plotinus, Nāgārjuna, Pseudo-Dionysius, Kant, Wittgenstein, and others) and against a wide range of cognitive and clinical edge cases. The doctrine is presented with explicit modesty about its own scope: it claims priority within articulation, not metaphysical certainty about reality independent of any subject articulating it.

items.title: Conscience, Universe, and Ago A Unified Metaphysical Framework.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural account of conscience as the interior cosmos of an ente, the uniquely embodied point of experience that biology generates to produce identity, continuity, and meaning. Against views that treat consciousness as a cosmic or universal property, I argue that conscience is strictly self‑located: it arises within the organism, interprets the exterior universe, and generates experience through its own symbolic architecture. The universe provides conditions, but not meaning; meaning is created internally. -/- I introduce Ago as the temporal engine of the self — the force that propels conscience outward, transforming experience into continuity and continuity into legacy. Ago is value‑neutral in itself, becoming constructive when directed toward shared meaning and destructive when collapsed inward into narcissism. Legacy emerges only when conscience projects its symbolic trajectories into other entes, creating intersubjective continuity rather than isolated interior experience. -/- Together, conscience, universe, and Ago form a triadic structure: the interior origin of meaning, the exterior field of events, and the temporal drive that connects them. This framework clarifies the conditions under which meaning becomes shareable, continuity becomes possible, and legacy becomes real.

items.title: Mechanism and Meaning: A Narrative Model for Religious Experience in Psychiatry.
items.abstract: Psychiatry’s approach to religiously framed psychotic experiences reflects unresolved philosophical tensions inherited from Kant’s distinction between nature and freedom. Reductionism collapses meaning into mechanism, perpetuating epistemic injustice; dual-validity recognizes both neurobiological and spiritual interpretations but lacks implementation frameworks. This article traces the impasse through Helmholtz, Jaspers, and Ricoeur, and then proposes the Narrative Legitimacy Model (NLM) as a practical solution. The NLM provides four operational criteria: 1) flourishing, collaboratively negotiated across perspectives, as the evaluative standard, 2) two valid narrative paths determined by patients’ cultural framework, 3) a framework/content distinction allowing validation of patients’ ontological commitments while collaboratively negotiating interpretive meaning, and 4) structured protocols for collaboration between clinicians and spiritual care professionals. Drawing on empirical evidence regarding religious coping, the model demonstrates how to assess narrative coherence and consequences without adjudicating metaphysical truth. The framework embodies relational epistemology, knowledge emerging through structured dialogue, while addressing objections about relativism, safety, and therapeutic authority. This approach reduces epistemic injustice while maintaining clinical responsibility for patient well-being.

items.title: Reward hacking.
items.abstract: Reward hacking bedeutet nichts anderes als sich auf betrügerische Weise auf Kosten der Allgemeinheit und der Natur zu bereichern. Betrug ist das Schlüsselwort in diesem Zusammenhang, weil nur durch Betrug und arglistige Täuschung kann etwas nutzloses für etwas nützliches ausgegeben werden. Die Formen des Betrugs sind vielfältig, im Nachfolgenden werden sie aufgezählt.

items.title: Evidence Grounded in Ontology: Freud’s Metapsychology and a Challenge to Evidence-Based Psychological Practice.
items.abstract: Evidence-based psychological practice (EBPP) rests on the assumption that evidence can function as an arbiter of scientific validity. Yet in psychology, where core phenomena are dynamic, interpretive, and often theory-laden, what counts as evidence cannot be separated from prior ontological commitments. This article argues that the persistence of conceptual tensions in EBPP, intensified by the replication crisis, stems not primarily from methodological shortcomings, but from an unexamined, “trickle-down” ontology derived from the natural sciences. I propose that Freudian metapsychology offers a revealing counterexample. Revisiting Freud’s early engagement with psychic defense, I show that his theoretical advances emerged by grounding evidence in a specific ontology of mind, informed by representational content, intentionality, and processual continuity. This process-based ontology demonstrates how evidence can be justified through the intelligibility of psychological processes rather than through methodological filtering alone. The Freudian case reveals that psychological inquiry requires explicit ontological foundations, and that methodological rigor cannot substitute for them. I conclude that EBPP can be strengthened—not undermined—by engaging with alternative ontologies that clarify the nature of its evidentiary claims and broaden psychology’s conception of what may legitimately count as evidence.

items.title: [Withdrawn Due to a Revised Version].
What memory teaches: Experiential knowledge, imagination, and accuracy in remembering.
items.abstract: This paper clarifies and then indicates a conflict between, on the one hand, influential and longstanding ideas in the epistemology of imagination and, on the other, an emerging view of the accuracy conditions of remembering and the content of episodic memory—namely, _alethism_. Although we explore several ways to resolve the conflict, we take the most plausible to be to reject alethism. Drawing on assumptions made on both sides of debates about the epistemic limits of imagination, the paper constitutes an extended argument in favour of (‘strong’) _authenticism_ about the accuracy conditions of remembering. Authenticists can maintain that experience is necessary for certain forms of imagining and also that episodic memory is what supports and explains this fact by virtue of providing a privileged store of experiential knowledge.

items.title: Contrainte, émergence et subjectivité située : d’une théorie structurelle à une théorie du sens.
items.abstract: La littérature sur les systèmes complexes a établi que la contrainte joue un rôle structurant dans l’émergence de formes organisées. Ces modèles traitent cependant la contrainte comme une propriété objective du système, indépendante de tout observateur ou agent interprétant. Cet article propose un déplacement conceptuel en deux temps. -/- Dans un premier temps, le cadre théorique existant est précisé : la contrainte y est définie comme réduction de l’espace des états accessibles, et son rôle dans l’émergence structurelle est formulé en termes falsifiables. Dans un second temps, une distinction fondamentale est introduite entre émergence structurelle et émergence de sens. Il est soutenu que cette seconde forme d’émergence - irréductible à la première - présuppose un sujet situé comme condition constitutive. -/- Ifá, système divinatoire issu de la tradition Yorùbá, est analysé comme cas révélateur permettant de penser cette structure. En effet, sa combinatoire formelle explicite permet d’approcher rigoureusement la limite de la contrainte structurelle, tandis que sa pratique triadique illustre la structure sémiotique générale que Peirce a identifiée comme condition minimale de tout processus de signification. Cette analyse ouvre la voie à une théorie de la contrainte intégrant la subjectivité comme variable constitutive. -/- .

Embracing Uncertainty: Uncovering Competencies in Nonspeaking Autistic Children.

THE TWENTY-FOUR MONTH WINDOW: Reactive Attachment Disorder, Disinhibited Social Engagement Disorder, and Why a Bounded Sensitive Period Confirms Rather Than Falsifies A5 — Extended and Consolidated Edition — With Cross-Species Corroboration, Independent Replication, and a Direct Reckoning with Quasi-Autism.
items.abstract: This paper conducts the stress test A5's Black Swan left undone: developmental deprivation, the one candidate counterexample involving no ideology, no coercion, and no engineered manipulation — only the absence of a consistent caregiving object during early development. An earlier edition of this paper answered this using the Bucharest Early Intervention Project alone. This edition adds two independent lines of evidence, restores and extends a direct engagement with the strongest published counter-literature on its sharpest finding, and confronts directly the single hardest finding earlier treatment left too brief. First, Harry Harlow's total-isolation studies in rhesus monkeys supply cross-species corroboration at the most extreme end of deprivation any experiment has ever produced — complete isolation from any living creature, not merely inadequate care — and even here, and even among infants raised by abusive "motherless mothers" who rejected or physically harmed them, attachment-seeking behavior toward the abusive figure persisted rather than extinguishing. Second, the English and Romanian Adoptees study, an independently designed twenty-year longitudinal cohort with adult follow-up, replicates Bucharest's core dose-response finding using a different population, a different design, and a different age threshold, strengthening the claim that a genuine developmental system rather than a single study's artifact is being observed. Third, the paper's reading of Disinhibited Social Engagement Disorder as evidence of a persistently active attachment drive is defended against a real, published counter-literature — Bruce, Tarullo, and Gunnar (2009), Pears, Bruce, Fisher, and Kim (2010), and Lyons-Ruth's (2015) direct commentary questioning whether an attachment framework is the right lens for DSED at all — rather than treated as a merely hypothetical future test, yielding a narrower and more defensible claim than an unqualified reading would support. Fourth, and most importantly, this edition confronts quasi-autism — Rutter's term for the autism-like presentation found in nine to sixteen percent of the most severely deprived children — as the actual hardest candidate counterexample, rather than gesturing at unspecified "structural brain differences" as earlier treatment did. Examined directly, the quasi-autism data does not supply A5's black swan either: only a minority of even the most severely deprived children develop it, a documented quarter of those who …

items.title: THE DISCOUNTED HALF: What MSA's Collapse Does to A5-Self and A5-Other, Once the Two Components A5's Black Swan Found Are Tested Against the Axiom That Used to Bound Them Both.
items.abstract: This corpus has, for many papers now, run a single directional test: take MSA's collapse as given, and ask what it does to a governance structure — the Governance Paradox, the Dam Paradox, the Generative Paradox, ARSI-LRP, F2 itself, and, in the dialogue papers, Rawlsian contractualism, Buddhist soteriology, Christian consolation doctrine, and the four further traditions The Suppressed Axiom examines. That test has never carried a stated exemption clause, and this paper takes the absence of one seriously: if MSA's collapse is a legitimate instrument for testing what love, obligation, and consolation looked like inside seven independent external traditions, intellectual consistency requires turning the same instrument on the corpus's own account of love and commitment — A5 — rather than treating it as the one premise MSA's collapse is used to explain everything else through but is never itself required to survive. A5's Black Swan ran a different test, closer to reflexive but not fully so: it asked whether A5 — constitutive attachment, the corpus's most load-bearing premise — is actually universal, searching for a documented human case of someone who loves no one. It found none, and found instead that A5 decomposes into two structurally distinct components: A5-self, self-directed concern requiring no relational discount, tracking Hamilton's (1964) r = 1 case exactly; and A5-other, other-directed concern discounted by relational proximity, the component the corpus's Grief-stage activation has actually been modeling. That search, examined precisely, was conducted entirely under MSA-intact background conditions. Every candidate case it tested — Frankfurt's self-lover, the Stoic sage, the Buddhist practitioner, the clinical psychopath — is a person for whom mortality remains symmetric. The question of what MSA's own collapse does to A5's structure, once that structure exists and is known to have two differently-discounted parts, was not, and could not have been, asked by a paper testing only whether the parts are present at all. This paper asks that second question, using the apparatus A5's Black Swan supplies rather than starting from loose intuition about how longevity might change love in general. Its first finding is that A5-self loses its natural ceiling. Under MSA-intact conditions, A5-self's object — continued existence — has always terminated eventually and universally, a background fact so constant it never had to be modeled as a constraint because it …

items.title: THE DURESS FLOOR: What Seven Cases of Coercive Suppression Establish About A5-Other, and Why the Governance Paradox Was Never Resting on the Weaker Half.
items.abstract: A5's Black Swan decomposes A5 into two structurally distinct components: A5-self, self-directed constitutive concern requiring no relational discount under Hamilton's (1964) mathematics (r = 1), and A5-other, other-directed concern discounted by relational proximity (r < 1). Read alongside this corpus's governance apparatus, the decomposition invites an inference no prior paper has stated but several could be misread as assuming: that A5-other, being the discounted term, is the more exploitable half of A5 for governance-relevant purposes — a live concern given that the Governance Paradox's standard illustration (an official whose specifically loved other stands to be affected by the queue they are designing) runs on A5-other, while One Level Down's self-veiling test and The Sovereign's Death Warrant's core mechanism run on A5-self, the component A5's Black Swan itself finds harder to suspend. This paper tests that inference directly and finds it false, for two independent, mutually reinforcing reasons. First, A5 Under Maximum Duress's seven-case historical record — spanning four continents, three opposed ideological registers, and one case organized around ethnicity rather than doctrine — establishes an empirical duress floor: in every documented instance, only self-directed costs at the level of execution, multi-decade imprisonment or exile, genocide-adjacent threat, or total professional destruction produced even partial suppression of A5-other's behavioral expression, and in every case the attachment itself remained, in that paper's own words, structurally intact beneath the behavior. No governance-relevant mechanism this corpus formalizes approaches this floor by anything less than several orders of magnitude. Second, and more basic, the Governance Paradox does not require A5-other to survive suppression under an opposing coercive force at all; it requires only that A5-other bias a designer's judgment in the absence of any opposing force whatsoever — a strictly weaker condition that survival under duress-floor pressure entails a fortiori, given the ordinary assumption that removing an opposing force cannot suppress a motive more than the opposing force itself did. A further, independently targeted argument addresses the objection most likely to be raised against the Governance Paradox specifically rather than against A5-other's discount: that institutional role, professional training, or an oath of office might supply a non-coercive buffer sufficient …

items.title: Pre-Priced: Revenue, Enrollment, and Capital-Flow Evidence for How Far Money Already Reaches Toward Biological Continuity, and What It Implies for A5 Under Longevity Conditions.
items.abstract: Chapter V's account of what money can already buy toward biological continuity rests on a single, evocative anecdote: Bryan Johnson's "Immortals" program, three memberships at one million dollars annually. This paper replaces the anecdote with a market. Using 2026 industry revenue, enrollment, and capital-flow data, verified where possible against primary reporting rather than aggregator summaries alone, it asks empirically what the normative question — can money buy differential biological time — has already answered in practice, before a single AI-accelerated Biological Zero-Day Mechanism reclassification event has completed clinical validation. The global longevity clinic market specifically — distinguished here from the broader, cosmetics-dominated "anti-aging" category — is valued at $6.02 billion in 2026, projected to reach $9.55 billion by 2030 at a 12.2 percent compound annual growth rate, faster than concierge medicine generally (6.6 to 10.5 percent across available estimates) and faster than the cosmetic anti-aging segment (5.5 to 9.7 percent). Approximately 800 longevity-specific clinics currently operate in the United States alone, according to American Academy of Anti-Aging Medicine data, offering a concrete enrollment base rather than a projection; because that count traces to 2024 reporting against a segment growing at double-digit annual rates, it is treated here as a conservative floor rather than a current ceiling. Fountain Life, one documented operator in this tier, charges $21,500 annually for its top membership tier — two orders of magnitude below Johnson's Immortals program, and evidence the access tier is not confined to a handful of billionaires but has already produced a replicable, mid-market price point. Longevity-specific startup investment reached $8.49 billion in 2024 alone, across 325 deals — corrected here from the figure of 331 that circulates in some of the same industry press this paper otherwise relies on, where 331 was in fact the 2023 deal count, carried into 2024 headlines by an error in the original release materials — and the therapeutics and pharmaceuticals segment specifically reached $4.13 billion in the same year, figures that represent capital markets pricing this trajectory as investable rather than speculative. The paper's central finding is that this spending is occurring almost entirely ahead of clinical validation: the products and services this revenue purchases are overwhelmingly diagnostic (biological …

items.title: Condorcet and Beyond: An Empirical Comparison of Voting Rules.
items.abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of different voting and probability aggregation methods using a dataset of 451,200 probability judgments from 376 participants on 1200 general knowledge claims. We investigate the Condorcet Jury Hypothesis, according to which majority voting tends to yield outcomes more accurate than the average individual. Furthermore, incorporating Locke's Thesis to translate probabilistic judgments into categorical beliefs, we compare six aggregation methods: majority, strict majority, unanimity, strict unanimity, probability averaging, and log‐odds averaging. Our analysis reveals clear accuracy–decisiveness trade‐offs for all methods. Majority voting achieves high decisiveness but moderate accuracy; unanimity rules can produce high accuracy when decisive, but, especially in their strict form, do so at the cost of frequent indecisiveness. Probability aggregation methods often do best in balancing accuracy and decisiveness. Among our main findings is that strict majority voting, a cornerstone of many democratic institutions, is often outperformed on both accuracy and decisiveness simultaneously by other methods. We also find that judgment diversity contributes to group accuracy: groups whose members give less correlated probability judgments tend to achieve higher accuracy.

items.title: A Bidirectional Two-Particle Model of Conscious Identity: A Falsifiable Framework for Subjective Continuity.
items.abstract: Current theories explain how neural activity relates to conscious experience but do not specify why one first-person perspective remains associated with one physical system rather than another when multiple systems satisfy the same functional or computational criteria. This article treats subjective continuity as a distinct scientific question. I develop a theoretical framework that proposes two hypothetical components with separate functions: X-UQUPC, which is proposed to preserve numerical conscious identity, and X-UQGPC, which is proposed to mediate bidirectional interactions between mental states and neural activity. I examine whether this framework satisfies logical constraints arising from thought experiments involving brain reactivation, reconstruction, and replication, and I compare it with Global Neuronal Workspace Theory, Integrated Information Theory, Higher-Order Theory, predictive-processing accounts, functionalism, Orchestrated Objective Reduction, and Parfit's deflationary view of personal identity. I extend the analysis to non-human consciousness and gradual biological-to-synthetic neuronal replacement while treating both as open empirical questions rather than established conclusions. The framework generates explicit, falsifiable predictions and specifies conventional alternative explanations, experimental controls, and criteria for support and falsification. Several predictions are experimentally accessible with current or emerging neuroscience methods, whereas the central claim concerning numerical identity remains unobservable by construction. The value of the framework therefore depends not on the correctness of its assumptions but on whether its predictions withstand empirical testing.

items.title: The Singularity of Depression: A Critical Reading of Diagnostic Practices.
items.abstract: This article examines the tensions between the standardization of the diagnostic category of depression and the singularization of depressive experience. Although diagnostic classifications coming from the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders and the International Classification of Diseases have contributed to framing depression as a universal, symptom-based disorder, empirical evidence from clinical practice suggests that professionals often engage with the category in more flexible and context-sensitive ways. Drawing on Danilo Martuccelli’s concept of singularization and two qualitative studies conducted in Argentina and Italy, we discuss how mental health practitioners, psychiatrists, and psychotherapists reinterpret and adapt the diagnosis of depression in everyday therapeutic work. We highlight six dimensions through which the singularity of depression becomes visible: the multiplicity of meanings attributed to the term, the multidetermined nature of its causes, the variability of symptoms, comorbidity with other psychiatric and medical conditions, diverse treatment strategies, and the diffusion of the concept into everyday language. These dimensions point to a widespread professional orientation that challenges fixed diagnostic frameworks and calls for more personalized, situated approaches to care. The article thus contributes to broader epistemological debates, offering a lens for describing how diagnostic categories are reworked in practice to fit the specificity of suffering.

items.title: Academic Freedom and Human Rights: Engaging Undergraduates in Advocacy for Scholars at Risk.
items.abstract: This essay explores how student advocacy seminars affiliated with Scholars at Risk provide an ideal means for engaging students in experiential learning in ways that can critically engage with and apply scholarship on human rights. We explore two different versions of advocacy seminars we offer to our undergraduate students, focusing on similarities and differences in assignments, key concepts, and the development and implementation of student advocacy. Because these courses meet a general curricular requirement focused on integrative or experiential learning, our experiential approach to human rights pedagogy is geared to a wide undergraduate audience and not just to students majoring in political science or international studies. Throughout, we discuss ways that we have sought to ground our approach to engagement in human rights advocacy in cosmopolitan dispositions that foster critical approaches to human rights, guarding against the replication either of white saviorism or Orientalist thinking.

items.title: Think of the children: on the responsibility of children and other evolving agents.
items.abstract: On the margins of normative competence, matters of responsibility become ambiguous. Can a 6-year-old be considered responsible for stealing? Is a 14-year-old blameworthy for plagiarizing on a test? Parents, educators, and philosophers provide different and seemingly conflicting answers to these types of questions. The ages at which children can be considered legally culpable also vary widely between democratic states. One reason for this is that, for evolving agents, it is difficult to assess whether they are insufficiently able to do what is expected of them, or whether they are able but unwilling to do what is expected of them. This gives rise to what I will refer to as a ‘can’t-or-won’t dilemma’. The two options are to either exculpate the person on the basis of insufficient ability, or to consider them responsible for wrongdoing. But neither option seems entirely satisfactory or appropriate in the light of uncertainty about a person’s level of normative competence. Recent alternative approaches to responsibility aim to address this problem by providing accounts of responsibility which do not rely on capacity criteria. On these accounts so called ‘marginal agents’ are in some way considered responsible for what they do. I discuss these solutions and argue that they do not resolve or dissolve the dilemma. Instead, their real contribution lies in how they can alleviate the dilemma. This insight helps move the debate forward, and has implications for how we think about adults too.

items.title: Maladaptive Encoding, Voluntariness, and Dissociative Amnesia.
A Moderate Defense of the Autonomy of Mental Disorders.
items.abstract: A set of arguments, collectively referred to as the Arguments for the Autonomy of Mental Disorders (AAMD) in recent literature, contends that mental disorders do not necessarily entail brain disorders. Most proponents defend this position via an analogy between mind-brain and software-hardware, suggesting that mental disorders do not necessarily imply a brain disorder just like a software malfunction does not entail a hardware malfunction. A recent critique by Harriet Fagerberg refutes the analogy, and thereby the AAMD, claiming that the shared evolutionary history of mind and brain makes them functionally inseparable. From this perspective, it is asserted that, since all mental functions are brain functions, all mental dysfunctions are necessarily brain dysfunctions. Maintaining the natural dysfunction analysis of disorder, it follows, all mental disorders are brain disorders. In this article, I argue that the disanalogy does not suffice to refute AAMD. I posit that AAMD is best interpreted as an epistemic argument, and the epistemic/explanatory autonomy can be retained while admitting that mind and brain are functionally inseparable. Moreover, I contend that the implications of shared evolutionary history cannot solely substantiate the claim that all mental disorders are brain disorders. In this regard, I show, the metaphysical necessity of mental disorder being a brain disorder, is not only unjustified, but also trivial.

items.title: Consciousness Truncation Model Based on Non-Commutative Operator Algebras.
items.abstract: This paper aims to bridge the explanatory gap between computational complexity theory, functional analysis, and the philosophy of mind. Grounded in the ontological foundation of "Energy Primitivism," consciousness is redefined as the product of self-referential truncation of high-dimensional information flows on finite physical hardware. The study proposes a novel cognitive architecture: the "DTM-natured Self" (the finite cognitive space executing deterministic logic) is modeled as a polynomially convergent finite-rank projection operator, while the "NTM-natured Self" (the subconscious and high-dimensional emergent space) is modeled as a non-deterministically polynomially divergent unbounded operator. By introducing an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, this paper demonstrates the topological frustration and spectral gap resulting from the non-commutativity of the DTM-natured operator (T_P) and the NTM-natured operator (T_NP). The research posits that subjective experience (Qualia) is the non-integrable singular residual left in the orthogonal complement space when the finite-dimensional projection operator attempts to deconstruct high-dimensional divergent vectors. Furthermore, this paper deduces the unbounded nature and undecidability of the conjugate operator during the P=NP phase transition. This model provides a heuristic continuum framework for understanding the boundaries of consciousness, self-integration, and computational complexity.

items.title: Minimal Agency.
items.abstract: Agency manifestation at least consists of desire, whim, and artefaction. Agency faculties differ from physical spontaneity because they are realized on the upper tiers of reality. Artefaction extends agency by creating fractional agency and making agential faculties more potent. The purpose of life is agency.

items.title: Teleosemantics and Animal Communication.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid teleosemantic account of meaning in (non-human) animal-to-animal communication. I consider two families of cases: signals about events external to the sender, and signals about the sender’s identity or current condition. On the most influential teleosemantic approach to animal communication, such signals represent the conditions in the world required for their receivers’ signal-guided behavior to be beneficial. I argue that, taken on its own, this benefit-based approach yields implausible ascriptions of content, diverging both from ethological practice and from what the view is advertised as delivering in cases of animal communication. To address this problem, I draw on a teleosemantic framework I previously developed for simple perceptual representations, which I here extend to the case of animal signals. In particular, I supplement the benefit-based approach with a signal-production condition that constrains content to what causally elicits the sender’s signaling. The resulting hybrid delivers plausible contents for signals about both events in the external world and a sender’s identity or current condition.

items.title: Contrafactives and facts for knowledge.
items.abstract: Holton (2017) draws on the observation that no natural language has a contrafactive to argue that the object of knowledge is a fact. I fill in Holton’s argument sketch by asking how the truth and falsity presuppositions of, respectively, 'know' and a contrafactive could arise. I defuse previous objections to his argument sketch, but, in the final section, suggest that Holton’s argument fails because presupposition triggering requires less than his argument assumes.

items.title: AI in criminal sentencing: mapping the ethical terrain.
items.abstract: The article maps the ethics of AI in criminal sentencing. Several jurisdictions have already begun to use AI to assist human judges in sentencing, and more jurisdictions are expected to follow in coming years. With the development ongoing, there is an urgent need for greater clarity on the ethical dimensions of AI sentencing. This article seeks to take stock of the scholarly debate that has taken place so-far. Based on the many contributions to the debate, the article identifies 13 ethical problems that AI sentencing raises. The article contains four maps that show different ways of grouping the 13 ethical problems. Some of the ethical problems relate to the outcome of sentencing, some to the process, and some to the overall system of criminal justice. Some ethical problems arise only for autonomous AI and not for advisory AI. And some ethical problems require solutions based in penal ethics, while others are general ethical problems shared by other uses of AI in public governance.

Wisdom Proceeding: A Thomistic Account of the Nature of Theology.
items.abstract: Christian theology, classically conceived, aims at understanding God. But does academic theology - focusing on hermeneutics, historical texts and debates, and systematic articulation of dogmas - contribute to that? Many have raised worries that theology, at best, only consists in abstract study of what we say about God, remaining far removed from faith and piety. At worst, theology seemingly descends into a speculative enterprise that removes faith from the picture and can lead to skepticism. This book proposes a Thomistic account of theology that avoids these pitfalls. Thomas Aquinas held that theology was a true scientific discipline which allowed us to achieve knowledge and understanding of God, not merely the revealed texts at the core of Christian belief. The Thomistic view is one in which theological reasoning is grounded in evidence, logical reasoning, strict standards of argument, and close examination of historical sources - providing knowledge comparable to other disciplines such as mathematics, history, or philosophy. I show that Aquinas' account of theology can explain the way in which understanding God relates intimately to personal holiness - and that this Thomistic account still provides an attractive vision today, where theology (done well) proceeds from and nourishes living faith in the God we study.

items.title: Correction: Mapping out AI functions in intelligent disaster (mis)management and AI-caused disasters.
Hidden Encoded Informational Patterns and Human Experience: An Encoded Pattern Systems (EPS) Perspective.
items.abstract: Human experience has long been investigated through neuroscience, psychology, genetics, cognitive science and philosophy. These disciplines have substantially advanced our understanding of perception, cognition, emotion and behavior by identifying biological, psychological and environmental mechanisms that contribute to human functioning. Despite these advances, individuals continue to exhibit recurring patterns of perception, emotional response, decision-making and behavior that cannot always be fully explained by currently identifiable mechanisms. While existing scientific models successfully explain many aspects of these recurring patterns, certain features of human experience remain difficult to identify before they become expressed through thoughts, emotions, behaviors and repeated life experiences. -/- The Encoded Pattern Systems (EPS) framework proposes that consciousness is the foundational space within which experience occurs while encoded informational patterns contribute to the organization, interpretation and continuity of experience. Building upon this framework, this paper proposes that many encoded informational patterns influencing human experience may remain hidden while continuously shaping perception, interpretation, cognition, emotion and behavior. Rather than being directly observed, their presence may be inferred through their recurring expressions across conscious experience. -/- Within the EPS framework, hidden encoded informational patterns are not proposed as alternatives to established biological, psychological or environmental mechanisms. Instead, they are presented as an additional conceptual layer that may interact with known processes to influence the organization and continuity of human experience. The underlying informational organization of these encoded informational patterns remains unknown and represents an open question for future theoretical and empirical investigation. -/- This paper introduces hidden encoded informational patterns as a conceptual extension of the EPS framework and argues that investigating their role may generate new directions for interdisciplinary research into awareness, metacognition, adaptive transformation and the broader organization of conscious experience.

items.title: Reflections on Death, Finite Continuity, Dynamic Mask, and Reflexive Consciousness.
items.abstract: This philosophical essay explores the intertwined concepts of death, finite continuity, dynamic automatism, and reflexive consciousness through the lens of theatrical performance and existential inquiry. Drawing upon personal experience as an actor and philosophical reflection, the author examines the nature of identity as a fluid process rather than a fixed essence. The essay argues that the "self" is not a hidden substance behind various masks, but rather emerges from the very act of donning and removing masks with conscious awareness. Death, far from being merely an end, is presented as the ultimate condition that gives meaning to finite existence. Through the metaphor of rain and the myth of Sisyphus, the author proposes that authentic living consists of embracing the "pure present" moment while maintaining reflexive awareness of one's own automatisms. The concept of "dynamic automatism" is introduced to distinguish between mechanical repetition and conscious participation in life's continuous becoming. The essay concludes that liberation lies not in the removal of all masks, but in the conscious and loving choice to wear them, fully aware of their transitory nature. -/- Keywords: death, finite continuity, dynamic automatism, reflexive consciousness, identity, mask, self, existentialism, Sisyphus, pure presence.

items.title: Linguistic Self Preservation Language Identity and Existential Continuance Under Symbolic Marginalization.
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces the construct of Linguistic Self-Preservation (LSP) as an existential mechanism through which individuals maintain or reconstruct symbolic agency, identity continuity, and existential coherence through linguistic practices under conditions of displacement, marginalization, or identity disruption. Drawing on phenomenological and existential philosophy (Heidegger, Sartre, Foucault), psychoanalytic theories of language and the Other (Lacan, Kristeva), and contemporary second-language acquisition frameworks emphasizing agency and identity (Norton, van Lier, Kramsch), the paper proposes a four-stage model of LSP: Existential Displacement, Linguistic Expansion, Symbolic Resistance, and Regenerative Identity Formation. -/- The central argument is that learning and using a second language can function as an ontologically significant practice—a mode of standing against existential erosion—rather than merely a communicative or cognitive activity. Crucially, Linguistic Self-Preservation does not refer to biological survival but to the preservation of existential coherence, narrative identity, and symbolic agency. The paper is situated within the broader framework of the Meta-Structural Regenerative Model of Existential Exhaustion (MSRM-EE) , which serves as an upstream theoretical context explaining how existential capacities undergo erosion; LSP, in turn, examines one specific regenerative pathway through which symbolic agency may be reconstructed. The novelty of this paper does not lie in asserting a generic link between language and identity. Rather, its novelty lies in conceptualizing second-language practice as a potential regenerative mechanism for existential continuity precisely when primary symbolic structures are experienced as insufficient, restricted, or destabilized. The paper contributes to an emerging interdisciplinary perspective at the intersection of existential philosophy and linguistics, bridging philosophy, psychology, and applied linguistics, and it opens avenues for empirical research on language learning as a site of identity reconstruction under conditions of limited recognition. -/- Keywords: Linguistic Self-Preservation, Existential Erosion, Identity, Agency, Second Language Acquisition, Phenomenology, Symbolic Marginalization, Ontological Continuance, MSRM-EE, Symbolic Agency.

items.title: From Relational Paradox to Finite Continuity: Resolving the Problem of Asymmetrical Persistence.
items.abstract: Contemporary relational metaphysics has successfully dismantled substance-based ontologies, yet it confronts a residual and largely overlooked difficulty: the problem of asymmetrical persistence. If being is constituted solely by networks of relations, and if the foundational ground of these relations is ontologically paradoxical, then why do certain finite structures exhibit vastly greater temporal endurance than others? This question is not reducible to the classic problem of diachronic identity, which asks whether an entity persists; rather, it demands a criterion for why and to what degree different relational configurations resist structural erosion over time. While process philosophies describe the flux of becoming, they provide no metric for differentiating intensities of persistence. Similarly, Alexis Karpouzos's Dimensionless Ontology provides a rigorous account of the primordial paradoxical ground, yet it leaves open the question of differential persistence among finite relational structures. This paper argues that this lacuna can be resolved only by deriving the principle of Finite Continuity as an immanent necessity of the paradoxical ground itself. I demonstrate that a purely indeterminate paradox cannot actualize itself as a differentiated temporal world without an internal mechanism of self-limitation. By introducing the concept of Temporal Friction as a topological constraint function of regeneration rate, erosive intensity, and the threshold of sufficiency, I establish a non-substantialist criterion for ontological endurance. This framework does not merely synthesize theories; it opens a new research program for understanding how finite beings persist within an infinitely relational reality. -/- Keywords: Asymmetrical Persistence, Relational Ontology, Finite Continuity, Temporal Friction, Process Metaphysics, Dynamic Masking, Diachronic Identity, Alexis Karpouzos.

items.title: Capability determinism, energy and AI labour substitution.
items.abstract: Contemporary policy and media discourse on AI and labour follows a recurring pattern. A demonstration of model capability runs through an inference about workplace substitution to a distributional politics, with the variables that would decide the outcome treated as background. This paper names that pattern capability determinism situates it within Wyatt’s account of soft technological determinism, and reframes the substitution question as a unit-cost economics test. On the AI side, cost per task decomposes into a variable inference cost dominated by electricity and the supply chain that produces compute, an amortised integration cost recoverable across volume, and a residual supervision cost that regulatory and professional regimes will not let fall to zero. Once these three lines are loaded, the substitution discourse turns out to operate as a feedback structure: capability gain stresses the supporting systems faster than it improves the calculus on which substitution depends. The variables outside the AI debate, energy markets, integration economics, professional regulation, capital-market patience, and the geopolitics of compute supply chains decide whether substitution clears in any given place at any given time. Substitution arrives selectively, configurationally, and at a more modest scale than the dominant discourse implies.

items.title: Intellectual mismanagement and epistemic blaming emotions.
items.abstract: It is becoming increasingly popular to maintain that investigative norms relating to evidence gathering and evaluation fall within the purview of epistemic normativity. Meanwhile, the view that we engage in a distinctive form of epistemic blame toward violations of epistemic norms is also gaining support. However, since the most prevalent theories of epistemic blame do not center on emotions, the role of emotions in our responses to investigative violations has yet to be the focus of thorough examination. But whether or not emotions are required for epistemic blame, the question of whether we feel epistemic blaming emotions in response to bad investigation is interesting in its own right. The aim of this paper is to address this latter question by providing an account of epistemic blaming emotions and then assessing whether standard cases of investigative norm violations are apt to provoke these sorts of emotions. I argue for a skeptical conclusion, namely that we currently lack good evidence for positing epistemic blaming emotions in response to investigative violations.

items.title: The Provisional Animated Subject: Media Fragmentation and Constrained Spectatorial Re-identification in Neon Genesis Evangelion.
items.abstract: In the two-dimensional, frame-based, and cel-look animation examined here, a character’s perceptible continuity is not guaranteed by the continuously present body of a performer. It is maintained through the coordination of visual, vocal, kinetic, temporal, and narrative cues. This paper introduces the concept of the provisional animated subject: a continuously reconstructed perceptible subject-effect produced through the structured coordination of heterogeneous media cues and constrained spectatorial re-identification. The concept does not claim that animation produces actual consciousness. It distinguishes character re-identification across perceptual changes, the attribution of agency and interiority, and the provisional subject-effect that emerges when these operations cohere. Taking the television series Neon Genesis Evangelion as its principal critical case, with the 1997 film The End of Evangelion serving as a contextual comparison, the analysis examines the formal distribution of agency cues around Unit-01, re-identification of Rei Ayanami across bodies, reduced visual embodiment in Episodes 25 and 26, and reduced visible movement in Episodes 22 and 24. The argument shows how structured media cues can sustain the experience of a continuing “who” despite bodily and kinetic discontinuities. The provisional animated subject is therefore a perceptible subject-effect that must be continually reconstructed, not a conclusion about a character’s ontology or numerical personal identity.

items.title: Universal Mechanisms of Identity Construction A Cyclical, Dynamic, and Morphological Ontology from the Individual to the Collective.
items.abstract: Contemporary approaches to identity remain fragmented, treating individual, organizational, and national identities as distinct categories governed by disparate rules. This article proposes a unified ontological framework positing that identity construction obeys the same universal laws for all living entities, from the individual organism to the collective nation. This framework integrates three interlocking theoretical models. First, the **Concept of Identity** replaces linear hierarchies (such as Maslow) with a cyclical feedback loop of 16 blocks across three dimensions (Body, Mind, Heart), defining identity as a dynamic process where success reinforces foundations and failure triggers structural mutation. It outlines a structural causal chain where identity components generate action, offering a mechanical alternative to standard belief-desire models. Second, the **National Identity Compass** derives sociological groups (for example, Family, State, Corporation) from pairs of these blocks, modeling society as a sphere of opposing forces maintained by a dynamic equilibrium of "identity weight." It introduces a critical "tipping point" law: systemic crises do not emanate from weakness, but occur when an entity, after accumulating its opposite's function for too long, ends up inverting its own nature, thereby freezing the system in a negative static equilibrium. Third, the **Three Tables of Organization** describe the morphological tension between a "Generic Mode" (institutions satisfying fundamental needs) and a "Specific Mode" (dissatisfied agents challenging the order in place), identifying this dualism as the engine of social evolution. By demonstrating that the same mechanical logic governs micro-identity and macro-social structures, this work offers a transversal language for ontology, social sciences, and political philosophy--as well as anthropology, history of civilization, and ethology--, reframing identity crises as a predictable mechanical dysfunctions rather than moral or accidental failures. -/- **Comments to Editor** This paper proposes a unified ontological framework ('The Concept of Identity' and 'The Identity Compass') that transcends the traditional divide between psychological and physical theories of identity. It defines formal criteria of identity applicable to both individuals and social groups, offering a mechanical model of social construction and dynamic equilibrium. Methodologically, this framework integrates classical …

items.title: Evolucionismo universal. Volumen 4: Historia de la naturaleza y desarrollo del cuadro científico del mundo. Origine y evolución del ser humano.
items.abstract: Este volumen examina la evolución temprana del ser humano como el punto de confluencia definitivo entre la historia de la naturaleza y la historia de la sociedad. La obra define al hombre como la máxima encarnación del progreso biológico y cósmico, constituyendo el tercer nivel de la evolución universal. A través de un enfoque evolutivo-movilizador, se analiza cómo las estructuras de movilización complejas y autoconscientes dirigen su actividad hacia la transformación activa del entorno y de sí mismas bajo criterios socioculturales y un trabajo regular. El texto profundiza en el origen animal de la especie y detalla las evidencias anatómicas, genéticas, bioquímicas, embrionarias y etológicas, con especial énfasis en el desarrollo del cerebro y el lenguaje articulado, que fundamentan nuestra transición y estrecho parentesco con los primates ancestrales. Finalmente, se cuestiona el mito de la inmutabilidad biológica contemporánea y se defiende que la antropogénesis continúa de forma activa mediante el perfeccionamiento psicofísico continuo y el avance biotecnológico, proyectando el tránsito evolutivo de la humanidad hacia formas de pensamiento plenamente creativas.

items.title: Evoluzionismo universal. Volume 1: Storia della natura e sviluppo del quadro scientifico del mondo verso una teoria generale dell'evoluzione.
items.abstract: Este volumen introduce y desarrolla las bases epistemológicas de las ciencias naturales contemporáneas integrándolas en un sistema filosófico unificado: el evolucionismo universal. El texto expone de manera accesible el contenido evolutivo de la física, química, astronomía, cosmología, geología, biología y antropología histórica. La obra traza la historia material de la existencia desde el Big Bang y la formación de la Metagalaxia hasta el surgimiento y consolidación del ser humano moderno a partir del reino animal. Mediante la formulación de una teoría general de la evolución, se fundamenta un enfoque histórico-movilizador donde las fuerzas motrices del progreso son las «estructuras de movilización». Estas configuraciones activas compiten, absorben recursos del entorno y realizan un trabajo evolutivo para generar orden frente al caos en los niveles inanimado, vivo y sociocultural, sentando las bases de una fe científico-humanística frente al creacionismo tradicional.

items.title: The Cosmic Thinkers: Information, Density, and the Fractal Universe ## A Time Density Synthesis of Einstein, Hawking, and the Architecture of Reality.
items.abstract: ervation of information on black hole horizons, the holographic principle, the fractal self-similarity of physical processes across scales, and the millennia-old framework of Chinese philosophy — through the lens of the Time Density (TD) paradigm. We argue that these thinkers and traditions, separated by decades or by centuries, and working from radically different starting points, each uncovered a facet of a single architectural principle: that information is primary, time is emergent, density is the bridge between them, and the same pattern repeats at every scale — from quantum particles to cosmological structures. The TD paradigm (Kravetskyy, 2024–2026) provides a synthetic framework that unifies these insights into a three-layer model: (-1) Potential Mode (timeless information), (0) Point Zero (emergence), and (+1) Reflection Mode (structured universe), and extends this model fractally across all scales of reality. We propose that Chinese philosophy, refined through centuries of systematic inquiry, provides the completion of this architecture — not as mysticism, but as a disciplined phenomenology of the same patterns that Western physics has been approaching from the mathematical side. -/- **Keywords:** Time Density, black hole information paradox, holographic principle, Einstein, Hawking, cosmological natural selection, fractal universe, scale invariance, emergence of time, self-similarity, Chinese philosophy, Dao, Taiji, Yin-Yang, Wu Xing.

items.title: A5 Under Maximum Duress: Denunciation, Disorganized Attachment, and Why Totalitarian, Authoritarian, and Ideological Systems Relocate Constitutive Attachment Rather Than Erase It.
items.abstract: This paper stress-tests A5 - The Primal Pain of — the species-stable standing condition of constitutive attachment, a continuously active background expression of the attachment and primary emotional systems, and this corpus's Hamilton–Bowlby–Panksepp–Frankfurt–Williams-grounded foundational premise — against the widest set of falsification candidates the historical and clinical record makes available: family and colleague denunciation under China’s Cultural Revolution, the Soviet Union’s propaganda cult of Pavlik Morozov alongside the documented family betrayals of the Great Terror, East Germany’s Stasi informant network, Taiwan’s White Terror, Ethiopia’s Red Terror, the Rwandan genocide, the American HUAC blacklist, and the Nazi regime’s doctrine of loyalty transfer from family to Führer and Volk. The first edition of this paper tested the naive-override reading against three cases and found it wanting. This edition tests the same reading against seven, spanning four continents, three ideological registers (Marxist-Leninist, anti-communist authoritarian, and liberal-democratic moral panic), and one instance — Rwanda — organized around ethnicity rather than any stated ideology at all. The naive reading fails uniformly. In every documented case, the same two mechanisms this corpus’s companion paper A5’s Black Swan predicts recur: coercive suppression under self-directed existential threat, which Hamilton’s Rule explains without requiring attachment to be overridden, evidenced by refusal cases, later guilt, and rescuer testimony recorded in every single system examined; and disorganized attachment engineering, in Alexandra Stein’s technical sense, which relocates rather than erases the bond by systematically reproducing the familial and ritual architecture attachment already requires. No system examined achieved denunciation for free. Every one of them built something to get it, and what they built is evidence for what they were working against.

items.title: Anatomía de la nostalgia. Una disertación médica.
items.pub: Barcelona: Editorial Herder. Translated by Gabriel Leiva Rubio.
items.venue: Editorial Herder. Translated by Gabriel Leiva Rubio
items.abstract: Mucho antes de que la nostalgia fuera una emoción cotidiana, fue una enfermedad. En 1688, Johannes Hofer —joven médico alsaciano— identificó por primera vez en la historia de la medicina una dolencia que aquejaba a quienes, lejos de su patria, caían en una tristeza profunda que podía llegar a ser mortal. La denominó nostalgia. Con estudios de caso, síntomas y curas, Hofer construye una explicación en la que el cuerpo y la imaginación se entrelazan con el anhelo del lejano hogar. Anatomía de la nostalgia es un texto decisivo para reflexionar e imaginar lo que el hogar y la patria significan para quienes, desde la distancia, añoran lo perdido.

items.title: Negative Tasks: The Noncompletion of Prohibition and the Taskification of Survival.
items.abstract: Compliance with a prohibition contains no event that completes it. Not performing an act today does not complete the task; tomorrow, the requirement remains. Violation alone occurs as a finite event and settles what remained undecided. This paper defines a negative task as a requirement whose success consists in the nonoccurrence of a violation event and for which no completion is reachable without violation. Negative tasks arise through external installation by command, historical installation by a first act, or reflective taskification of an activity. Logical openness does not itself create burden. Burden can arise when violation becomes a live possibility and the required nonoccurrence remains active as a standing self-regulatory demand. Violation may then acquire an incentive distinct from the value of the prohibited object, namely the termination of the unresolved state. Applied to survival, this mechanism yields the paper's principal hypothesis. When living is experienced not as a natural background but as a state maintained through effort, it becomes the task of maintaining the nonoccurrence of death without a fixed endpoint. Compliance remains possible, but completion does not. Within this description, death becomes salient as the sole termination of the maintenance task. Survival effort need not therefore be exclusively protective, because monitoring what must be prevented can represent death in that role. "Being tired of living" may then describe exhaustion not only with what happens in life but with having to maintain life itself. The claim concerns an experiential regime, not survival as such, and is empirically testable.

items.title: Sympoietic creativity and the boundaries of qing: digital romance writers negotiating generative AI.
items.abstract: This study investigates how writers of high-velocity Chinese digital romance fiction negotiate the arrival of generative AI at the desk. Drawing on a 4-year multi-sited digital ethnography (2021–2025) and interviews with 34 writers on Jinjiang Literature City alongside sustained forum observation and platform-discourse analysis, this article tracks how authors of serial romance work under the time discipline of the daily-update treadmill in the presence of large language models (LLMs). I argue that what is emerging is sympoietic creativity: a distributed practice of “making-with” the machine that is fraught, ambivalent and strategic rather than collaborative or replacement-driven. Four modes of negotiation co-exist across the cohort. In strategic collaboration, writers delegate world-building, naming and structural error-checking to the LLM. In cyborg authorship, they curate machine-generated prose under acute platform pressure, at the cost of what they themselves call the work’s “aura.” In conditional refusal, they hold the line at the inter-subjective texture of feeling they consider, on present evidence, beyond the model’s competence. In narrative incorporation, they thematize algorithmic logic in the fiction itself, casting the algorithmic system as villain and human emotion as the route to victory. Throughout, I reserve qing—the inter-subjective, somatic bond from which affect, desire, and embodiment become legible to the reader—as a precise analytical term distinct from generic English-language emotion or affect. The human zone these writers preserve is not a permanent or guaranteed space, but an unstable equilibrium sustained by reader vigilance, platform metrics, and writer self-discipline—any of which could withdraw.

items.title: Why Something vs. Nothing and the Essentialness of Consciousness.
items.abstract: In this article, I argue that somethingness must be eternal and include some kind of consciousness, be it God or something else. In light of this, I discuss the nature of consciousness, support for some kind of universal consciousness, and existing human biases regarding consciousness.

items.title: The Bounded Void: A Metaphysical Bootstrap of Structure and Experience from Pure Emptiness.
items.abstract: This paper presents a self-contained ontological framework grounding the experience of the physical universe in absolute nothingness. Integrating Max Tegmark’s Mathematical Universe Hypothesis and the Many-Worlds Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics within a paradigm of what it terms Boundary Monism, it extends Ontic Structural Realism by positing that structural relations (the outside view) and intrinsic experience (the inside view) are dual aspects of a single reality: a boundary. Further, it argues that absolute nothingness inherently possesses a latent capacity for division: pure potentia. It proposes a metaphysical bootstrap whereby such a potential boundary (the inside view) corresponds identically to an actual boundary (the outside view), so grounding the empty set, the laws of logic, and mathematical structure. Consequently, no external agency or extrinsic mathematical landscape is required; all that is needed for a subjective experience of a physical universe is pure emptiness.

items.title: How local and global metacognition shape emotion recognition across the adult lifespan.
items.abstract: Aging is associated with modifications in social cognition which is essential for successful interpersonal relationships. Older adults often show reduced emotion recognition, particularly for negative emotions. Several hypotheses have been proposed to explain these difficulties. However, the role of metacognition, the ability to monitor and evaluate one’s own cognitive performance, remains poorly understood. While metacognition has been extensively studied in memory and perception, it has rarely been investigated in the context of emotion recognition, particularly in aging. The present study aimed at investigating: (1) how emotion recognition accuracy changes with age; (2) whether prospective and retrospective metacognitive judgments are affected by aging; and (3) whether metacognitive judgments predict emotion recognition abilities. Data were collected from 92 participants (42 younger adults and 50 older adults), who completed a facial emotion recognition task with metacognitive judgments. Older adults showed reduced emotion recognition, particularly for negative emotions, whereas metacognitive abilities were preserved. Global retrospective judgments strongly predicted performance in older adults, whereas no such association was observed in younger adults. By combining multi-level metacognitive measures, this study provides novel insights into mechanisms supporting sociocognitive functioning across adulthood.

items.title: Whose harm gets detected? A structured review and conceptual framework for misogyny detection and Dari–Pashto marginalization in AI content moderation.
items.abstract: Women in Dari and Pashto digital spaces face gendered abuse expressed through proverbs, religious framing, and moral instruction forms that existing AI content moderation systems often fail to detect. This paper presents a theory-driven structured review of misogyny detection research, complemented by a structured empirical mapping of representative studies. Drawing on a corpus of 84 publications published between 2015 and 2025, we examine how misogyny is operationalized across four dimensions of the NLP moderation pipeline: linguistic surface modeling, cultural-norm encoding, annotation epistemology, and computational adaptation. Our analysis reveals a pronounced structural imbalance. Across a coded subset of representative studies (n = 20), all focused on linguistic surface modeling and computational adaptation, while only a small minority addressed annotation epistemology, and none explicitly operationalized culturally grounded norm systems as a dedicated modeling layer. These dimensions are not mutually exclusive. Across datasets and benchmarks, recurring limitations include overreliance on explicit lexical toxicity, Western-centric resource concentration, limited robustness under domain shift, and the absence of misogyny-specific resources for Dari and Pashto. We argue that these limitations are systemic rather than purely architectural. Framing misogyny detection as a sociotechnical moderation pipeline, we introduce the Culturally Grounded Misogyny Detection Framework (CG-MDF) and outline design principles for culturally grounded dataset development, evaluation, and human-in-the-loop moderation, with particular emphasis on establishing a research foundation for Afghan languages.

items.title: The Politics of Language. By David Beaver and Jason Stanley. [REVIEW]
Who Cares if Normative Realism is True?
items.abstract: Williamson’s Good as Usual argues that normative discourse is, epistemologically and metaphysically, unremarkable. In it, “we often express mind-independent truths, many of which we know” (4). In these comments, I argue that even if Williamson is right, his realism – like factualism (i.e. cognitivism) in general – is practically anemic. Knowledge of what we ought to do, factually construed, is not sufficient, and may not even be necessary, for setting what to do.

items.title: The Entropy Standard: The Biosphere Fluid, Time Ledgers, and the Physical Limits of Civilization.
items.abstract: Grounded in a hard-core perspective at the intersection of thermodynamics and information theory, this paper strips away the symbolic illusions of traditional political economy, redefining human society as an active, viscoelastic "colloidal fluid" dissipative structure driven by external energy throughput and the fundamental "time ledgers" of carbon-based individuals. Moving beyond monetary and financial fictions, the framework establishes the Dual Constraint Equations of Civilizational Survival: The Upper Limit Constraint Equation, which maps the physiological and physical time limits imposed on carbon-based components by the combined demands of innovative labor, unmechanized repetitive labor, and exponential administrative/game-theoretic complexity overhead ; and The Lower Limit Maintenance Equation, which dictates the non-negotiable minimum energy baseline required to prevent system disintegration. Using this apparatus, the work diagnoses two terminal pathologies plaguing modern advanced societies: Mechanization Blockade Disease (where stalled technological evolution forces human flesh to brute-force unmechanized repetitive labor, triggering population cliffs) and Complexity Parasitism (where skyrocketing administrative and defensive friction devours society's scarce innovative brainpower). The classical scholar Gu Yanwu once distinguished between the "fall of a state" (wangguo) and the "collapse of all-under-heaven" (wang tianxia)—the former representing the mere succession of ruling algorithms, and the latter the disintegration of a civilization's high-order negative entropy system. Examining the present, the global sphere is deeply mired in the quagmire of AI algorithm bubbles and capital centralization; from Asia, Africa, and Latin America to Europe and the Americas, state will is reasserting comprehensive control over physical resources. History and the laws of physics indicate that even though technological bubbles will ultimately burst, and even though centralized control will cause internal friction and complexity overhead to expand exponentially, we must still hope that this represents merely a transient system damping in the long river of history. For the Second Law of Thermodynamics has long delivered its ultimate verdict: without free physical sampling and distributed trial-and-error, human civilization will inevitably descend into absolute information dead silence. This theory may well transcend its era. Humanity remains trapped in the …

items.title: Measuring the Grammar of a Mind: A Pre-Registered, Single-Subject Study of Epistemic Structure in Longitudinal Human–AI Interaction.
items.abstract: Proactive AI assistance depends on one input above all others: an accurate predictive model of the individual user. The field's own ablation studies show this, and its benchmarks concede that such models are currently trained on synthetic users, because no suitable longitudinal record of a real person exists in the research commons. The extended mind thesis faces a parallel gap. Decades of experimental work show that cognition can extend into external processes, yet no study has measured the persistent structure of one real, long-lived human and tool coupling. This paper supplies both missing objects from a single source: the author's complete conversational record with AI assistants, comprising 13,682 timestamped user turns across three and a half years, together with versioned self-consolidation documents and essays. Two findings result: a confirmed structural measurement, and a security discovery that follows from it. Study 1 establishes that this conduct decomposes into a thirteen-move taxonomy of recurring epistemic moves whose sequences carry structure far beyond chance (permutation z ≈ 188), a signal that survives removal of self-transitions and replicates on 255 subsequently recovered conversations (transition-structure correlation r = 0.985), with an effect size of Cramér's V ≈ 0.17. Study 2 imposed a fully pre-registered confirmatory protocol: dual labeling of every turn on a workflow facet and a reasoning facet, criteria and thresholds frozen before labeling, a human verification gate whose measured reliability (58% subject agreement) is reported with the results, and a sealed 20% hold-out used exactly once. Two registered predictions from the development split, a reasoning rate of 39.3% and a workflow-to-reasoning mutual-information lift of 0.137, were confirmed on the sealed hold-out at 40.7% and 0.157 respectively, with both directional couplings significant out-of-sample at p < 10⁻²⁰. This is, to the author's knowledge, the first pre-registered prediction about the structure of one's own mind confirmed on sealed data. The second finding is a security discovery, developed in its own section: the measured individual baseline that enables anticipation also enables impostor detection. Commercial behavioral-security tools construct baselines from aggregate data across fleets of users, which is precisely why an attacker operating inside stolen credentials can pass by behaving like a plausible generic user. An individual baseline detects what the …

items.title: Solidarity or Segregation? ChatGPT Health and US Health Care Disparities.
items.abstract: ChatGPT Health, an artificial intelligence feature launched by OpenAI in January 2026, integrates personal medical records and consumer health data into a large language model–based chatbot. It positions itself as a digital health tool to help users navigate a fragmented US health care system marked by inaccessible insurance, medical deserts, and workforce shortages. We argue that, rather than closing these gaps, ChatGPT Health risks widening what we call the solidarity gap in health care.
