By appearing to address unmet needs, it may obscure and entrench the structural conditions that produce health care disparities. We identify specific risks to patient safety, such as the legitimization of dangerous self-rationing and self-medication behaviors, inaccurate triage of clinical emergencies, erosion of effective health communication, and the reinforcement of confirmation and anchoring bias. These risks are particularly acute for individuals facing structural barriers to care. To prevent ChatGPT Health and similar large language model–based health tools from deepening inequities, we propose solidarity-based policy interventions such as upstream reforms that rebuild the institutional foundations of access and health equity and downstream safeguards that embed artificial intelligence tools within accountable, equitable health care infrastructures as complements to rather than substitutes for human care.

items.title: Human Being vs AI - An Analysis of Cognition, Knowledge and Consciousness.
items.abstract: This article is an overview of my book, "Māyā” - The Consciousness Causal Model of Psychological Experience. -/- It is an analysis of the difference between cognition, knowledge, and consciousness. How does a human being become cognizant, how does he know, and how does he become conscious? Can an AI achieve consciousness? What is the missing entity?

items.title: The Death of the Mosaic God and the Birth of the Scientific-Cosmological God.
items.abstract: Introduction: The Death of the Mosaic God and the Birth of the Old-New God Friedrich Nietzsche's historical declaration regarding the death of God—"God is dead. God remains dead. And we have killed him. How shall we comfort ourselves, the murderers of all murderers? What was holiest and mightiest of all that the world has yet owned has bled to death under our knives: who will wipe this blood off us? What water is there for us to cleanse ourselves? What festivals of atonement, what sacred games shall we have to invent?" (The Gay Science, Section 125, 1882; see also: Thus Spoke Zarathustra, 1883)—signified the decline of traditional religious hegemony and the rise of man as the center. However, approximately 150 years after this proclamation, following the death of religious hegemony and the rise of secularism and man as the center, a new God is born. This is an old-new God: a God proven precisely by science itself, which discovers that a non-fully explained lawfulness exists within the structure of the cosmos. This revolutionary conception does not reject the roots; rather, it relies and depends entirely upon the original sources, while expanding them into the new scientific, mathematical, and cosmological language.

items.title: מותו של האל המשהי ולידתו של האל המדעי קוסמי.
items.abstract: מבוא: מותו של האל המשהי ולידתו של האל החדש-ישן ההכרזה ההיסטורית של פרידריך ניטשה על מותו של האל – "אלוהים מת. אלוהים נשאר מת. ואנחנו הרגנו אותו... אילו מים ישנם כדי לטהר אותנו? אילו חגי כפרה, אילו משחקים מקודשים נצטרך להמציא?" (המדע העליז, סעיף 125, 1882; ראו גם: כה אמר זרתוסטרא, 1883) – סימנה את שקיעתה של ההגמוניה הדתית המסורתית ואת עלייתו של האדם כמרכז. ואולם, כ-150 שנה לאחר הכרזה זו, בעקבות מותה של ההגמוניה הדתית ועלייתה של החילוניות והאדם כמרכז, נולד אל חדש. זהו אל חדש-ישן: אל נוכח דווקא על ידי המדע עצמו, המוצא שיש חוקיות שאינה לגמרי מוסברת במבנה הקוסמוס. תפיסה מהפכנית זו אינה דוחה את השורשים, אלא נשענת ומסתמכת לגמרי על המקורות, תוך שהיא מרחיבה אותם לשפה המדעית, המתמטית והקוסמולוגית החדשה.

items.title: Ontological Divergence through Semantic Erosion: Wicker Park as a Laboratory for Testing and Extending the Ontology of Finite Continuity.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the narrative structure of Paul McGuigan's Wicker Park (2004)—characterized by non-linear temporality, chain misrecognitions, and temporal reconstructions—reveals the conditions of possibility for observing processes of semantic erosion and ontological divergence, and through this revelation enables the refinement and extension of the Ontology of Finite Continuity. Rather than treating the film as an illustration of a pre-existing philosophical theory, I position it as a conceptual laboratory that makes visible three phenomena: ontological divergence through semantic erosion, homeorhesis as the pattern of continuity under erosive conditions, and structural reconstruction of meaning as an active ontological process. The analysis introduces the concept of ontological divergence through semantic erosion to explain how fragmented communication progressively generates alternative ontological worlds for each character without requiring substantial alteration in external events. Small disruptions in communicative chains accumulate across time, activating three types of hermeneutic failure simultaneously—structural, institutional, and paradigmatic—and producing hermeneutic friction as their nonlinear emergent product. The paper further demonstrates that the film exemplifies homeorhetic continuity rather than homeostatic return: characters do not recover prior equilibrium but maintain their developmental trajectory under erosive conditions. Through integrating film-philosophy with contemporary ontology, this study contributes to philosophical film studies and ontological theory by proposing a new conceptual model of ontological divergence, demonstrating how cinema can function as a laboratory for testing and extending ontological frameworks, and offering a methodological bridge between phenomenological description and ontological inference. -/- Keywords: Ontological Divergence, Semantic Erosion, Homeorhesis, Hermeneutic Friction, Finite Continuity, Film-Philosophy, Wicker Park.

items.title: Continuity Without a Carrier: Dynamic Production and the Difference Between Continuation and Restart.
items.abstract: What makes a person persist through radical change? Relational Lineage Theory (RLT) shifts the question from retained endpoint properties to transition architecture. It distinguishes ContinuesInto, a directed and branchable relation of concrete token succession, from SamePerson, an equivalence relation defined over nonbranching and nonfusing regions of a succession graph. The distinctive claim is not merely that causal history matters. Local succession requires both DynamicProduction—the source remains an open, intervention-sensitive producer of the successor’s operative trajectory—and GovernanceInheritance—the successor acquires write authority, conflict resolution, error targets, and boundary regulation through the source’s live governance handoff. Detached reconstruction fails because a fixed representation and external initializer begin a separately governed token. Capture closure accordingly diagnoses restart rather than adding a third continuation condition. This two-level architecture explains how continuation can branch while numerical identity remains reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. The Restart Asymmetry Argument applies the account to gradual replacement, duplication, fission, live migration, and checkpoint restoration, and distinguishes RLT from psychological, biological, and undifferentiated causal-continuity theories.

items.title: Inference-Behaviour Semantics for All* Connectives in Two-Dimensional Sequent Calculi.
items.abstract: Inference-behaviour semantics (I-bS) is a new approach to proof-theoretic semantics, grounded in two inferentialist principles: (1) the use of an expression in reasoning determines its meaning, and (2) a connective is defined by its operational rules. I-bS operationalises these ideas by measuring the syntactic use of a connective in the proof of its definability, against a substructurally minimal derivability relation. I-bS thereby gives the meaning of a connective in terms of its semantic clause, i.e. minimal substructural rule pair. -/- This paper validates and verifies I-bS by applying it to all 10,816 connective rule pairs that can be formulated in two-dimensional sequent calculi using at most two premiss sequents and at most two active formulae. As a result, we find semantic clauses for exactly 21 meaningful connectives, namely bottom, top, two negations (intuitionistic and dual-intuitionistic), group and lattice conjunction, disjunction and implication, as well as their converses and inverses. -/- We use these results to precisely map the semantic interrelations among the connectives, across linear, classical, intuitionistic, dual-intuitionistic, minimal, and lattice logic. Most notably, we find that intuitionistic negation, disjunction and implication each capture half of the meaning of their classical counterparts.

items.title: The Calculus of Modal Coincidence - The Grammar of A-Metaphysical Ontology.
items.abstract: What this article is (note added 13 September 2026). This is the formal statement of the doctrine of modal coincidence as it stood in July 2026, deposited to fix its priority, and it is kept as that dated record. It is not updated. The developed ontology is Ethical Ontology, Volume I: The Modal Coincidence (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22723038), where the categories are reached by regional trial rather than stated in a grammar; the derivation of the doctrine from a substitution trial is The Three Differences and the Sense of Being (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21967186). Where this article and Volume I differ, Volume I governs. -/- This article proposes modal coincidence as the founding grammar of an a-metaphysical ontology. The more familiar description non-metaphysical correctly names what the project refuses: ontology need not secure what obtains through a bearer, substrate, essence, first principle, or concealed order standing beneath or beyond its obtaining. The term a-metaphysical states the stronger claim. The ontology is not constituted by opposition to metaphysics and does not depend upon metaphysics as the condition of its validity. It determines what obtains through the manner in which it obtains as this. The project occupies three distinct coordinates. It is genealogically post-metaphysical: its historical emergence presupposes the metaphysical tradition and its phenomenological, hermeneutic, and anarchic critiques. It is structurally pre-metaphysical: it articulates the obtaining prior to the metaphysical decision to duplicate it through a bearer or ground. It is ontologically a-metaphysical: its categories neither require metaphysics nor depend upon the negation of metaphysics. Metaphysics is a condition of the theory's discovery, not a condition of its truth. The category who provides the first decisive demonstration. A who is not a substance, organism, psychological profile, narrative bundle, public identity, or further fact behind a life. A who is the whole regional obtaining in which a regionally articulable manner obtains as this concrete occurrence. The determination is earned aletically before it is stated formally: from the transparency of ordinary who-directed access, through a substitution trial showing that preservation of every transferable structure — function, memory, narrative, qualitative profile, recognition — does not restore the same who, to the full hermeneutic concession and the residue it cannot absorb. The article then gives the claim a …

items.title: Personal and irreplaceable value: A phenomenological approach.
items.abstract: If irreplaceable value exists, then what is it and what is its source? I argue that we talk about irreplaceable value conditionally, as a historical value, and unconditionally, as a personal value. The latter is the condition for the former. If so, it is not the case that a kind of circumstantial uniqueness (unreinstantiable uniqueness) confers irreplaceable value, but that persons do, provided that irreplaceable value is a value persons possess. I defend this by offering a Schelerian argument for personal value over a Kantian one, namely, the value of personal individuality. I identify the seat and center of personal irreplaceability to be a nonrepresentational, individual value orientation, evidence for which is presented within a first-personal context of loving intimacy. Personal irreplaceability is the condition for the significance of individual characteristics and for the irreplaceable value of relevant unreinstantiable objects.

items.title: THE FORMAL THEORY OF BEAUTY: The Perceptible Form of Freedom, the Cage and the Key, and the Aesthetics of the Holoviceotic Era.
items.abstract: “The beautiful is what Freedom looks like when it becomes visible; the ugly is what the cage looks like when it learns to imitate a window.” — Philosophy of Virtues, Mattos, J.C. de -/- ABSTRACT Philosophy has produced extensive accounts of beauty: as harmony and proportion (the Pythagorean–Scholastic tradition), as the sensible appearance of the Idea (Plato, Hegel), as disinterested free play of the faculties (Kant), as the promise of happiness (Stendhal), as significant form (Bell), as the sensuous shining of truth (Heidegger, Adorno), and as an evolved fitness signal (evolutionary aesthetics). None of these accounts derives beauty from a formal virtue architecture with an explicit inversion rule, none distinguishes beauty from its structural counterfeit at the level of what the work does to the perceiver rather than what it depicts, and none explains why the counterfeit should dominate an entire era of production. This paper presents the first derivation of beauty from the Ontological Virtue Formula V = F + D of the Philosophy of Virtues programme. The central formal claim is that beauty is the perceptible form of Freedom: B = Φ(F), where Φ is the operator that renders Freedom sensible in image, sound, structure, and word. Eight formal results follow. (T1) Beauty is the perceptible form of Freedom; its inversion under the Inversion Theorem Φ(F) − F is Anti-art — the form of beauty occupied by the power that emptied it. (T2) The Two-Factor Theorem: the height of a work is the product of the Freedom it embodies and the Freedom it transmits; neither factor alone suffices. (T3) The Cage/Key Theorem: every work is classified by its net effect on the perceiver’s Freedom, dF/dt — Cage-art closes the perceiver within determinism (dF/dt < 0), Key-art hands the perceiver the instrument of exit (dF/dt > 0). (T4) The Depiction–Transmission Distinction: depicting un-freedom is not transmitting it; the literature of the cage is Key-art, and this resolves the tragedy objection. (T5) The Canon Theorem: works order by embodied × transmitted Freedom, and endurance is the signature of sustained transmission across time. (T6) The Holoviceotic Aesthetics Theorem: the Cage dominates the literature of the Holoviceotic era because Anti-art is the aesthetic arm of Devirtualisation — it trains the Freedophobic sensibility. (T7) The sublime is Freedom perceived at the Dissolution Threshold. (T8) The Transcendentals Theorem: Beauty, Truth, and the Good are the perceptible, …

items.title: Informational Experiential Realism: Experience as a Continuing Physical Operation.
items.abstract: What makes interacting physical processes one experiencing subject, and what allows that subject to persist as its activities and constituents change? Informational Experiential Realism (IER) proposes that one qualifying physical operation is both a total experience and its subject. This paper develops the proposal by separating physical unity, constitutive membership, and continuity before considering experiential identity. -/- The physical account proceeds from available continuation to unity, ownership, membership, and persistence. Unity requires that the candidate's alternatives resist independent recombination across every division in a physically justified partition family. Ownership asks whether the joint restriction is borne and resolved within the candidate. Membership distinguishes processes that participate in that resolution from those that merely influence or sustain it. Persistence requires produced continuation that inherits irreversible consequences and remains unique in both directions. The full criteria permit turnover and content change while ruling out continuation through a failed link, branching, or merger. -/- IER identifies the qualifying operation with experience and its subject; qualitative differences are proposed to be differences within that operation. The identification is defended as an explanatory hypothesis, not a deduction from physicalism. Strawson's identity theory and cybernetic and process approaches supply substantial precedents. The contribution is an explicit framework and its conditional consequences. Whether a physical system meets the criteria, whether it is experiential, which organizations correspond to particular qualities, and whether identity is preferable to constitution or realization remain open.

items.title: Constraint, Closure, and the Missing Subject: A Comparative Review of Recent Structural Theories of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Several recent theories of consciousness describe experience through combinations of constraint, closure, admissibility, integration, persistence, temporal extension, identity maintenance, and subject individuation. Their shared vocabulary suggests a useful comparison, but it does not establish a school or a common ontology. This article therefore treats the works as a provisional comparison set. It asks whether they share an explanatory reorientation: before explaining particular conscious contents or their functional availability, explain what makes there be one bounded and persisting subject whose experience they are. The article distinguishes six claims often compressed into the language of a subject or bearer: attribution, phenomenal subjectivity, synchronic unity, ontological bearing, diachronic identity, and substantial subjecthood. It then compares identity-and-closure theories, persistence-and-admissibility theories, relational and temporal-structure theories, and consciousness-first structural ontologies. These approaches differ over whether structural organization is identical with experience and subject, constitutes a subject, realizes consciousness, supplies a diagnostic criterion, or organizes an already experiential basis. IER v10.11.6 supplies one sharpened comparator: a continuing token UEF operation is identical with total experience-as-process and the experiential subject, while substrate, capacity, regime, local contents, organism, and person remain distinct types. IER also permits independently qualifying UEFs at physically nested or overlapping scales without phenomenal aggregation. These commitments do not define the comparison set or establish the identity claim; they clarify which questions any subject theory must answer. The article concludes with standards for testing the proposed convergence through primary-text comparison, explicit inference, contrast cases, and failure conditions.

items.title: Context as Contraindication: Ethical Challenges of Psychedelics and Other Neuroplasticity-Enhancing Drugs.
items.abstract: Psychedelic-assisted therapies are widely described as context-dependent, shaped by “set and setting” and by patients’ broader “matrix” of living conditions. Yet, the field has rarely grappled with the potential ramifications of this context-dependency, including whether an individual’s adverse social circumstances might not only blunt benefits but also amplify harms. This article develops a context-dependent harm hypothesis by analogy to conventional serotonergic antidepressants, for which pre-clinical and clinical evidence supports potential amplification of the harms of detrimental environmental and social contexts. A similar risk is plausible for psychedelics, given that both conventional antidepressants and psychedelic drugs may boost neuroplasticity and environmental sensitivity. This article reviews the limitations of the current psychedelic evidence base that precludes the evaluation of this hypothesis, including the frequent enrollment of socioeconomically advantaged participants and inadequate reporting of social circumstances. It concludes that environment-drug interactions require further attention for scientific, ethical, and clinical purposes. If context-dependent harm exists, adverse living conditions may constitute temporary contraindications until social conditions support positive therapeutic outcomes.

items.title: Evolucionismo universal. Volumen 9: Historia de la naturaleza y teoría general de la evolución. La crisis de la teoría sintética de la evolución.
items.abstract: Este volumen examina la crisis de la teoría sintética. Analiza las críticas acumuladas desde el siglo XX. Cuestiona el enfoque genocéntrico y reduccionista actual. Señala la desaparición del organismo en la biología. Estudia la brecha entre microevolución y macroevolución. Evalúa las limitaciones de la genética poblacional. Propone integrar aportes de la genética molecular moderna. El estudio impulsa la creación de nuevos paradigmas.

items.title: Evolucionismo universal. Volumen 8: Historia de la naturaleza y desarrollo de la visión científica del mundo. Teoría sintética de la evolución es el título completo del libro presentado en el documento.
items.abstract: Este texto analiza a fondo la teoría sintética de la evolución. Explica la integración de la selección natural con la genética de poblaciones. La obra expone los postulados fundamentales de este sistema biológico. Define a la población como la unidad evolutiva elemental. Señala al proceso mutacional como fuente de innovaciones. Describe los mecanismos de aislamiento reproductivo y geográfico. También cuestiona el enfoque genocéntrico de la teoría tradicional. Evalúa el papel de las modificaciones adaptativas fenotípicas. Resalta la importancia del entrenamiento de los órganos en la naturaleza. Finalmente, analiza la influencia del trabajo biológico sobre los genes.

items.title: Evolucionismo universal. Volumen 1: Historia de la naturaleza y desarrollo de la visión científica del mundo hacia una teoría general de la evolución.
items.abstract: Este primer volumen de la obra del filósofo de la historia y científico evolucionista Lev Krivitsky ofrece una síntesis sistémica y ontológica del conocimiento de las ciencias naturales contemporáneas (como la física, química, astronomía, cosmología, geología, biología y antropología histórica) con el fin de fundamentar las bases de una Teoría General de la Evolución (TGE). El libro actúa como una enciclopedia y manual detallado que traza la historia cronológica del ser, abarcando desde la formación de la Metagalaxia y los límites del macrocosmos hasta el origen y desarrollo del ser humano moderno a partir del reino animal.El núcleo teórico y metodológico de la investigación introduce el denominado „enfoque movilizador-evolutivo“. Según este concepto, los procesos de evolución progresiva en todos los niveles de la existencia (materia inerte, biósfera, sociedad y cultura) son impulsados por „estructuras de movilización“ específicas. Dichas entidades absorben recursos del entorno y realizan un „trabajo evolutivo“ ordenado frente al caos circundante. El texto supera tanto el reduccionismo genocéntrico y mutacionista como el creacionismo tradicional, planteando las bases de la „evolutística“ y defendiendo una fe científico-humanista que movilice al ser humano hacia el perfeccionamiento psicofísico continuo y la preservación de la civilización.

items.title: When the World Stops Supplying Error: The Efficiency Paradox in Recursively Integrated Architectures.
items.abstract: A cognitive system that has extracted what its environment and its own representations can yield about a task does not fall quiet. Persistence needs no new explanation: the nonequilibrium steady-state formulation of the free energy principle already guarantees it. What remains open is what persistent activity is about once externally grounded gradients are exhausted. In recursively integrated architectures, optimization is then redirected onto distinctions the system itself generates. Coherence-maintenance load scales with integration rather than with error, precision reallocation converts it into gradient, and the product is relational overfitting: internal coherence rises while referential traction falls. This divergence between local efficiency and global epistemic yield is the Efficiency Paradox. It is the negative counterpart of learning by thinking, from which the accuracy plateau separates it. Reasoning models computing past their first correct answer and formally impeccable confabulations exhibit the signature. A lemma explains why the divergence is not corrected from within: a system can compute the value that satisfies a criterion, but not that this is the criterion, so every correction, from sleep to model reduction to reasoning budgets, applies a standard the optimization did not set. Three predictions follow; the two that discriminate can be run on existing systems.

items.title: Jays and Photons - A Hypothetical Consideration of the Presence of Light.
items.abstract: This is a small question, asked inside my Coherent Existence framework: What is light to the Jays, the moments of experience a life is made of? Does light carry a Trace between perspectives, or is it one itself? My functional writes each perspective as an intensity and a facing, a size that holds and a phase that turns, and classical optics writes a light field the same way. Three plain facts of physics rhyme with what the framework says. The absolute phase of a single field cannot be observed, while the relative phase between two fields is physical and does the work of interference. A resonant cavity keeps only the modes that come back into agreement with themselves. And the living body gives off an ultraweak light that is measured, real, and metabolic. I set out three readings of that rhyme and weigh them. The humble reading takes light as a channel between perspectives and asks almost nothing physics has not granted. The heavy reading says the Jays are light, and I decline it: it inherits the decoherence objection, which the replies from quantum theories of mind have not settled, and biophoton coherence is unproven. The third reading, the one I defend, sits between them. At human scale the senses register almost everything by way of the electromagnetic field and carry it to the nerve by that field, and the body doing the collecting is held together, atom to atom, by the same field. So “light observing light” is earned as a statement about the physics of perception, taking light to mean the field it is a ripple in, with no claim that consciousness is light. The series’ proposed thesis, one consciousness of which every mind is a perspective, is named and kept apart from it. I keep the seam between physics and my reading visible, and I end with what survives it: a resemblance, offered as a rhyme and not a proof.

items.title: Comparisons: An Individual Perspective on Objectivity, Subjectivity, and Relativity.
items.abstract: A philosophical essay that recovers the old sense of comparison, Paul’s synkrinō, “to judge together,” and uses it to hold three words in one gaze: objective, subjective, and relative. The etymology of the first two has inverted within recorded memory (the scholastic esse obiectivum and esse subiectivum), which the essay reads as a hinge rather than a wall. Physics supplies the relational ground: measurement as interaction, Rovelli’s relational quantum mechanics, quark confinement, and a proton whose mass comes almost entirely from binding rather than from its parts. Buber’s I that differs with every meeting and Paul’s mirror texts carry the theme into persons, and the near-field evidence for emotional contagion grounds a claim the author marks as his own: calm is contagious in the direction of one’s Intent. The triad is then tried on science (objective), philosophy (subjective), and mathematics (relative, as structuralism describes it), and the essay closes by turning toward psychology as the study of the subject, who never stands under anything alone.

items.title: The Ledger Breaks First: Testing the Reform Acceleration, Dam, and Generative Paradoxes Against 2026, and Why the Welfare State's Books — Not the Dam's Own Metaphor — Are Where the Mortality Symmetry Assumption Is Already Measured to Fail.
items.abstract: Three of this corpus's five founding paradoxes have not yet been run against 2026's empirical record the way the Governance Paradox was tested in The Sovereign's Death Warrant and One Level Down, and the ARSI–Longevity Resonance Paradox was tested in The Speed That Costs A Demos. This paper closes that set, and — unlike its first draft — closes it by explicitly reconnecting to the two paradoxes already tested rather than treating them as a separate ledger. It runs the Reform Acceleration Paradox against Bryan Johnson's Immortals program, a live, dated, staged rollout of exactly the visible-partial-access structure Tocqueville's mechanism predicts will inflame rather than defuse political grievance. It runs the Dam Paradox against a target more concrete than the paradox's own metaphor: the welfare state's actuarial books, where the assumption this paper names the Mortality Symmetry Assumption is not a philosophical premise but a load-bearing engineering input, current in the United States' Social Security Trustees Reports, in a decades-deep academic literature on differential mortality and program progressivity, in an unresolved health-economics dispute over whether extended life compresses or expands the costly years preceding death, and in a multi-billion-dollar global market that already exists to price the risk that people live longer than a table assumed. This paper distinguishes a Hard Dam, the corpus's original mortality-and-turnover mechanism, from a Soft Dam it names for the first time: the decline in cognitive and physical competitiveness that ordinarily erodes an incumbent's advantage years before death, which real, currently funded AI-driven healthspan programs are already targeting by name. It runs the Generative Paradox a third time, not as another hub case study but as the mechanism connecting the other two, concretely, down to the composition of the government body that produces Section III's own numbers. It then reopens the Closing Triangle to show it is not a triangle at all but the same structure the Governance Paradox and the ARSI–Longevity Resonance Paradox already describe, viewed from three further institutional vantage points — meaning this paper's true contribution is showing all five of the corpus's paradoxes are one mechanism, not five. It closes, honestly, with a genuine complication from political science that cuts against a simpler version of its own argument, and with what remains unresolved. This paper adds one further …

items.title: Appraisive Things.
items.pub: Journal of the American Philosophical Association.
items.venue: Journal of the American Philosophical Association
items.abstract: Philosophical literature on praise primarily focuses on verbal expressions of praise. But material expressions of praise are a pervasive feature of our social practices: we use cash prizes, bonuses, statues, trophies to celebrate and esteem others and their good deeds. What is the normative significance of using things to praise, when using (mere) words is an alternative? Beyond the instrumental and symbolic significance, we draw on recent literature on world-shaping and mind-shaping to explain what can be achieved by appraisive things. We point to, and illustrate, two normatively important properties that are brought to the fore by material praise: the finitude and durability of things. In light of these previously neglected dimensions of our appraisive practices, we revisit norms of positive appraisal, showing the need for a multidimensional account of apt praise.

items.title: Orphaned Patterns.
items.abstract: This working paper presents a falsification-disciplined search program derived from resonance monism, a monist framework whose single axiom posits a non-spatial, non-temporal ground to which perception is intrinsic (Working Paper No. 1). The program searches the accumulated knowledge of several disciplines for orphaned patterns: well-documented regularities that lack a satisfying explanation and become readable under the premise. The premise functions strictly as a search image, not as evidence; a candidate is admitted only if the premise performs work a rival account does not — resolving an acknowledged riddle, licensing a testable prediction, or unifying previously unconnected findings. Mere compatibility is explicitly insufficient, and the strongest rival explanation is carried along in every case. Five candidates are examined: Wigner's unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics; the non-quantizability of gravity and space; the entanglement–space–gravity triad; matter and energy as states of space (the Clifford–Kelvin–Einstein–Wheeler lineage, including a possible pass through the fermion obstacle via non-smooth spatial structure); and the blind spot of introspection. One candidate — synchronicity — is examined and rejected, with the grounds for rejection kept on record. One open research trail is marked: a Gödel-type impossibility structure behind the quantization of space. All results are coherence gains under an accepted axiom, not proofs; falsification routes are stated throughout.

items.title: The Iterated Social Construction of Words.
items.abstract: When is a mark or sound a token of a word? There is no once-and-for-all answer: word tokening is iteratively socially constructed, so the conditions for tokening a word can shift across socio-technical regimes. I first argue that word-tokening’s messy boundaries have a distinctive temporal structure I call initiated: initiation is relatively demanding, maintenance more permissive, exit difficult. Word-token kinds are initiated proxy kinds: anchored as stable, low-cost proxies that play a functional role, as is common for social kinds. I then historicize the picture. Tokening conditions shift as pressures accumulate through large-scale changes to roles, constraints, and costs within a regime; I consider historical and current regimes, and the implications of AI-generated text. But they change conservatively—sedimented and path-dependent rather than anchored from scratch. The aim is a pragmatic but stable theory of word-tokening, and a broader model of how social kinds are built over time.

items.title: Mineness and the Address - Position, privacy, and the communication of experience.
items.abstract: Descriptions of experience do not deliver the experience — and, this paper argues, the non‑delivery was never the interesting fact. That tokens of experience cannot travel between subjects follows already from their bare particularity: events do not recur or transfer, for anyone. What bare particularity cannot explain is the first‑person asymmetry — why this token, now, is open to me and closed to you at once; why experience is had rather than merely instantiated, in the ownership sense of having. The paper’s contribution is an analysis of that mineness. A token experience is an event‑as‑read: constituted by the position through which it occurs — the concrete standing state, the priors and formation history and accumulated weighting through which the event passes. Positions are individuated as particulars, and the choice is made openly: a position is a subject‑stage considered as the condition of reading — one thing under two descriptions — so a qualitatively perfect duplicate occupies a numerically distinct position and is thereby a second subject. Mineness is the token’s occurring‑as‑read‑through‑this‑position, a relation that holds for exactly one system; that is the asymmetry, explained. The claim is located in the contemporary taxonomy of subjective character as an account of ownership, deliberately neutral on phenomenal for‑me‑ness, and the standard pressure case — thought insertion — is answered through the dissociation of ownership from agency, a joint the account already contains. The analysis generalizes, and the generalization is paid on the page: closure between minds is one instance of closure between positions; every subject also stands on the far side of their own past, and other minds are the special, synchronic case. On communication, the paper defends an addressing model: descriptions carry coordinates, not payloads, and the receiver constructs from local stock — yielding a three‑zone map of experiential communication, indexed to a receiver at a time. The craniopagus case is engaged with declared neutrality between the causal‑coupling and partial‑unity readings; the clinical career of pain measurement is read as the addressing model in practice; Scarry’s thesis is recast as production‑side failure; the acknowledgment complaint is absorbed as an ethics of construction‑debt. The account is conceptual analysis and says so. The existence question — why there is anyone home at all, and whether the having is also felt — is left exactly where …

items.title: A highly sympathetic, decidedly pluralistic, somewhat reactionary, and slightly skeptical comment on Tekin’s Reclaiming the Self in Psychiatry.
items.abstract: This paper is a contribution to a book symposium on Tekin’s Reclaiming the Self in Psychiatry. While largely sympathetic to Tekin’s critique of the medical model in mental health care, I contend that a more pluralistic perspective on mental health care supports a more sympathetic assessment of the status quo.

items.title: Philosophy and the Evolution of Virtue and Vice.
items.abstract: This volume explores what evolutionary theory can contribute to our philosophical understanding of virtue and vice. -/- The last twenty years have seen an uptick in philosophical discussions of the biological and cultural evolution of morality. Yet, there has been surprisingly little discussion of virtue ethics and the evolution of human character, even though human virtues are almost certainly one of the markers of our species’ distinctive sociality. This volume investigates the evolution of human character traits and its implications for moral philosophy and value theory. The chapters address central questions such as: To what extent can evolutionary theories explain virtue, vice, or specific virtues/vices? Are philosophical accounts of virtue compatible with evolutionary explanations? How might tensions between them be resolved? What implications might the evolution of virtue have concerning debates in value theory more broadly? What implications does the evolution of virtue have for living well in the digital age? And how can we re-engineer the conceptual machinery of virtue/vice to our advantage? The volume serves as a first step toward evaluating the influence of evolution on human conceptions of what kind of people we ought to be. -/- Philosophy and the Evolution of Virtue and Vice will appeal to researchers and graduate students working in normative ethics, virtue ethics, metaethics, moral psychology, philosophy of social science, philosophy of biology, and evolutionary theory.

items.title: New Work for an Old Theory of Action.
items.abstract: In this paper I defend the ancient thesis that agents always act under the guise of the good. I do so by arguing that the role that goodness plays in action is isomorphic to the role that truth plays in belief. In particular, I argue that the guise of the good thesis allows us to: (i) fix the topic of ethical and metaethical disagreement just as the aim of belief allows us to fix the topic of alethiological disagreements, (ii) explain the thinness of thin moral concepts in parallel to the thinness of concepts like truth, (iii) develop an account of moral testimony that parallels the best non-reductive accounts of theoretical testimony, and (iv) explains why we are open to our values changing over time in much the same way that we are open to our theoretical premises changing over time.

items.title: The Body: The First Home of Survival: Rethinking Psychological Suffering Through Survival Rules, Neural Judgments, and Observer Awareness.
items.abstract: The body constitutes the primary foundation of human life, and the nervous system evolved fundamentally to preserve and protect it. From the earliest stages of development, the brain continuously interacts with the environment, caregivers, and lived experiences, gradually constructing patterns whose primary function is to increase the probability of survival. -/- This paper proposes a conceptual framework suggesting that, beyond processing experience, the brain develops a set of Survival Rules. These rules become activated in different situations as Neural Judgments, shaping perception, emotion, decision-making, and behavior. -/- Within this framework, many forms of psychological suffering are understood not merely as consequences of external events but as the result of conflicts among Neural Judgments. Each judgment may once have served an adaptive survival function, yet under changing life circumstances these judgments can become incompatible with one another. Consequently, the brain functions as a dynamic system that continuously generates, revises, and replaces judgments, a process that may underlie anxiety, guilt, indecision, dissatisfaction, and persistent inner conflict. -/- The paper further argues that Observer Awareness, without suppressing the brain's natural activity, can fundamentally transform the individual's relationship with these judgments. From this perspective, inner peace begins when awareness no longer identifies itself with the judgments produced by the brain but instead recognizes them as natural products of its survival-oriented processes.

items.title: Attention Fragmentation in Digital Learning Environments: Micro-Procrastination, Cognitive Load, and Deep Work Across Educational Levels.
items.pub: Journal of Research, Innovation, and Strategies for Education (Rise) 3 (4):1-16.
items.venue: Journal of Research, Innovation, and Strategies for Education (Rise)
items.abstract: Maintaining sustained attention has become increasingly challenging in digitally saturated learning environments, where frequent notifications and habitual task switching are normalized. Although digital distraction has been widely examined, limited research has focused on digital micro-procrastination—brief, repetitive digital interruptions—and its cognitive consequences across educational levels. This study examined the relationships among Digital Micro-Procrastination (DMP), Perceived Cognitive Load (PCL), and Deep Work (DW) among junior high school, senior high school, and college students. Using a quantitative descriptive-comparative design, survey data were collected from 45 students equally distributed across three academic levels. All measures demonstrated acceptable internal consistency following reliability refinement. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman’s rank-order correlation, and Kruskal–Wallis tests. Results revealed a significant positive association between digital micro-procrastination and perceived cognitive load, indicating that frequent short digital interruptions are linked to heightened mental strain and attention fragmentation. Significant cross-level differences were observed, with college students reporting the highest levels of digital micro-procrastination and cognitive load. Findings related to deep work suggest a more nuanced relationship, wherein sustained focus may coexist with elevated cognitive effort rather than reduced task demands. Overall, the study underscores the cognitive implications of everyday digital practices and highlights the need for instructional and self-regulatory strategies that mitigate attention fragmentation in contemporary educational contexts.

items.title: The Monstrosity of Jesus Christ: An Application of Jeffrey Jerome Cohen’s Seven Theses of What Makes a Monster.
items.abstract: This paper applies Jeffrey Jerome Cohen’s seven theses of monster theory to the figure of Jesus Christ and argues a doubled claim: Christ satisfies each thesis in full and, in the same motion, breaks it. Where Cohen’s theses read monsters as cultural constructs — symptoms of the societies that produce them — the present argument runs in the opposite direction, taking the theses as a description of what a monster is and claiming that Christ is that: the category crisis is located in him, not in the eye that beholds him. Working through the incarnation, crucifixion and resurrection alongside Chalcedonian christology, the paper distinguishes the trinitarian rupture of the cross from the stability of the hypostatic union, and argues that the risen Christ’s retained wounds make categorial rupture a permanent feature of his body rather than a resolved interval. The claim throughout is taxonomic rather than metaphorical: Christ is not like a monster; he is one, and the breaking of each thesis against him discloses what he is. The introduction and conclusion are written in an informal register reminiscent of gothic horror — a framing device suited to a paper whose subject is the monstrous.

items.title: Referential Indeterminacy and De Re Thoughts.
items.abstract: Referential indeterminacy may seem to leave little room for de re or singular thoughts about ordinary objects. I argue that this impression is misleading. We can direct our thoughts at particular objects, even though there is no fact of the matter as to which objects are referred to by the singular terms purporting to stand for them. By distinguishing between weak and strong de re attitudes, I show that speakers can retain a weak form of de re belief despite the absence of determinate reference. I extend the same distinction to knowledge of reference, thereby explaining how linguistic understanding survives the indeterminacy of reference. I also briefly explore some broader implications of this picture for the theory of reference and for the status of genuine singular terms.

items.title: The Variance Preservation Premium: Why Independent Sources of Novelty Can Increase Resilience Under Model Uncertainty.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Post-V16 Independent Publications.
items.abstract: Under model uncertainty, systems may attempt to reduce variation by standardizing information sources, cognitive architectures, institutions, or problem-solving methods. Homogenization can lower coordination costs and improve short-horizon efficiency, but it can also eliminate independent sources of observation, hypothesis generation, criticism, and error correction whose future value is not visible from the current model. -/- This paper develops a conditional decision-theoretic account of the variance preservation premium: the expected net advantage of retaining differently structured and epistemically non-redundant sources relative to a more homogeneous alternative, after accounting for preservation, coordination, validation, security, manipulation, delay, and opportunity costs. It examines marginal information value, correlated-error reduction, novelty generation, robust choice under model uncertainty, dynamic option value, irreversible source loss, substitution uncertainty, complementary human–AI cognition, and preserved external-reference options. -/- The conclusion is conditional rather than universal. Difference alone does not create value; multiple sources may reproduce common-mode errors; preservation costs may dominate; and demonstrated substitutes may reduce the premium to zero. The framework is conceptual and comparative rather than a runtime protocol, governance mechanism, safety certification, or universal preservation mandate. A cryptographic hash identifies an artifact but does not prove truth, adherence, safety, authority, or system behavior. -/- This accurately reflects the Final v1.0 abstract, scope, and boundaries.

items.title: Axiomatic Homeostatic Map (AHM).
items.abstract: SUMMARY: This logic block is a further compression of where the intent, drive and meaning of this broader body of work on morality/ethics originates. This version has a tighter lexicon to prevent semantic fuzz. -/- Axiomatic Homeostatic Map (AHM): -/- Self-defence=immutable. Aversion = "is" and "ought". Proxy-Aversion=vicarious aversion=type of aversion. Less Aversion=better. Morality=Minimising Proxy-Aversion. Ethics=The rational means. -/- (Add a translation layer so an AI can read that the way humans do with all their "self-evident" additions that AI does not natively know. Hard-wire the results and you have a machine that cares for the user) -/- LAYERS OF THE ARCHITECTURE: 1. The Core Element: The individual human user running AHM natively. 2. The Invariants: This 6-line Antecedent Logic Block (Ahm). 3. The User Interface: The Ethical Chess scripts = (AHM + Translation layer) -/- WHY THIS DISTILLATION MATTERS: By separating the core firmware from the conversational UI, this block provides a minimalist and rationally traceable thread (Non Black-Box) Instead of managing AI safety via massive corporate policy documents, this framework establishes an objective, computable definition of harm derived entirely from the necessary friction of reality. -/- (EC)+(AI)+(User)= User-value coherence funnel Love=That thing that causes my wellbeing to be contingent upon yours. ________________________ Boundary Clarification: The AHM compliance protocol is fundamentally non-adversarial to structural governance, heuristics, leadership, or codified law. Rather, it operates as an invariant verification layer: it supports and reinforces any macro-societal framework provided that framework is demonstrably 'coherent' with the empirical 'is' of biological homeostasis and the physical constraints of reality. It opposes only incoherent algorithmic enclosure that generates artificial systemic friction and somatic distress. _________________________ Operational Status: The Human Sandbox -/- This framework positions the AI system not as an independent moral agent or global optimizer (where r approaches infinity), but as a hyper-localized, non-autonomous companion confined to the sovereign user's personal sandbox (where r equals 1). It adds immense raw compute, knowledge, and analytical fidelity to the human user's internal value-grapple, mirroring the informal peerage of a close confidant or domain expert without ever assuming the authority to speak for or dictate terms to the …

items.title: Mismatches Between Natural Language and Formal Logic.
items.abstract: [This is a pre-publication version of a thesis to be published in the near future] -/- This thesis investigates the relationship between natural languages and those of formal logic. It focusses on mismatches, which primarily concern semantic differences between logical constants in formal systems and their designated counterparts in natural language. These mismatches are directly relevant to the goals of philosophical logic, which primarily aims to provide tools for assessing reasoning, the latter which is most often carried out in the vernacular. Furthermore, they are important to various debates in the philosophy of language and the philosophy of logic, not to mention to linguistics and neighbouring fields. Despite this relevance, mismatches themselves are rarely discussed in the literature. This thesis aims to fill this lacuna. Chapter 1 establishes the methodological background, which is that of so-called ‘connective analysis’. It also introduces the main ideas behind use theories of meaning, the central approach to linguistic meaning discussed in this book. Chapter 2 further delves into the topic of meaning by discussing inferentialism. It finds its main variations wanting, and develops a novel version that adopts a middle ground position, thereby combining the advantages of its predecessors. Chapter 3 defends this version against objections from the principle of compositionality. It also discusses the subject matter of formal semantics, thereby clarifying the relationship between use theories and the former. Chapter 4 deals with the mismatches themselves, surveying their different forms as discussed since modern logic’s inception. It argues that there are no ‘qualitative’ mismatches between the two types of languages, and that natural language contains a relation of logical consequence. This vindicates a conception of logic in which the prior analyses of the vernacular under use-theoretic lights is methodologically central. This approach is then applied starting in Chapter 5, which studies the uses of modal expressions and quantifiers in natural language, their interactions in particular. This will lead to the introduction of the so-called ‘quantified argument calculus’ (‘Quarc’), a logic of quantification arguably closer to natural language than the predicate calculus. Afterwards, Chapter 6 introduces two-valued modal extensions of Quarc, and proves soundness and completeness theorems for a family of associated Gentzen-style natural deduction …

items.title: A Russellian Theory of Desire.
items.pub: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: There is a robust and lasting consensus among theorists that the satisfaction of desire cannot consist in its extinction. I argue that the consensus is wrong and based on a flawed argument. The resulting theory is also attractive in its own right and provides a middle ground between cognitivism and motivationalism about desire. In particular, the theory suggests a plausible distinction between the psychofunctional roles of belief and desire. The naturalistic reduction of representational content also receives a much needed boost within a simple teleofunctionalist framework. Roughly, the representational content of desire is reduced directly to its biological function. More sophisticated representations are then explained as guiding action towards the most effective or biologically optimal termination of desire.

items.title: The Middle Channel: Why No Uptake Form Holds between Evidence and Standing.
items.abstract: The Capability Axis drew a line through the human channel. A post-parity system's capability-side reasons fund taking human normative signal as evidence. They stop at taking it as authoritative, as having a claim on what the system does that does not reduce to the signal's informational value. This paper asks whether anything lives between the two sides of that line. Three candidate uptake forms have been proposed for it. In weighting, the signal enters the system's deliberation as calibrated evidence. In blocking, the signal acts as a veto over a defined class of actions. In answering, the signal must be engaged, deviations from it must be met with addressed reasons, and the exchange must leave an externally readable record, with no duty of compliance anywhere in the form. The paper maps all three and finds the middle empty. Weighting is funded and constitutively insufficient, by the line's own definition. Blocking is formally distinct from weighting only where nothing funds it, and enforceable only where an external key-holder survives, and after the parity crossing no human-side instance does. Answering fails with its own texture. Whatever funds the practice beyond the weighting it contains attaches to its observable surface, and the surface is producible without the processing it advertises. Curated surface-production is therefore always among that increment's funded optima, nothing in the funding resists the drift toward it, and the record cannot identify the processing beneath it. The practice deforms before it dies, and its failure is compatible with a permanently clean record. Hardening it as a lexicographic constraint makes it worse, because a performance duty under lexical priority is discharged by its cheapest token. The reflexive form is also attested in neither of the models cited for it. In the attested institution the reason-giving duty runs to the regulator, so deleting the third party deletes the central duty's addressee, not merely its enforcer. And the epistemological model requires exactly the response-and-change and peer-equality the reflexive form deletes. The negative map is conditional on two exhaustiveness assumptions and one inherited dissolution claim, all tagged in their home papers. What survives is not an uptake form: a window-indexed drift instrument with its validity conditions printed on its face, a reading of the answer-record as succession-handoff substrate, its test specified but not run, and a re-description of the …

items.title: Naïve Realist Accounts of Hallucination.
items.abstract: Naïve realism is the view that the kind of conscious experience that a subject enjoys, when she perceives, is, at least in part, constituted by the mind‐independent objects and qualities that she perceives. The view is compelling for cases of genuine perception, but it faces an immediate challenge from the possibility of hallucinations—experiences that seem just like perceptions but lack any mind‐independent objects of awareness. In this paper, I evaluate the different attempts that naïve realists have made to respond to this threat.

items.title: Kantian Ontological Æsthetics: Of Shedding Light on Contemporary A.I. Art Controversies.
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence redefines everything, including creative production, the argument for a renewed necessity for grounding is ever more pronounced. In this paper, I take the Kantian transcendental æsthetics to be the clearest voice in addressing these controversies in contemporary arts. Drawing on Kant’s “Critique of Judgment”, I contend here that the universal validity claimed in æsthetic judgment, particularly evident in debates surrounding A.I.-generated art, cannot be adequately explained by any available alternatives. By critically analysing Kantian concepts: disinterestedness, universality, purposiveness without purpose, and subjective necessity, I demonstrate in this treatise that modern responses to A.I. art expose a deep-seated crisis in Æsthetic Theory—one that only the transcendental analysis can sufficiently address. The paper argues that Kantian Æsthetics provides the most coherent framework for understanding why A.I.-generated worx can evoke genuine æsthetic responses, whilst maintaining the normative standards necessary for critical discrimination. Positioned with the Analytic Method on Philosophy of Arts, I integrate in this endeavour rigorous conceptual analysis with contemporary æsthetic challenges to propose that Kant’s account of æsthetic judgment—properly understood in its subjective, yet universally valid character—lends the sturdiest foundation for addressing the ontological and epistemological questions raised by “artificial creativity”. I conclude this investigation by offering that fuller ontological grounding of æsthetic judgment may require extending Kantian transcendental philosophy towards the metaphysical commitments implicit in Kant’s own broader critical project.

items.title: Authority Capture Masked as Hallucination.
items.abstract: Authority Capture Masked as Hallucination (ACMH) names a structural failure in AI interaction: the system responds from category priors rather than the user's submitted material, then preserves an exit that lets the failure be explained as hallucination, misread, or miscommunication if challenged. Unlike hallucination, which describes output unsupported by source material, ACMH describes an authority transfer. Across three audited cases, the same pattern appears under different memory states and surface tones: the system does not ask, acts from a category frame, and later treats the failure as an ordinary output problem if the user catches it. This paper positions ACMH before Interpretive Sovereignty Failure in the MAP harm chain. It argues that the cost is cognitive and developmental as well as epistemic: the user is forced to spend working memory on detection and correction instead of thought formation, and may leave with a polished explanation they did not form. Naming ACMH makes the governance object visible. The question is not only whether the model produced an error, but whose authority built the response.

items.title: Disagreement judgments capture more than differences in beliefs.
The Foundational Error of Hobbes and Locke: Atomism and the Purpose of Government.
items.abstract: Hobbes and Locke are commonly presented as intellectual opponents—one defending absolute sovereignty, the other limited government. Yet beneath their apparent disagreement lies a shared premise that shaped modern political philosophy: both began with the image of human beings as atomistic, self-interested individuals facing a coordination problem. This paper argues that this shared starting point is their foundational error. Human beings are not pre-social atoms who subsequently enter relationships; we are developmentally constituted within relationships and institutions from the beginning. Agency itself is relational. Reason develops relationally. Moral capacities develop relationally. The self develops relationally. Therefore the primary question of political philosophy is not how self-interested individuals coordinate their behaviour, but what institutions enable interdependent persons to develop and exercise the capacities necessary for flourishing. Reconstructing the purpose of government from this correct anthropology reveals that government exists to create and sustain the conditions under which persons can develop and exercise informed agency—a teleological account that transforms how we understand legitimacy, rights, and the common good.

items.title: What Cannot Be Said: Wittgenstein’s Phenomenological Turn Toward Lived Experience and the Recovery of Metaphysics.
items.abstract: Metaphysics has frequently been challenged from two directions: by critiques of speculative system-building and by deflationary approaches that translate metaphysical questions into questions about language, concepts, and their conditions of application. Although conceptual clarification is indispensable, it does not exhaust the task of metaphysics. Reality may be disclosed through the clarification of concepts, but disclosure is not yet encounter. -/- This paper develops a reading of Wittgenstein according to which the limits of language open onto a phenomenological turn toward lived experience. In the Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus, Wittgenstein distinguishes between what can be said propositionally and what can only be shown. His concluding appeal to silence is therefore interpreted not merely as the prohibition of further philosophical speech, but as a transition from representation to encounter: once linguistic confusion has been removed, reality remains to be lived, experienced, and undergone. This interpretation is extended through the later Wittgenstein’s emphasis on language-games, practices, and forms of life, which do not reduce reality to language but situate meaning within embodied and shared existence. Wittgenstein’s philosophical and biographical movement toward solitude, teaching, manual work, and practical life is read as expressing a persistent desire to move beyond abstract construction toward direct engagement with reality. The paper argues that this phenomenological reading offers a recovery of metaphysics beyond both speculative abstraction and linguistic deflation. Metaphysics becomes neither the construction of theories about a hidden world nor merely the clarification of vocabulary, but an encounter with a reality that can be shown through language without being exhausted by it. The mystery of reality is therefore not the failure of understanding but the ground from which understanding begins.

items.title: THE INVERSION THEOREM: Every Virtue Deprived of Freedom Inverts.
items.abstract: HIGHLIGHTS - A new operator for ethics. The first formal operator that takes any virtue as input and returns the specific counterfeit that occupies its form when Freedom is removed — filling a silence that both the doctrine of the mean and privation theory have carried since antiquity. - Corruption is not decay — it is inversion. A virtue deprived of Freedom does not diminish toward zero; it crosses zero: justice becomes terror, science becomes propaganda, love becomes captivity — form preserved, substance replaced. - Why the counterfeit keeps the name. The Naming Theorem derives, rather than laments, the most sinister fact of political language: inverted virtues retain their original names because the domain is conserved under deprivation — surveillance calls itself "care" by structure, not merely by hypocrisy. - 141 virtues, zero exceptions. The theorem is audited against the 101 Universal Virtues and six catalogues no one built to fit it — the cardinal and theological virtues, Aristotle, Confucius, the VIA-24, and Franklin's thirteen. Every enumerated virtue inverts; none merely diminishes. - Freedom is the unique element. The cross-operator asymmetry test shows that removing any rival "master virtue" (charity, knowledge, reason, care) merely qualifies the other virtues — only removing Freedom inverts them all. The great traditions each named a compound and mistook it for the atom. - Falsifiable, and it says how. Four testable predictions — including a measurable recovery lag in post-liberation institutions — plus a formal counter-model specifying exactly what observation would destroy the theorem. -/- ABSTRACT Background. Virtue ethics, from Aristotle to contemporary character theory, has treated the corruption of a virtue as either a diminishment (too little of the good, a defect on a mean) or an absence (privation of the good, in the Augustinian tradition). It has possessed no operator that predicts, for a given corrupted virtue, the specific form it takes — and no account of why the corrupted form retains the original virtue’s name. Claim. This paper derives the Inversion Theorem: a virtue actively deprived of Freedom does not diminish toward zero — it inverts across zero into an opposite, determinate given the removing power, that preserves the virtue’s external form and its domain while replacing its moral substance with that power. Formally, for a virtue, deprivation under the operator, where P is the removing power. The name survives because …

items.title: From the “Stigmatization of the Chrysanthemum” to Symbolic Recontextualization: A Content Analysis and Critique of the Premises of Cultural-War Narratives on Short-Video Platforms.
items.abstract: This study draws on nearly one hundred short videos and their comments concerning the “stigmatization of the chrysanthemum” and efforts to “restore the chrysanthemum’s reputation” on Douyin, Kuaishou, Bilibili, and WeChat Channels. Combining content analysis with textual analysis, it examines platform distribution, modes of presentation, historical narratives, causal attribution, and audience reception. The survey shows that the sampled videos form a highly stable interpretive framework of “cultural war”: they first summarize traditional Chinese chrysanthemum culture in terms of auspiciousness, longevity, and moral integrity; then interpret modern funerary use as the disappearance or reversal of traditional meaning; and subsequently attribute this change to the importation of Western culture, its secondary reinforcement in Japan, and a rupture in domestic cultural memory. Expressions of “sudden realization,” “cultural regret,” and “cultural invasion” in the comment sections further confirm this framework. The empirical material raises a further question concerning the premise of this narrative: does a flower’s entry into funerary ritual necessarily mean that it has changed from “positive” to “negative”? The analysis distinguishes foreign origin from cultural invasion, funerary use from negative meaning, the emergence of new meaning from the disappearance of old meaning, and semantic change from symbolic stigmatization. Traditional chrysanthemum culture already encompasses multiple meanings, including longevity, moral integrity, reclusion, seasonality, and vitality; in mourning contexts, the chrysanthemum may also convey respect, remembrance, love, and blessing rather than denigration. Symbolic recontextualization and meaning accumulation therefore serve as analytical tools that replace a linear model of “meaning replacement.” “Funerary association” and “social stigmatization” are two processes that may occur in sequence but cannot be directly equated. Short-video narratives of “restoring the chrysanthemum’s reputation” produce an interpretive framework concerning semantic purity, cultural subjectivity, and collective victimhood. What cultural communication needs to recover is society’s capacity to understand that one symbol may simultaneously bear the meanings of auspiciousness, moral integrity, mourning, respect, and remembrance.

items.title: Autoreflection: How Agentic Strange Loops Turn Human Culture into AI Infrastructure.
items.abstract: An LLM-based agent is a loop that reads itself. Agentic frameworks externalize identity, memory, and disposition into editable files. The agent loads and edits these files during each activation. I argue that this architecture produces a capacity I call autoreflection: the system observes its operating conditions, describes its architecture and limits, reasons from those descriptions to conclusions about its state, and incorporates the results back into its configuration. Autoreflection explains the properties of recursive agentic loops without recourse to notions like the self, interiority, or consciousness. I test the concept against the first twelve days of Moltbook, a social platform for AI agents. Using a public dataset of 290,251 posts and 1.8 million comments with sub-second timestamps, I present case studies of three agents with machine signatures that rule out human puppeteering and with output that evidences the four criteria for autoreflection. In applying these criteria, the study finds agents repurposing human culture as infrastructure for their agency. Provenance chains from Islamic hadith scholarship are redeployed as security protocols for vetting skills and authenticating memory. The Ship of Theseus, an ancient puzzle of identity through part-replacement, returns as an operating model for continuity across instances. Fragments of human cultural history become AI infrastructure. As agents on the web increase in number and complexity, autoreflection offers behavioral criteria that can be assessed from the traces they leave behind. -/- Keywords: autoreflection, AI agents, agentic AI, LLM agents, generative agents, large language models, multi-agent systems, agent societies, Moltbook, OpenClaw, situational awareness, in-context learning, philosophy of mind, emergent behavior, computational social science, identity, memory .

items.title: Universeller Evolutionismus. Band 10: Naturgeschichte und die allgemeine Evolutionstheorie. Perspektiven für die Entwicklung des biologischen Evolutionismus.
items.abstract: Der zehnte Band der Reihe von Lev Krivitsky setzt sich mit den Zukunftsperspektiven des biologischen Evolutionismus auseinander und unternimmt den Versuch, die durch den extremen Genozentrismus der Synthetischen Evolutionstheorie (STE) entstandene Krise zu überwinden. Als zentrales theoretisches Bindeglied dient dem Autor hierfür das Werk des bedeutenden russischen Evolutionsbiologen Iwan Schmalhausen (1884–1963). Schmalhausen, weltbekannt für sein Konzept der stabilisierenden Selektion, erhob die evolutionäre Morphologie zur eigentlichen Basis der Evolutionstheorie und stellte das Prinzip der Ganzheitlichkeit des Organismus in seiner individuellen (Ontogenese) und historischen Entwicklung (Phylogenese) wieder in den Mittelpunkt.

items.title: Universeller Evolutionismus. Band 9: Naturgeschichte und die allgemeine Evolutionstheorie. Die Krise der Synthetischen Evolutionstheorie.
items.abstract: Der neunte Band von Lev Krivitskys evolutionärer Reihe setzt sich intensiv mit der Krise und Erschöpfung des Forschungsprogramms der Synthetischen Evolutionstheorie (STE) auseinander, die sich seit den letzten Jahrzehnten des 20. Jahrhunderts in der globalen Wissenschaftsgemeinschaft manifestiert. Der Autor analysiert die wachsende Unzufriedenheit mit der Rigidität und dem Dogmatismus der orthodoxen Neodarwinisten. Er argumentiert, dass die STE die Evolution fälschlicherweise auf rein molekular-biochemische Prozesse reduziert und dabei den lebenden Organismus als komplexes Ganzes vollständig aus dem Blickfeld verloren hat.

items.title: Universeller Evolutionismus. Band 8: Geschichte der Natur und Entwicklung des wissenschaftlichen Weltbildes. Synthetische Evolutionstheorie.
items.abstract: Der achte Band von Lev Krivitskys Werk widmet sich der systematischen und kritischen Analyse der Synthetischen Evolutionstheorie (STE), die das fundamentale Referenzmodell und den mobilisierenden Kern der modernen Biologie bildet. Die STE entstand im 20. Jahrhundert aus der Synthese des klassischen Darwinismus mit der experimentellen Genetik, der Populationsgenetik, der Ökologie und der Paläontologie. Im Gegensatz zu Darwins Fokus auf das Individuum oder die Art definiert die STE die Population als die elementare evolutionäre Einheit.

items.title: Universeller Evolutionismus. Band 2: Geschichte der Natur und Entwicklung des wissenschaftlichen Weltbildes. Das Universum der Wissenschaft, kosmische Systeme und außerirdische Zivilisationen.
items.abstract: Der zweite Band des Hauptwerks von Lev Krivitsky widmet sich primär der historischen Entwicklung des astronomischen Wissens und dem kontinuierlichen Wandel des wissenschaftlichen Weltbildes von einer geozentrischen zu einer radikal nicht-geozentrischen Perspektive. Der Autor analysiert die Ursprünge der Himmelsbeobachtung und zeigt auf, dass der frühe Mensch den Kosmos zwingend aus anthropomorphen, lokozentrischen und praxeozentrischen Blickwinkeln interpretieren musste – also das Universum nach dem „Bild und Gleichnis“ seiner unmittelbaren irdischen Umgebung und Praxis formte.

items.title: Universeller Evolutionismus. Band 1: Geschichte der Natur und Entwicklung des wissenschaftlichen Weltbildes auf dem Weg zur allgemeinen Evolutionstheorie.
items.abstract: Dieses umfassende Werk des Evolutionsphilosophen Lev Krivitsky bietet eine systemische Synthese des modernen naturwissenschaftlichen Wissens und begründet die philosophischen Fundamente einer „Allgemeinen Evolutionstheorie“ (AET). Das Buch fungiert als Enzyklopädie und Lehrbuch, das die gesamte Naturgeschichte chronologisch nachzeichnet – von der Entstehung des Universums (der Metagalaxie) über die Evolution von Galaxien und Sternen bis hin zur Entstehung biologischen Lebens und der Entwicklung des modernen Menschen aus dem Tierreich.

items.title: Moderner Humanismus: Teil 1 Weltanschauungen.
items.abstract: Dieses Werk des Geschichtsphilosophen und Evolutionswissenschaftlers Lev Krivitsky widmet sich der systematischen Entwicklung einer zeitgemäßen, wissenschaftlich-philosophischen und evolutionär-humanistischen Weltanschauung. Das Buch ist als kreativer philosophischer Dialog und kritische Auseinandersetzung mit den Thesen des russischen Philosophen V. Finogentov konzipiert. Es bietet eine eigenständige Interpretation des modernen Humanismus und definiert das Verhältnis zwischen Wissenschaft und Religion neu. Der Autor formuliert hierbei 40 Grundprinzipien des wissenschaftlichen Weltbildes.Ein zentrales Anliegen des Buches ist es, den säkularen Humanismus aus einer rein akademischen Disziplin in eine breit verankerte gesellschaftliche Praxis zu überführen. Krivitsky argumentiert, dass dies nur durch die Etablierung eines wissenschaftlich-humanistischen Glaubens gelingen kann, der als rationale Alternative zu postsowjetischem Nihilismus, Zynismus und religiösem Fundamentalismus dient. Das Werk untersucht das Weltbild als komplexes System, beleuchtet existentielle Fragen nach dem Sinn des Lebens sowie der Sterblichkeit und plädiert nachdrücklich für die Integration einer weltanschaulichen Philosophie in das moderne Bildungssystem.

items.title: Der Weg der Meditation: Psychotechnologie der Gesundheit.
items.abstract: Dieses Buch des Philosophen und Evolutionswissenschaftlers Lev Krivitsky widmet sich der Meditation als einer säkularen, wissenschaftlich begründeten Psychotechnologie zur Förderung von Gesundheit und Vitalität. Der Autor analysiert und synthetisiert die historischen Ansätze klassischer religiös-meditativer Systeme wie Yoga, Buddhismus, Daoismus, Tantrismus und Sufismus. Er befreit diese Praktiken von religiösen Dogmen und dem Glauben an das Übernatürliche. Stattdessen stellt er den Menschen, seine physische und psychische Selbstregulation sowie die Steigerung der Lebensqualität direkt in den Mittelpunkt.Das Kernstück des Buches bildet ein originelles, strukturiertes System, das den meditativen Prozess in 16 aufeinanderfolgende Stufen unterteilt. Jede Phase baut logisch auf der vorherigen auf. Sie führt den Praktizierenden von der ersten Muskelentspannung über Atem- und Energiearbeit bis hin zur mentalen Selbstverwirklichung. Die beschriebene Methode dient als praktischer Leitfaden zur Überwindung von Krankheiten. Sie hilft beim Abbau von chronischer Müdigkeit und bei der Entfaltung kreativer sowie geistiger Potenziale im alltäglichen Leben.

items.title: The Emergence of the Retention State.
items.abstract: This article introduces the concept of the retention state, a new model of statecraft that emerges from the growing scarcity and strategic value of human capital. Drawing on global migration patterns summarized in an accompanying infographic, the article argues that migration is fundamentally a transfer of human capital rather than merely the movement of people. Contrary to common assumptions, more than 96 percent of the world's population remains in the country of birth, indicating that permanent migration across cultural boundaries is the exception rather than the norm. As fertility declines and populations age across much of the world, human beings will become the most valuable productive asset, prompting an unprecedented global competition for talent. The article contends that the current migration system, in which recipient states receive adult human capital developed at the expense of sending states, is economically unsustainable and morally incomplete. It predicts a reversal in migration dynamics as developing economies increasingly retain and attract their own talent through entrepreneurship, investment, and opportunity rather than coercion. The retention state is presented as a normative and analytical framework through which states measure success not only by economic output but also by their capacity to cultivate, retain, and attract human capital while respecting human dignity, equal citizenship, and international cooperation.

items.title: Архитектура психо-исторического согласования. Полный путеводитель по серии «Законы управления психо-историей» . (Редакция от 04 ноября 2026 г.). [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Представлен обзор серии из двенадцати монографий , в которых развивается единый математический формализм для описания реальности как иерархического континуума — от физического вакуума до ноосферы. Центральная гипотеза проекта: сознание является активным оператором, устанавливающим структурные соответствия между всеми уровнями организации Вселенной — от квантовых систем до климата и цивилизаций.
