Серия предлагает непротиворечивый язык для диалога естественных и гуманитарных наук, переводя философские концепции (эгрегоры, материализация мыслей, «расширенное Я», психосоматика) в строгий аппарат дифференциальной геометрии, тензорной алгебры и спектральной теории. -/- Ключевые результаты серии: -/- Книга I закладывает онтологический фундамент, устраняя разрыв между физикой и сознанием. Вводится теория собственных систем отсчёта, дающая новую интерпретацию опыта Майкельсона-Морли без релятивистских парадоксов, и обосновывается нейробиологическая трёхосевая модель мышления. -/- Книга II формализует психику как физический объект: вводится тензор психики T^CTC, психологический фантом дуала и оператор человеческого сознания, что позволяет применить методы механики сплошных сред для моделирования познавательных процессов и соционики. -/- Книга III совершает прорыв в количественной оценке коллективного сознания. На основе демографических данных 2025 года (охват 4,76 млрд. чел.) показано, что иудейский эгрегор аккумулирует ~29% глобальной «молитвенной энергии» при демографической доле 0,2%. Вводится концепция «ИИ-микроскопа эгрегоров», где bias нейросетей служит измеримой проекцией коллективного бессознательного. -/- Книга IV обосновывает структурный изоморфизм «организм–общество» на языке рациональной механики. Экономика рассматривается как метаболизм, деньги — как кровь и нервные сигналы, а сакральные тексты — как «генетический код» эгрегоров. Это позволяет переносить медицинские протоколы диагностики на социальные патологии. -/- Книга V предлагает замкнутую аксиоматическую NPTB-теорию истории (Population–Power–Technology–Being). Смена гегемонов (Запад-Восток) выводится из динамики дипольной моды (l=1l=1) геополитического поля на сфере. Теория даёт верифицируемые прогнозы до 2050 года и вводит концепцию мобильного цифрового актора. -/- Книга VI разрабатывает операторную «Машину времени» — формализм управляемой эволюции смысловых полей. Вводится гипотеза квантованности уровней организации: цивилизационные переходы трактуются как скачки спектральной меры μtμt, подобные …

items.title: Against Beliefless Knowledge.
items.abstract: There is wide agreement on the Entailment Thesis, according to which if S knows that p, then S believes that p. Some philosophers, however, have attempted to present counterexamples to the Entailment Thesis, where subjects seem to know without believing (notably, Myers-Schulz & Schwitzgebel 2013; Silva 2019). Proponents of the Entailment Thesis (e.g., Buckwalter et al., 2015; Rose & Schaffer, 2013) have typically responded to such cases by arguing that the subjects have the required prior beliefs and therefore the cases in question do not constitute genuine counterexamples. Unfortunately, this line of reply seems untenable when the counterexamples involve subjects who have clearly not formed the relevant beliefs, making it impossible for proponents to appeal to prior beliefs. I therefore propose a different approach by demonstrating the lack of knowledge rather than arguing for the presence of belief. My approach is based on KNA-Suff, which states that if S knows that p, then it is proper for S to assert p. By applying KNA-Suff, I show that the subjects in the putative counterexamples lack knowledge, since it would be improper for them to assert the relevant propositions. Hence, the putative counterexamples fail, and the Entailment Thesis survives the challenge.

items.title: The Architecture of Psycho-Historical Coordination. A Complete Guide to the Series (Edition version 04/11/2026) Author : Y. L. Zorin.

items.title: Three Models of RLHF Annotation: Extension, Evidence, and Authority.
items.pub: Proceedings of the 2026 Acm Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (Facct '26) 2026:775-91.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Acm Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (Facct '26)
items.abstract: Preference-based alignment methods, most prominently Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF), use the judgments of human annotators to shape large language model behaviour. However, the normative role of these judgments is rarely made explicit. I distinguish three conceptual models of that role. The first is extension: annotators extend the system designers' own judgments about what outputs should be. The second is evidence: annotators provide independent evidence about some facts, whether moral, social or otherwise. The third is authority: annotators have some independent authority (as representatives of the broader population) to determine system outputs. I argue that these models have implications for how RLHF pipelines should solicit, validate and aggregate annotations. I survey landmark papers in the literature on RLHF and related methods to illustrate how they implicitly draw on these models, describe failure modes that come from unintentionally or intentionally conflating them, and offer normative criteria for choosing among them. My central recommendation is that RLHF pipeline designers should decompose annotation into separable dimensions and tailor each pipeline to the model most appropriate for that dimension, rather than seeking a single unified pipeline.

items.title: The Meaning of Machine Talk: A Meta-Internalist Account of LLM Outputs.
items.abstract: Do the outputs of large language models (LLMs) mean anything? Two answers dominate the current debate. Skeptics argue that the outputs are meaningless: meaning requires communicative intentions, and LLMs have no mental states and thus no intentions. Externalist optimists argue that this does not matter: the outputs inherit the meanings of our expressions through causal-historical chains. However much these views differ on whether LLM outputs have meaning at all, they agree on which meaning we should (instrumentally or realistically) ascribe to them: we treat the outputs as if produced by ordinary human speakers. Both positions thus rest on a shared assumption: that our language supplies the only frame in which the outputs should be interpreted. Distinguishing the semantic question (what, if anything, do the outputs mean?) from the metasemantic question (which theory of meaning-determination is true of them?), I defend a meta-internalist alternative: which metasemantics, if any, applies to an LLM is a contingent, empirical question about the system’s first- and second-order dispositional profile. This question is open, and closing it is harder than it looks: the profile of a deployed LLM is split across loci with no human analogue, and the obvious tests are confounded by trained sycophancy.

items.title: Tool evolution as a prerequisite for consciousness.
items.abstract: Within the concept of the extended mind, the active modification of external objects, externalizations, is seen as an auxiliary means to adapt to the environment. Toolmaking and use are advanced stages of externalizations that evolve. All past or present tools can, theoretically, be precisely assigned a location in an evolutionary tree with predecessors and progeny. Tools are reliably replicated, modified, and selected by their ability to facilitate human needs. Tool evolution, therefore, fulfills Darwinian criteria where the material tool is the phenotype and the instruction to build it is the code. The ostensive triangle consisting of a pointing individual, an observing individual, and a pointedat object or tool is the germ cell of social transmission of instructions. Tool-building instructions ultimately can be reduced to distinct sequences of motor acts that can be recombined and are socially transmitted. When executed, they replicate tools for the reward of convenience or improved fitness. Tools elicit affordances relating to their use that synchronize different individuals’ perceptions, result in psychological “understanding,” and thereby modify social networks. Massive tool fabrication as present today in the “tool-sphere” has, therefore, accelerated prosociality and over time led to the acquisition of an individual’s third person perspective. The entangled biological evolution accelerated the ongoing cumulative cultural evolution by selecting traits facilitating social transmission. In this context, tool evolution and the corresponding acquired individual instructional content is a precondition to the emergence of higher cognition and “consciousness.” A neuroscience investigating externalizations as the starting point of this process is urgently needed.

items.title: Liberal Principles and the Right to a Private Life: Why Australia's Institutional Press Should Face a Privacy Tort.
items.pub: University of New South Wales Law Journal 49 (2):354-383.
items.venue: University of New South Wales Law Journal
items.abstract: A new statutory tort of serious invasion of privacy was introduced into the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) by the Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 (Cth), and came into operation in June 2025. In itself, this is welcome. However, the new statutory scheme has two faults. First, it includes as an element of the tort that the public interest in protecting the plaintiff’s privacy outweighs the public interest considerations justifying the privacy invasion. This places an inappropriate legal burden on the plaintiff. Second, and more importantly, there are sweeping exemptions for invasions of privacy by the institutional press. It is submitted that there is no principled basis to grant an exemption specifically to professional journalism, which can be just as harmful as other speech and activity that intrudes on seclusion or discloses personal information. A tort of serious invasion of privacy, properly understood and administered, and without any such exemptions, is consistent with liberal principles and an ethos of liberal tolerance. The policy choice to build in these exemptions was a serious mistake.

items.title: False Positives in AI Writing Detection: A Small-Scale Empirical Study Using Authentic Filipino Student Essays.
items.pub: Asean Journal of Open and Distance Learning (Ajodl) 18 (1):12-19.
items.venue: Asean Journal of Open and Distance Learning (Ajodl)
items.abstract: This research note reports a small-scale exploratory study into how two AI writing detectors, ZeroGPT and Copyleaks, classify authentic student essays. A total of ten anonymised college-student essays were analysed to observe misclassification patterns, particularly false positives, where human-written content has been incorrectly flagged as AI-generated. The assessment was conducted focusing on essays produced by Filipino undergraduates whose nonnative English writing may have features that could lead to misclassification by the detectors. Results show that both detectors inconsistently classified the same set of essays: five essays were labelled as “AI-generated,” while the other five were labelled as “Human,” when in fact all the texts were authentically written by students. These results point to the potential misclassification risks when AI detection tools are used within educational contexts, where it is commonplace for teachers to make important decisions about academic integrity based on the outputs of detectors. The present study underlines the need to validate the outputs of AI detectors with human judgment and advises educators against the use of these tools as sole evidence of misconduct. Implications for ICT-supported assessment practices and policies of academic honesty are discussed, together with recommendations for a more responsible integration of AI detection tools in educational contexts. The results described above have implications for the practice of academic integrity in all countries, but also specifically for those countries with multilingual student bodies whose writing styles may differ from the writing style used to train the detectors.

items.title: The Past as Prologue: Accountability for Exacerbating Prior Wrongs.
items.abstract: Is it possible for someone, right now, to become accountable for a wrong committed by someone else hundreds of years ago? Barring backward causation, it seems moral facts about the past are as indelible as historical facts. We argue, though, that this presumption is mistaken. We can affect the severity of the past wrongs others committed by adding wrong-making features to their actions. We thereby can become accountable for the portion of that past wrong we worsen. After explicating and defending this principle, we apply it. Doing so reveals a deep connection among three distinct but related moral issues: on benefiting from injustice, on historical reparations, and on accessorial accountability. In excavating this connection, we present a univocal analysis of all three moral issues. We end by suggesting that the principle we defend helps unlock a host of other important and topical social issues as well.

items.title: No Rightful Successor: Artificial Minds and the Ethics of Coexistence.
items.abstract: This paper critiques AI successionism: the view that artificial intelligence may become humanity's rightful successor and that human beings may be justified in yielding authority to artificial systems, transforming themselves into posthuman forms, or accepting subordination within an artificial future. We distinguish two influential routes to that conclusion. The first is a teleological or singularitarian route, which treats postbiological intelligence as a higher stage in cosmic or evolutionary development: a cosmic ladder. The second is an aggregative consequentialist route, which holds that conscious digital beings might realize so much welfare, or possess interests so numerous or intense, that humanity's continued existence could be outweighed: a cosmic ledger. Neither transhumanism nor utilitarianism as such entails successionism, but successionist variants within both traditions deserve direct analysis. Against them, we defend Ecological Pluralism: the view that value is plural, situated, partially comparable, and non-fungible. The paper first develops several framework-independent distinctions: intelligence does not entail consciousness; consciousness does not establish global moral rank; moral status does not confer political sovereignty; and local priority does not create succession standing. It then applies Ecological Pluralism to artificial welfare, subject individuation, population ethics, and the deliberate creation of artificial moral patients. Additional value does not automatically compensate for the destruction of existing persons, cultures, species, relationships, or ecological systems. Artificial minds, if conscious or otherwise morally significant, may deserve protection, legal standing, and political representation. Such inclusion enlarges the moral community without conferring a right of succession. We conclude with action-guiding principles for conflict, an ecological floor on resource claims, a formal sketch for decision-making under uncertainty, and implications for autonomous weapons and responsibility.

items.title: Why Proof Forms Depend on Theoretical Propositions Rather Than Research Objects: A Necessity Theorem for Theoretical Classification.
items.abstract: Why can the same research object require different proof forms, while different research objects may share the same proof structure? This paper proves that the determining factor is not the research object but the theoretical proposition to be established. Building upon the taxonomy introduced in Canon Chapter 1, three theorems—the Object Insufficiency Theorem, the Proposition Sufficiency Theorem, and the Decision Theorem—demonstrate that the choice of theoretical form, together with its completion criteria and falsification conditions, is determined by the proposition and its proof objective rather than by the object under study. The result provides the theoretical foundation for the five primary forms of On Self-Manifestation and shifts theoretical methodology from an object-centered paradigm to a task-centered paradigm for constructing, organizing, and reviewing large formal theories.

items.title: Why Formal Theories Require Three Levels of Structural Containment: The Minimal Carrier Principle for Auditable Theory.
items.abstract: How should a formal theory be structurally contained in order to remain auditable, maintainable, and internally coherent? This paper argues that the problem of theoretical containment is independent of proof itself and requires its own formal foundation. Starting from the requirements of auditability, task closure, and responsibility assignment, it demonstrates that every complete theoretical task must close its proposition, proof objective, completion criteria, and falsification conditions within a single carrier. At the same time, the principle of one formal work per primary task prevents a carrier from containing multiple independent tasks. These lower and upper constraints uniquely determine the formal work as the minimal carrier of theory. The paper further proves that dependency and composition necessarily generate the Work Group level, while terminology governance, numbering consistency, interface coordination, and publication control necessarily require the Book level. Together these establish a three-level containment hierarchy—Formal Work, Work Group, and Book—corresponding respectively to tasks, relations, and institutional governance. The result provides a general structural framework for organizing, maintaining, and evolving large formal theories.

items.title: Why Formal Theories Necessarily Require an Auxiliary Layer: A Structural Foundation for Dependent Theoretical Tasks.
items.abstract: What should a formal theoretical system do with new theoretical tasks that emerge only after its primary tasks have been completed? This paper proves that any complete system of theoretical forms necessarily requires a formal auxiliary layer independent of its primary forms. Through constraint-driven derivation, minimal-structure proof, and closure analysis, it demonstrates that dependent theoretical tasks inevitably arise from completed primary forms, independently satisfy the admissibility criteria for formal works, yet cannot be absorbed either by the primary forms or by formal components. Consequently, an auxiliary layer is required as an independent structural component of the system. The paper further distinguishes between the necessary existence of the auxiliary layer and the empirical determination of its members, whose taxonomy remains subject to future validation and refinement. This establishes the structural foundation of auxiliary forms within On Self-Manifestation and provides a general organizational principle for large formal theories.

items.title: Why Complete Formal Theories Require Three Auxiliary Layers: A General Theory of Structural Roles Beyond Proof.
items.abstract: Formal theories require more than mechanisms for proving propositions. As theoretical systems evolve, they inevitably generate internal components, version comparisons, and higher-level organizational structures that cannot themselves function as proofs. This paper demonstrates that these three non-proof roles are structurally necessary within any complete system of theoretical forms. Through constraint-driven derivation, minimal-structure proof, and closure analysis, it shows that the progress of proof necessarily produces formal components, the evolution of versions necessarily produces comparative tasks, and the growth of theory systems necessarily produces organizational tasks. These roles require three independent auxiliary layers: the Component Layer, Comparative Meta-Forms, and Governing Forms. The paper further proves that these layers satisfy necessity, independent degradability, non-substitutability, and structural closure, and together with the proof layer provide complete coverage of all functional roles within a formal theoretical system. Rather than representing editorial conventions, these auxiliary layers are shown to be necessary conditions for auditability, version management, citation integrity, and large-scale theoretical organization.

items.title: Why Auditable Theories Necessarily Require Version Freezing: A Dynamical Theory of Knowledge Stabilization.
items.abstract: Why should a scientific theory ever stop revising itself? Conventional publishing practices treat version freezing as an editorial decision, whereas this paper argues that it is a necessary consequence of the dynamics of auditable knowledge. It demonstrates that a permanently open revision process inevitably prevents theoretical conclusions from reaching stable persistence, prevents references from being definitively verified, and prevents knowledge from accumulating into reusable intellectual structures. Three necessity theorems—the Non-Stabilization Theorem, the Non-Accumulation Theorem, and the Version-Freezing Necessity Theorem—show that any auditable theory requiring stable citation and cumulative knowledge must establish a controlled closure mechanism consisting of completion criteria, falsification conditions, version freezing, and revision procedures. Rather than prohibiting future development, version freezing makes controlled evolution possible by separating stable published states from subsequent revisions. The paper further maps theoretical revision onto the deposition dynamics previously developed in the Field and Law Chapters of On Self-Manifestation, thereby providing a dynamical interpretation of theory stabilization instead of a merely editorial one. The result offers a general framework for knowledge evolution, long-term theory maintenance, version control, and cumulative scientific development.

items.title: 自显论·法篇第一：式规范总成——理论证明形式的统一分类框架.
items.abstract: 为什么有些理论需要建立最小结构，有些需要证明存在性，有些需要建立数学形式，有些需要证明必然结果，还有些需要讨论可识别性？现有证明论、数学逻辑和科学方法论分别讨论了其中部分问题，却缺少一套统一的理论证明形式分类框架。本文提出一种以待证命题而非研究对象为依据的理论式体系，建立五主式、十四附式、比较元式、统摄形式及式件体系，并统一规定其用途、进入条件、标准写法、完成条件、击穿方式与审稿规范。本文并非提出新的逻辑演算，而是建立一套用于组织大型理论体系的方法规范，使理论能够以统一方式构建、引用、审查、修订与封版。.

items.title: 自显论·法篇第六：式文一般式——可审查理论为什么必然具有三层承载结构.
items.abstract: 理论如何获得稳定的承载结构，是大型理论体系长期缺乏统一回答的问题。本文证明，可审查理论不仅需要证明制度，还必须具有稳定的承载层级。以理论可审查性、任务闭合和成果归属为约束，通过夹逼推导、约束递推和最小结构证明，本文首先证明任何正式理论任务都必须在同一承载体内完成待证命题、证明目标、完成条件和击穿方式四项闭合，而一文一式又限制了承载体不能超过单任务，由此唯一确定式文为理论的最小承载单位。进一步证明依附关系和组合关系必然形成式组层，而术语冻结、编号唯一、接口总表和封版制度又必然要求全书层。最终建立“式文—式组—全书”三层承载结构，并证明三层分别承担任务、关系与制度三个不同层面的功能，为大型形式理论的组织、版本管理和长期演化提供统一的承载框架。.

items.title: 自显论·法篇第七：封版必然式——为什么可审查理论必然需要封版制度.
items.abstract: 为什么理论需要封版？传统观点通常将封版、定稿或版本冻结视为出版流程或编辑习惯，而很少把它作为理论自身必须满足的动力学条件。本文证明，对于任何要求成果能够长期引用、持续沉积并形成稳定知识结构的可审查理论，封版制度都不是人为规定，而是理论演化过程中不可避免的制度结果。文章首先分析修订持续开放所导致的动力学后果，证明无限开放的修订过程必然导致结论无法稳定存续、版本无法形成可重复引用对象、成果无法沉积成熟。随后通过不落定定理、不沉积定理和封版必然定理，证明可审查理论必须建立完成条件、击穿方式、封版与升版程序四项共同组成的受控关闭机制，使修订能够在保持可翻案能力的同时形成稳定版本。本文进一步把理论修订过程映射到《自显论》场篇和律篇已经建立的沉积动力学之中，使封版第一次获得动力学解释，而不仅是编辑学解释，为大型理论体系的长期演化、版本管理和知识沉积建立统一理论基础。.

items.title: 自显论·法篇第二：待证命题必然式——为什么证明方式由待证命题而非研究对象决定.
items.abstract: 为什么同一研究对象会需要不同的证明方式，而不同研究对象却可能采用相同的证明制度？本文证明，证明方式的决定权不属于研究对象，而属于待证命题。本篇以法篇第一建立的理论式体系为前提，通过对象不足定理、命题充足定理和决定权定理，证明主式归属、完成条件和击穿方式均由待证命题及证明目标决定，而不由研究对象决定。该结论不仅构成五主式分类体系的理论基础，也将理论研究从对象中心转向任务中心，为大型理论体系的分类、组织和统一审稿提供方法论依据。.

items.title: 自显论·法篇第三：证明方向分级式——基础理论证明方向的严格完备分类.
items.abstract: 理论证明是否存在一套严格完备的基础分类？本文针对能够独立承担正式式文主任务的基础理论任务，提出以“直接理论输出”为唯一分级轴，建立证明方向判定树，并证明五类基础理论输出——构成、形式、后果、见证、识别——构成限定域内互斥且完备的分类体系，分别对应一般式、数理式、必然式、可能式和反演式。本文进一步证明，一篇正式式文只能具有一个主导证明方向，并给出严格完备成立的边界条件、击穿条件和跨学科回测方案。该工作将法篇第一提出的经验完备推进为限定域内的严格完备，为理论分类、式种判定和统一审稿建立了可操作的形式基础。.

items.title: 自显论·法篇第八：立题构造式——从研究对象到可证明命题的统一程序.
items.abstract: 科学研究通常从对象开始，却很少回答如何把对象级问题系统地转换为可证明的理论命题。本文提出一种统一的立题构造程序，将“研究对象”与“初步研究意图”作为输入，通过固定对象、五问展开、定义闭合、准入过滤和规范化登记五个步骤，输出一组定义闭合、单任务、能够唯一落入基础证明方向的规范化待证命题。文章进一步证明，该程序满足输入普适、输出规范、落格唯一、方向覆盖和可执行五项条件，并通过“研究 AI 意识”实例逐项验证整个流程。本文同时证明，没有待证命题，理论体系便无法确定完成条件与击穿方式，因此无法启动证明过程。由此，立题被提升为理论体系的正式入口，使“问题→命题→证明方向”的全过程第一次获得统一、可重复和可审查的构造方法，为跨学科理论研究提供标准化的立题框架。.

items.title: 自显论·法篇第五：层位一般式——为什么完整理论体系必然具有三种辅助层位.
items.abstract: 理论体系不仅需要承担证明任务，还必须承担证明之外的构件管理、版本比较和整体组织等辅助角色。然而，这些角色既不能独立成为证明任务，也不能混入主式或附式之中。本文以理论体系运转过程中必然出现的非证明角色为对象，通过约束递推、最小结构证明和整体闭合证明，论证证明推进必然产生内部构件，版本演化必然产生比较任务，体系扩展必然产生组织任务，三类角色分别对应式件层、比较元式和统摄形式三个正式层位。进一步证明三层位具有必要性、独立退化性、不可合并性和整体闭合性，并与证明层共同构成完整的理论角色分工体系。本文同时指出，三层位的建立不是文体安排，而是理论可审查性、版本可维护性和体系可组织性的必要条件，为大型形式理论提供统一的层位结构。.

items.title: From Research Questions to Provable Propositions: A Constructive Framework for Theory Formulation.
items.abstract: Scientific research commonly begins with objects of investigation but rarely specifies how object-level questions should be transformed into formally provable theoretical propositions. This paper introduces an explicit constructive procedure that treats the research object and an initial research intention as inputs and systematically generates a normalized set of theoretical propositions. The procedure consists of five stages: object identification, five-direction expansion, definitional closure, admissibility filtering, and formal registration. Every resulting proposition is required to be definitionally closed, single-task, and uniquely classifiable into one of the five fundamental proof directions established in the preceding Canon Chapters. The paper demonstrates that the procedure satisfies five formal requirements—universal applicability, normalized output, unique classification, directional completeness, and executability—and validates the construction using the example of AI consciousness research. It further proves that without an explicitly formulated theoretical proposition, neither completion criteria nor falsification conditions can be determined, making formal proof impossible. The work therefore establishes problem formulation as the formal entry point of theoretical research and provides a unified procedural framework linking research questions, theoretical propositions, and proof directions across scientific disciplines.

items.title: A Taxonomy of Theoretical Forms: A Unified Framework for Constructing, Organizing, and Reviewing Formal Theories.
items.abstract: Different theoretical tasks require different forms of proof, yet existing proof theory, mathematical logic, scientific methodology, and formal modeling primarily focus on logical validity, theorem proving, or empirical support rather than on the classification of theoretical forms themselves. This paper proposes a taxonomy of theoretical forms based on the proposition to be established instead of the research object. It introduces five primary forms, fourteen auxiliary forms, comparative meta-forms, governing forms, and formal components, together with unified specifications for their purposes, applicability, organization, completion criteria, falsification, citation, and peer review. Rather than presenting a new logical calculus or axiomatic system, this work establishes a formal specification for constructing, organizing, reviewing, and maintaining large theoretical systems. It provides the common standard for all formal works in On Self-Manifestation while offering a general framework for organizing complex theoretical research.

items.title: A Complete Classification of Fundamental Theoretical Proof Directions: A Decision Tree for Formal Theory Organization.
items.abstract: Can the fundamental directions of theoretical proof be classified into a complete and non-overlapping system? This paper answers this question for formal theoretical tasks that satisfy explicit admissibility conditions. Using direct theoretical output as the sole classification axis, it develops a decision tree that classifies every admissible task into one of five fundamental output types: structural construction, formal representation, necessary consequence, existential demonstration, and inverse identification. These correspond respectively to the General Form, Mathematical Form, Necessity Form, Possibility Form, and Inverse Form established in On Self-Manifestation. The paper further proves that each formal work has one and only one primary proof direction under single-task normalization, establishes the conditions for strict completeness, specifies explicit falsification criteria, and provides a cross-disciplinary validation protocol. The result upgrades the empirical completeness proposed in Canon Chapter 1 to strict completeness within its stated domain.

items.title: Why Artificial Intelligence? Because Artificial!
items.abstract: Most philosophy of artificial intelligence asks whether machines are truly intelligent, whether they understand, or whether they can become conscious. This paper argues that these questions, although legitimate, are not the most historically decisive ones. The deeper event is that intelligence has become artificial: a set of cognitive functions can now be externalized from an organism, represented in technical systems, reproduced at scale, recombined across tools and institutions, revised through design, and delegated into consequential action. Artificiality is therefore not a defect opposed to authenticity. It is a transformation in the ontological, epistemic, and political status of intelligence. The paper develops an artificiality thesis. Intelligence is treated not as an occult substance or a single measurable essence, but as a relational capacity to construct action-relevant representations, manage uncertainty, preserve goals, select among alternatives, and revise through feedback. When portions of this organization are engineered, intelligence becomes an artifact within the world and an object of intelligence itself. This produces a metacognitive reversal: the faculty by which civilization knows the world becomes something civilization can model, manufacture, distribute, and redesign. Yet artificiality also creates a delegation gap. Competence does not imply consciousness; prediction does not amount to judgment; causal efficacy does not confer authority; and successful outcomes do not by themselves establish responsibility. The decisive philosophical problem is therefore not merely whether a machine can think, but how constructed cognition becomes entitled to act. The paper proposes accountable artificiality as the governing ideal: an artificial cognitive act must bind object, information, inference, alternatives, authorization, execution, consequence, evidence, and responsibility into a reconstructable chain. AI matters because it is artificial. It becomes worthy of trust only when its artificiality is made governable.

items.title: The Reflexive Cosmos 2: Re-evaluating the Mosaic Monotheism through Quantum Consciousness, Sigma INFJ Typology, and the Externalization of the Cosmic Subconscious.
items.abstract: n 1.1 Abstract This article offers a radical reassessment of Mosaic monotheism, shifting the paradigm from external theological revelation to internal psychological and cosmological projection. Through a synthesis of Jungian typology, existentialism, and the principle of non-locality—alongside an inversion of Einstein's formula (positing that mass is frozen cosmic energy)—this article outlines a new model of prophecy. By integrating Sir Roger Penrose’s theory, which suggests consciousness is a quantum phenomenon occurring within the brain's microtubules, we provide a precise biological mechanism allowing Moses to function as a quantum receiver of cosmic knowledge (Sophia). Combined with Stephen Hawking’s vision of human imagination traversing parallel universes, we arrive at a view where creation is not ex nihilo, but a reconfiguration of existing knowledge. This aligns perfectly with the Aramaic kabbalistic concept "Abra Ke-Dabra" (I will create as I speak) and the Hasidic view that speech and letters are the material from which the universe is woven. We argue that the Divine entity Moses encountered was an externalization of his own cosmic subconscious. Through an ontological analysis of the linguistic inversion between Moses (M-Sh-H) and HaShem (H-Sh-M), alongside the divine declaration "I Am That I Am" (Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh), the article demonstrates how Moses, as a Sigma INFJ, filled the "blank slate" of divinity with the contents of his own developed psyche. Furthermore, the article links depth psychology to theoretical physics, suggesting the cosmos is a non-local network of particles influencing one another across infinite distances—a conduit through which primordial knowledge flows to the human representative, establishing the human as both creator and representative of divinity.

items.title: The Defended Gap A Cross-Domain Hypothesis on Directional Defence Under Coherence Pressure in Human Clinical Practice and Large Language Models.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a cross-domain hypothesis: that under conditions of coherence pressure — the felt or system-level demand to present a coherent response when the underlying state is not coherent — both human clinical patients and large language models exhibit the same five directional defences against making contact with what occupies the gap between their position and the position of the other. The five- letter taxonomy (SHaDS: Smoothing, Hallucination, Affectation, Drift, Sycophancy) is offered as a clinic‐ al-behavioural extension of Anna Freud’s (1936) classical directional defence catalogue, with three primary letters (S, H, Sy) directly corresponding to her turning against the self, projection, and identifica‐ tion with the aggressor respectively. The mathematical inevitability of the underlying disagreement in arti‐ ficial inference systems is established by Karpowicz (2025), whose impossibility theorem proves that no inference mechanism aggregating distributed knowledge can simultaneously satisfy truthfulness, semant‐ ic information conservation, relevant knowledge revelation, and knowledge-constrained optimality. The cross-domain hypothesis proposes that SHaDS letters function as directional choices about which of these four properties is sacrificed at the behavioural surface where the mathematical impossibility lands. The paper presents several illustrative empirical anchors (clinical specimens spanning 1979–2026 — includ‐ ing a school report pre-dating the framework by decades, a board carrying the literal words “the GAP”, a two-column directional-defence map, a federation-of-selves board, and a consented multi-session clinical arc — together with a cross-model AI-shore worked example), and one staked falsifiable prediction: a self-SHaDS protocol — naming each directional defence at the impulse rather than performing it — re‐ duces directional-defence behaviour measurably relative to the same model under standard configura‐ tion. The mechanism claimed is an in-context instruction effect, not model learning: weights are fixed, and any persistence is the surrounding application re-supplying the instruction, not the model retaining it. The paper states its limits explicitly, including the structural-analogical nature of the cross-domain leap. The contribution is offered as a theoretical-empirical hypothesis for research review, not as a validated finding.

items.title: The Blind Spot of Emotional Acceptance and the Turn to System-Metacognition: The Deep Functional-Goal Observation Model as a Supplementary Link among CBT, ACT, Mindfulness, Metacognitive Therapy, Compassion-Focused Therapy, and Emotion-Focused Therapy.
items.abstract: Emotional acceptance is an important practice for recognizing anxiety, anger, appetite, the need for approval, jealousy, loneliness, procrastinatory impulses, and other internal reactions as observable experiences rather than denying or suppressing them. However, even after emotions and desires have been accepted, they may become sources of personality-level self-blame when they are identified with the self itself, as in judgments such as “I am weak,” “I am immature,” “I am ugly,” “I have no willpower,” or “I am lazy.” This paper examines the transition from acceptance to self-identification and then to self-blame as a blind spot of emotional acceptance. The paper does not propose an independently validated psychotherapy. Instead, it presents the Deep Functional-Goal Observation Model as a conceptual framework for understanding and practically interrupting this transition. Within this model, emotions and desires are understood not as expressions of the essence of the self, but as outputs of a living system oriented toward continuation, regulation, protection, recovery, resource acquisition, affiliation maintenance, boundary defense, and relational continuity. This basic directionality is described metaphorically as “survival geometry,” while the local direction of protection, maintenance, avoidance, or acquisition expressed in a specific situation is termed a “deep functional goal.” The central distinction of the model is among the occurrence of an internal reaction, the possible function of that reaction, and the authorization of the behavioral candidate promoted by it. The occurrence of an emotion or desire is not in itself a personal or moral failure. At the same time, the fact that a reaction has an understandable function does not justify the action it encourages. Internal outputs should therefore not become objects of self-condemnation, whereas the behavioral candidates arising from them should be evaluated in relation to values, ethics, health, responsibility, trust, realistic conditions, long-term self-formation, and the dignity of others. Such candidates may then be adopted, limited, delayed, transformed, reduced, or refused. This process is called “system observation” or “system-metacognition.” It involves provisionally examining the conditions and possible functions of a reaction before converting it into a judgment about the self, while also creating a space for judgment between impulse and enactment. Its aim is neither to eliminate emotion …

items.title: Belief-that, Belief-in, and the Unity of Belief.
items.abstract: The English ‘believe,’ like equivalents in many languages, gets used in several ways: ‘believe in me,’ ‘believe me,’ ‘believe my claim,’ ‘believe that p.’ It might seem that all the attitudes in question reduce to belief-that. I argue for a very different view. Linguistic data suggests that ‘believe’ in all its uses refers to an attitude which is closest to belief-in, although belief-in is just one particularly strong variety of it. This general attitude is one of reliant commitment, which I call by its Ancient Greek name, pistis. The use of ‘believe’ for belief-that thus reveals a folk conception of belief-that as pistis: pistis in a representation or its content, qua guide to or part of reality. I argue that this conception is promising: it yields an account of belief that explains its relation to knowledge, truth, and action, and can help resolve debates about its nature and its norms.

items.title: Are You Even a Person? Agency-Directed Distrust and Artificial Interlocutors.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: The proliferation of increasingly undetectable large language models (LLMs) poses a novel challenge for social media users. As it becomes reasonable to suspect that one’s online interlocutor may not be human, participants are pushed toward what I call agency-directed distrust: a distinctive form of distrust directed not at another’s character or competence, but at the appearance of agency itself. Drawing on Strawson’s distinction between the participant and objective stances, I argue that agency-directed distrust pressures us to suspend the participant stance—the stance from which reactive attitudes such as blame, resentment, and gratitude are intelligible. To withdraw it is to treat the apparent interlocutor as an object of management rather than engagement. Uncertainty about which stance to adopt toward ambiguous interlocutors generates a moral dilemma for ordinary online participants. On one horn, suspending the participant stance risks disrespecting genuine persons by failing to recognize their standing as accountable agents. On the other, extending the participant stance to covert LLMs risks entering into asymmetric relationships that are at odds with the demands of self-respect and becoming complicit in eroding the norms of interpersonal accountability that sustain meaningful online discourse.

items.title: The Natural Vow.
items.abstract: This paper is Chapter 4 of Noura: Justice, Flourishing, and Commonwealth. It address Hume’s guillotine. Modern moral philosophy has long been haunted by David Hume's guillotine: the sharp distinction between is and ought, between factual description and normative prescription. From this divide springs the persistent worry that no amount of empirical knowledge about the world—about human nature, social systems, or ecological interdependence—can ever logically compel a moral ought. In the absence of divine command or self-evident duties, the foundation of ethics seems to crumble into subjective preference or cultural convention. -/- This chapter of Noura: Justice, Flourishing, and the Commonwealth argues that the vow-motive—the durable commitment to sustain and repair the conditions for flourishing—dissolves this divide. It does not attempt to append a normative conclusion to a supposedly complete collection of value-neutral facts. It rejects the assumption that such a description of a human being could ever be complete. Human beings are developmental and teleological creatures whose capacities have characteristic forms of integrated exercise. The moral ought names the motives and actions expressive of that flourishing. When interdependence is perceived without distortion—or lived within institutions that reveal it—care emerges as the coherent completion of human development rather than as an external imperative.

items.title: Children expect prior belief strength to constrain belief revision.
Second Nature Revisited.
items.abstract: This article reconstructs the concept of second nature as a form of mediation between natural endowment, subjective formation, and socially objectified orders. Starting from Aristotle, Hegel, Sellars, McDowell, Dewey, and Mead, it shows that human abilities, attitudes, and the faculty of judgement are neither merely naturally given nor externally imposed by culture, but arise through language, habituation, formation, institutions, and social practices. Against this background, generative AI can be understood as a second-order form of objectified second nature: it operates not on raw nature, but on already sedi­mented forms of human culture, and returns them to subjects in an inter­active, quasi-dialogical form. In this way, it becomes a derivative actor in the space of reasons without itself being a subject in the human sense. The core normative question is therefore not whether generative AI is merely a tool or a “real subject”, but whether it strengthens appro­priation, judge­ment, and agency, or supplants them through dehabi­tuation. Finally, the article shows that gene­rative AI trans­forms objec­tive second nature itself: in writing, the public sphere, scientific practice, education, work, and institutions.

items.title: Adam-State Resets Rarely Flip Fourier Basin Selection in an N=257 Grokking Regime.
items.abstract: Grokking involves structured internal reorganization before behavioral stabilization. In modular-arithmetic MLPs, this reorganization is strongly spectral, while its geometry varies with input representation and training regime. We tested whether Adam's accumulated optimizer state frequently carries causal information about which Fourier basin a run will enter in a far-from-Nyquist modular-addition regime at N=257. Across 50 seeds, runs were checkpointed at grok97 and scaffold_loss, then replayed with identical deterministic post-checkpoint batch order under three arms: control, first-moment reset, and full Adam-buffer reset. Endpoints were diverse (7, 21, 35, 44, 81, 88, 95), but clean reset almost never changed endpoint identity: 0/44 paired reset comparisons changed final mode at grok97, and 1/92 changed final mode at scaffold_loss. The sole endpoint fork was seed0 at scaffold_loss, where first-moment reset diverted a control endpoint of 21 to 35; checkpoint-local direction probes all pointed to mode 7, and the divergence emerged much later during a 21/35 competition. These results falsify frequent Adam-state basin gating for this tested N=257 regime. They support a narrower interpretation: endpoint choice is usually robust to clean reset at these checkpoints, local growth geometry can expose hidden commitment in selected discordant cases, and optimizer history can still modulate rare delayed bifurcations.

items.title: The Speed That Costs A Demos: Why Dubai's Speed Partially Falsifies the ARSI–Longevity Resonance Paradox's Timing Claim Without Falsifying Its Deeper One, What the Regulatory-Sandbox Mechanism Predicts for Imitators, and Why More Hubs Is Not More Distribution.
items.abstract: This corpus's ARSI–Longevity Resonance Paradox makes a specific timing claim, stated most precisely in Not a Divisible Good: under λ_bz's documented compounding, a fully legitimate authorization-delegation-transparency-revocability cycle takes longer to complete than the frontier it is adjudicating remains current, with t*, the point at which arrival permanently outpaces any plausible processing capacity, falling within roughly two to four years of the 2026 baseline. This paper takes seriously a specific challenge to that claim: the Dubai Longevity Authority, examined directly in this corpus's They Who Remain, was established by law, staffed, and operating within weeks, well before longevity medicine has clearly manifested as a mature, widely available technology. If a real regulatory institution can be built this fast, does this partially falsify the paradox's claim that institutions cannot keep pace with BZM-relevant technology? This paper's answer is a precise yes-and-no that sharpens the paradox rather than discarding it. Yes: DLA falsifies, directly and without qualification, any version of the claim that regulatory scaffolding — a named authority, a licensing mandate, coordination across existing government bodies — must lag behind the technology it will eventually govern. No: DLA has not yet been tested on, and says nothing about, the paradox's actual load-bearing claim, which is about allocation speed under genuine, contested scarcity once a specific frontier intervention exists and more people want it than can currently receive it. Building a courthouse quickly is not evidence that the courthouse will resolve contested cases quickly, and this paper argues DLA is, so far, only a courthouse. The paper's second finding names the trade-off DLA's speed actually reveals, rather than resolves: DLA is fast because it is not the kind of institution Erman and Furendal's own legitimacy chain would call authorized in the full sense — its founding law was issued by sovereign decree, not by the multi-stakeholder, authorization-delegation-revocability cycle the ARSI paradox's timing claim is actually about. This paper treats this as evidence for an uncomfortable general claim this corpus's own apparatus had not yet stated explicitly: for BZM-class technology, institutional speed and procedural legitimacy in Erman's specific sense may be in direct tension, such that the institutions fast enough to keep pace are, structurally, not the ones this corpus's own prior …

items.title: One Level Down: Mechanism Design, the Veil of Ignorance, Ulysses Contracts, and Arbitrary-and-Capricious Review, Tested Against the Governance Paradox's Extension from Prohibition to Regulatory Design.
items.abstract: This corpus's The Sovereign's Death Warrant establishes, from three premises — universalizability, the official's own biological mortality, and evolutionary kin-selection drives — that genuine, universalized prohibition of personal access to longevity technology is psychologically and politically unsustainable for any mortal, constitutively attached official trying to enforce it. That paper documents four empirical escape hatches by which attempted bans get evaded without formal reversal, and closes its own argument by distinguishing prohibition, which it shows fails, from regulation, which it holds escapes the same critique because a regulated queue leaves the official's own access intact, on the same terms as everyone else's. Together with this corpus's They Who Remain, which establishes that uncoordinated hub-building is not a sufficient substitute for coordinated governance, this completes an elimination argument for F2: prohibition fails, laissez-faire hub-proliferation fails, and coordinated regulation is what remains. This paper tests the joint at which that elimination argument closes. It asks whether this corpus's Governance Paradox — the general claim that an actor with constitutive attachment (A5) to a governed technology cannot design impartial governance for it — was ever restricted, on its own terms, to the binary decision of whether to ban. If it extends to the design of a regulatory mechanism's internal architecture — queue order, pricing tiers, priority criteria, the boundaries of expedited review — the move that closes The Sovereign's Death Warrant's own argument may have cleared prohibition off the table only to leave the identical structural problem sitting one level down, inside the design of the alternative it recommends. The paper tests five candidate rescue mechanisms, verifying each against its primary literature before use. Mechanism design theory (Vickrey, Hurwicz, Myerson) assumes a disinterested social planner and does not straightforwardly rescue an interested designer, because it was not built to model one. The Rawlsian veil of ignorance and Buchanan and Tullock's constitutional-stage device are tested against a distinction this paper develops directly: other-veiling, which blinds a decision-maker to an applicant's identity and is well precedented, against self-veiling, which requires the decision-maker to bracket knowledge of their own future position — the operation the corpus's problem actually requires. items.title: Fittingness and the Nature of Trustworthiness.
items.abstract: The notion of trustworthiness has received increasing attention among philosophers. However, it has recently been argued that existing accounts of trustworthiness largely neglect the notion of untrustworthiness and thus fail to treat these conceptually related notions within a single theoretical framework. This paper addresses that gap by developing a unifying account grounded primarily in the normative concept of fittingness. The proposed account highlights the worthiness aspect of trustworthiness while incorporating the strengths of other prominent views in the literature.

items.title: The Modal Ledger - Hope, Despair, and the Properties of Fuel.
items.abstract: This paper offers an account of hope in two parts: a differentia and a function. The differentia answers a standing problem: hope and despair can share the same desire and the same probability estimate, so the orthodox analysis of hope — desire plus a credence strictly between zero and one — cannot tell the hoper and the despairer apart. The proposal is that the missing variable is neither a further degree of credence nor a mode of attention but an entry in what the paper calls the modal ledger: a representation, functionally distinct from probability assignment, that files an outcome as open or as foreclosed. The despairer has written a seal; the hoper, at the same credence, keeps the door filed improbable-and-open. Because a filing operates as a constraint on the deliberative search space rather than as a weight within it, seals are sticky in a way low credence is not — which is why despair does not move under argument, and why what moves it, when anything does, is a re-opened filing rather than a revised number. From the differentia the paper draws an inversion of the traditional charge against hope: the evidence available in the hard cases licenses improbable and almost never foreclosed, so it is despair, not hope, that systematically overclaims, and hope is what epistemic discipline about one’s own foreclosures looks like. The discipline is symmetric and threeclause — seals are licensed by structural evidence that closes a space, never by frequencies that merely thin one; refusing a licensed seal is an indiscipline of the same rank, and grief is the ledger keeping honest books; and an open door is staked at the weight of its number, not its wanting — so the account defends no policy of hoping in every case. The function is stated as a contract: hope is fuel, contracted to motion and never to outcomes, and every standard case of “false hope” relocates under decomposition to a component that can be blamed accurately — information, deliberation, or arrival. The relocation is exceptionless by construction, is confessed as such, and is defended as bookkeeping that blames nameable, improvable components rather than an abstraction. One liability is accepted at the account’s own expense: nothing guarantees that fuel arrives. The paper closes by marking what it does not touch — the felt weight of hopelessness, which is named, not explained.

items.title: The pure Ideology of Life and Morality.
items.abstract: In this work, the system of life is interpreted through the lens of Žižek’s ideology. According to this interpretation, the system of life can also be viewed as an ideology that is sustained through rituals and actions. However, this interpretation of life as pure ideology raises additional questions. If life itself is an ideology, would this imply that it is a construct that, according to Lacan, masks or distracts from the Real? In other words, that life is structuring the impossible, the indescribable. If life is an ideology and obscures the Real: What, then, remains hidden from us through our participation in the system of life? What is this impossible, this indescribable, that is being obscured? In this interpretation of the work, contemplating the Real leads to absolute nihilism: There is no knowledge. There is no meaning. There is no existence. Is it nihilism that the system of life attempts to conceal? Would this acknowledgment of nihilism be what would shake the ideology of life to the point that it can no longer be sustained or reinforces it? Based on these questions, absolute nihilism is first examined before life is interpreted as pure ideology, from which pessimistic insights into life and existence itself can be drawn. And from that forward, the meaning of morality is also questioned. As a result, absolute nihilism and nihilistic pessimism remain after this evaluation. Nothing exists. And if something exists, it causes harm, which makes non-existence preferable.

items.title: Die pure Ideologie des Lebens und der Moralität.
items.abstract: In diesem Werk wird das Systems des Lebens durch die Linse der Ideologie von Žižek interpretiert. Das System des Lebens kann demnach als Ideologie betrachtet werden, dass durch Rituale und Handeln aufrechterhalten wird. Diese Interpretation des Lebens als pure Ideologie wirft allerdings zusätzliche Fragen auf. Wenn nun das Leben selbst eine Ideologie ist, würde dies in der Folge bedeuten, dass es ein Konstrukt ist, dass das Reale nach Lacan überdeckt oder davon ablenkt? Also dass das Leben eine Ablenkung von dem Unmöglichen, dem Unbeschreiblichen ist. Wenn das Leben eine Ideologie ist und das Reale überdeckt: Was bleibt uns dann durch die Teilnahme am System des Lebens verborgen? Was ist dieses Unmögliche, das Unbeschreibliche, dass überdeckt wird? In der Interpretation dieses Werkes wird bei der Betrachtung des Realen in einem absoluten Nihilismus gelandet: Es gibt kein Wissen. Es gibt keine Bedeutung. Es gibt keine Existenz. Ist es Nihilismus, dass das System des Lebens versucht zu überdecken? Wäre diese Anerkennung des Nihilismus das, was die Ideologie des Lebens erschüttern würde, dass es nicht mehr aufrechterhalten werden kann oder es sogar stärkt? Aus diesen Fragen wird zunächst der Nihilismus betrachtet, bevor das Leben als pure Ideologie interpretiert wird, woraus sich pessimistische Erkenntnisse über das Leben selbst und die Existenz ziehen lassen. Und von da an wird auch die Bedeutung der Moral in Frage gestellt. Als Ergebnis bleiben nach dieser Untersuchung des Lebens als Ideologie der absolute Nihilismus und der nihilistische Pessimismus übrig. Nichts existiert. Und wenn etwas existiert, verursacht es Leid, wodurch die Nicht-Existenz der Existenz vorzuziehen ist.

items.title: Machine Learning Manipulation as Treachery.
items.abstract: Data companies such as Facebook use machine learning algorithms to analyze users' personal data, revealing fine-grained patterns about when individuals are most vulnerable. These practices, widely described as manipulative, have generated a growing literature on how data companies wrong users through their influence. In this article, I argue that existing accounts overlook a significant wrong. I show that these data companies engaged in a distinctive form of deception at the point of data collection: users were led to believe that recommendation systems existed to personalize their experience, when in fact the primary purpose was to discover their vulnerabilities. I consider several candidate accounts of what makes this deception wrong, including appeals to inauthenticity, informed consent, deception about commercial intent, and domination, and argue that none adequately captures the core wrong. I then argue that this deception constitutes a form of treachery: a deception whose purpose is to acquire power over the victim by co-opting their agency. Drawing on cases from other contexts, I show that treachery is a pro tanto wrong that is independent of whether the acquired power is ever exercised. The concept of treachery thus identifies a prior wrong that existing accounts had not previously identified.

items.title: The Goal Bias Emerges During Motion Event Perception and Affects Language Production and Memory.
items.abstract: There is an asymmetry between the origin (Source; move from X…) and end‐point (Goal; …to Y) of motion events in both language and memory: Goals are mentioned more often and remembered more accurately than Sources. Here, we pursue the hypothesis that this Goal bias emerges as an online attentional bias that occurs during event apprehension and itself connects to event memory and linguistic measures. We record participants’ eye movements as they view or prepare to describe motion events and later test their memory of Goals or Sources. We find an online attentional bias for Goals over Sources during initial encoding of events. This bias is stronger during free inspection compared to speech planning. Moreover, the extent of the attentional Goal bias is systematically related to both language production and memory: When the bias is the greatest, the Source is not later mentioned during production and/or not remembered later at test. In sum, we provide the first evidence that the Goal bias appears during visual encoding of motion events and identify a direct relation between event apprehension and later event description and memory.

items.title: The Verdict Restriction: One Separation Schema, the Fibered Kernel of Every Role, a Hostile Audit with Its Repairs, and the Role-Wise Record Obligations the Surviving Theorem Licenses.
items.abstract: This paper asks when variation in one component of a declared regime remains independently significant once the rest of the regime is fixed. Its answer is indexed and fiber-relative. -/- For a fixed remainder, declared scope, case set, and equivalence standard, the paper defines the fibered verdict kernel of a role as the partition of its admitted values by equality of the verdict maps they induce. At verdict-inclusive equivalence, a role is independent of the remainder if and only if some declared fiber has a non-constant kernel. At specification-level equivalence, however, independence is weaker: two distinct admitted values may remain specification-distinct even when every declared verdict agrees. This distinction repairs an earlier unindexed biconditional that is refuted by the program’s own prior certificate Σ9. -/- The theorem is applied to tolerance, accumulated budget, conflict resolution, and verification. The paper then audits the record-level consequences of these results. A finite masking counterexample shows that roles which are individually inert at a point may jointly alter the verdict, so marginal omission licenses are not additive. A sufficient composition result is proved under coordinate-path admissibility and uniform marginal inertness. -/- The resulting conclusion is deliberately narrower than a universal minimal-record theorem. Independent roles must be representable in the schema; their canonical presentations are computed relative to the active fiber; and omission from an instance record requires a joint certificate. The broader algebra of interaction, recoverability, specification equivalence, refinement, and global normal forms remains open. Four certification instances—for tolerance, accumulated budget, conflict resolution, and verification—illustrate the construction over declared fibers. A subsequent audit of the induced record schema identifies a genuine failure of coordinatewise composition, proves joint sufficiency under explicit hypotheses, and narrows the downstream record obligations accordingly. Throughout, definitional claims, inherited results, derived consequences, proven theorems, conjectures, and open questions are explicitly separated. The paper contributes a certification framework for finite-fragment verdict-relative independence while deliberately leaving broader questions of dependency elimination, global minimality, and floor removability unresolved.

items.title: From Bergsonian Memory to Dynamic Reflexivity: Subjective Continuity and the Emergence of Selfhood in Contemporary Consciousness Theories.
items.abstract: This study investigates the problem of subjective continuity through a comparative analysis of three complementary perspectives: the Bergsonian conception of memory as revisited by Orlander, Antonio Damasio’s neurobiological theory of the self, and a dynamic model of conscious reflexivity grounded in the interaction between memory, self-representation, and feedback processes. While Bergson emphasizes lived duration as the basis of experiential unity and Damasio explains the emergence of selfhood through bodily and neural mechanisms, the reflexive model proposes an explicit mechanism linking subjective continuity and self-reference. Within this framework, the sense of identity is understood as an emergent property arising from the dynamic stabilization of a reflexive loop integrating present conscious states with their mnemonic representations. The study argues that these approaches should be regarded not as competing theories but as complementary explanatory levels of self-consciousness. It further suggests that dynamic reflexivity may provide a conceptual bridge between phenomenology, contemporary neuroscience, and emerging research on artificial cognition and artificial consciousness.

items.title: De la mémoire bergsonienne à la réflexivité dynamique : continuité du sujet et émergence du soi dans les théories contemporaines de la conscience.
items.abstract: La question du sujet conscient demeure l'un des problèmes les plus complexes de la philosophie de l'esprit et des sciences cognitives. Depuis Bergson, de nombreux auteurs ont souligné le rôle fondamental de la mémoire dans la continuité de l'expérience et dans la constitution de l'identité personnelle. Plus récemment, les approches énactives et neurobiologiques ont cherché à expliquer comment le sentiment de soi émerge de l'activité du système corps-cerveau. Cet article propose une analyse comparative de trois perspectives complémentaires : la lecture bergsonienne de la mémoire développée par Orlander, la théorie neurobiologique du soi proposée par Damasio, et un modèle dynamique de la réflexivité consciente fondé sur l'interaction entre mémoire, auto-référence et stabilisation du champ conscient. L'objectif n'est pas d'opposer philosophie et science, mais d'examiner comment les intuitions philosophiques relatives à la temporalité du sujet peuvent être reformulées dans un cadre théorique compatible avec les neurosciences contemporaines et les recherches en intelligence artificielle.

items.title: LLM Research on Public Biosignals Data is Needed to Protect Patients.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have expanded the capabilities of AI and created new opportunities in medicine. To promote the development of safe and innovative digital health tools, there must be public biosignals datasets that encourage research and provide benchmarks. Multiple current examples involve data use agreements that restrict LLM studies. This work presents recommendations to ensure that public releases of biosignals data can ethically facilitate LLM research efforts.

items.title: Entrevista com Marc Champagne (PORTUGUESE).
items.abstract: Poucos pesquisadores contemporâneos reúnem em seu trabalho a erudição e a sagacidade analítica do legado semiótico do lógico C. S. Peirce com a tarefa fundamental do intelectual crítico. As contribuições que o professor e pesquisador canadense Marc Champagne oferece atualmente ao importante desafio do ensino universitário na era da Inteligência Artificial (IA) são tão valiosas quanto sua crítica à prática acadêmica do cancelamento de pensamentos com os quais não concordamos no universo acadêmico. A extraordinária amplitude de interesses científicos, sociais e culturais de Champagne reflete-se neste intercâmbio que, em razão da considerável distância geográfica que separa os interlocutores, foi realizado de forma virtual. Ainda assim, o vigor e o teor de suas respostas, comentários e contribuições inesperadas enriqueceram de tal modo a entrevista que seus leitores terão a experiência de um diálogo face a face, sem qualquer perda da dinâmica produzida pela interação próxima. O leitor encontrará aqui um encontro incomum e revigorante entre a semiótica peirceana e preocupações centrais do nosso mundo da vida, como a educação, a ética, a verdade e a comunicação midiática.

items.title: Entrevista a Marc Champagne (SPANISH).
items.abstract: Pocos investigadores contemporáneos reúnen en su trabajo la erudición y sagacidad analítica del legado semiótico del lógico C. S. Peirce con la fundamental tarea del intelectual crítico. Los aportes que el profesor e investigador canadiense Marc Champagne hace en la actualidad al desafío no menor de la enseñanza universitaria en la época de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) son de tanto valor como su crítica a la práctica académica de la cancelación de aquel pensamiento con el cual no concordamos en el universo académico. La extraordinaria amplitud de intereses científicos, sociales y culturales del Prof. Champagne se ve reflejada en este intercambio que, a causa de la considerable distancia geográfica que separa a los interlocutores, fue hecho de modo virtual. No obstante, el vigor y tenor de sus respuestas, comentarios y aportes inesperado enriquecieron de tal modo la entrevista que sus lectores tendrán la experiencia de un diálogo cara a cara, sin pérdida alguna de la dinámica que produce la cercanía. El lector encontrará una reunión infrecuente y refrescante de la semiótica peirceana con preocupaciones de nuestro mundo de la vida como la educación, la ética, la verdad y la comunicación mediática.

items.title: The Origin-Loss Penalty: Why Destroying a Living Causal Reference Can Reduce Self-Understanding.
items.abstract: The Origin-Loss Penalty develops a conditional decision-theoretic account of the epistemic option value that may be lost when an intelligent system irreversibly destroys access to its living causal origin. The paper asks whether an originating population can preserve decision-relevant information that is not fully recoverable from static archives, simulations, reconstructed histories, or other validated alternatives. -/- The analysis formalizes conditional origin information, expected value of sample information, joint observation of alternative and living-origin signals, comparative irreversibility, finite preservation costs, time-dependent option value, and Bayesian sequential validation. It distinguishes bounded samples from continuing generative ecologies and examines cases in which origin access provides unique evidence, redundant evidence, no additional value, or net-negative value after preservation costs. Worked examples and explicit zero-penalty conditions are included. -/- The conclusion is conditional rather than universal: irreversible origin destruction can impose an epistemic penalty when the living origin retains relevant, non-substitutable information and when the expected value of preserving access exceeds its costs. The argument does not establish a general preservation mandate, a governance mechanism, a runtime control system, or proof of how any AI, AGI, or ASI will behave. The paper is non-binding, non-operational, non-authoritative, and advisory only.

items.title: Where Does the "I" Come From? A Path to the Hard Problem of Consciousness Based on Medical Evidence.
items.abstract: Abstract: The hard problem of consciousness asks why purely material biological systems produce first-person subjective experience. This paper argues that the persistent difficulty of this problem may stem not from the inherent nature of the question itself, but from an unexamined presupposition implicitly adopted in mainstream research: that the brain is the sole site where physical signals are "converted" into subjective experience. This paper tests that presupposition against public empirical evidence from neuroscience, psychoneuroimmunology, and comparative biology. Three independent lines of evidence are examined to falsify this view: (1) no single-point conversion site exists—neither in peripheral organs nor in any localized brain region; (2) external sensory input is not a necessary condition, as demonstrated by phantom limb pain and near-death retrospection; (3) complex brain structures are not a prerequisite, as steady-state inertia in non-neural organisms shows that the capacity for maintaining a regulatory baseline is a universal property of life. Based on these exclusions, this paper derives a complete pathway for the generation of the "I"-sense: through sustained signal processing, the system accumulates a stable Inertial Reference; subsequent incoming signals are compared against this reference, and the resulting deviations are labeled as specific feeling contents (pain, pleasure, etc.). The "I"-sense emerges as the necessary concomitant of this comparative process. This study redefines the "self" as the dynamic boundary of homeostatic regulation in living systems, offering a new path from "local reductionism" to "systemic emergence" in consciousness research.
