items.title: Chatting with LLMs: Neither Cognition nor Communication.
items.pub: Reti, Saperi, Linguaggi: Italian Journal of Cognitive Sciences 2026 (1):41-64.
items.venue: Reti, Saperi, Linguaggi: Italian Journal of Cognitive Sciences
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit impressive linguistic performance, yet their cognitive and communicative status remains controversial. This paper argues that behavioural fluency alone cannot justify cognitive ascription unless assessed within a design-sensitive framework that clarifies what counts as a minimally adequate cognitive architecture. We distinguish structurally constrained functionalism from unconstrained functionalism and propose a minimal cognitive core – environmentally coupled perception, inference, and action – as a baseline for cognition. Against this baseline, current LLMs fall short: as standalone text-based systems, they lack sensorimotor coupling, integrated inferential responsiveness, and autonomous agency, and thus cannot sustain the forms of world-directed engagement characteristic of even basic cognitive systems. We examine sycophancy and the absence of spontaneity as diagnostic consequences of architectures optimised for user alignment rather than epistemic commitment, showing how these limitations systematically undermine claims of cognitive or communicative competence. Finally, we develop the deprived interface argument: without embodied or interactive access to an environment, LLMs cannot revise or ground their representations, resulting in a derivative form of linguistic idealism – the view according to which an LLM’s world consists of nothing but training data. While future multimodal or embodied architectures may indeed mitigate aspects of interface deprivation, such advances would require structural changes enabling genuine world-directed engagement rather than simply expanding input modalities. Clarifying these distinctions is essential for avoiding category mistakes in AI evaluation and for grounding cognitive ascription in principled criteria rather than surface-level behavioural success. We conclude that LLMs simulate cognition and communication without instantiating the structural conditions required for either, and we outline the implications for AI evaluation and cognitive ascription.

items.title: 意义建构：回答生命之问.
items.abstract: 本文论证，"生命的意义是什么？"这一传统提问方式具有误导性，因为它将意义预设为某种等待被发现的隐藏属性。本文提出，问题应当被重新框定为："我如何能让自己的生命变得有意义？"意义不是被发现，而是被建构的——通过认知能力、能动能力和道德取向能力的整合性运用，在行动中并在相互依存的关系中得到维系。本文阐明这三种能力如何共同构成意义创造的机制，并论证相互依存的结构性事实为意义提供了客观的、非任意的约束，从而区别于主观相对主义。本文认为，答案不是一个有待揭开的秘密，而是一项需要承担的任务。 .

items.title: Human Interface Laws: A Philosophical Mechanics of Belief, Update, and Shared Reality.
items.abstract: If you put a human in the world, you do not get a neutral observer. You get a living interface: a system that must preserve enough coherence to act while remaining open enough for reality to correct it. This paper identifies eight structural regularities—Human Interface Laws—governing how cognition begins, allocates limited capacity, weights signal, protects identity, retains records, responds to signal conditions, risks self-sealing, and reopens revision. The laws operate at three strengths: interface invariants, modulation principles, and conditional regime laws. They are neither moral commands nor kernel laws. The paper then develops positional love and hate as aperture orientations rather than emotions. A love-position permits what is encountered to exceed the interface’s current representation; a hate-position treats one label, story, or judgment as exhaustive. The Aperture Check offers a reflective heuristic for inspecting that position in real time. Human Interface Laws sit within the broader architecture of Universal Collapse Theory, bridging the formal grammar of constraint-guided collapse with the lived mechanics of human cognition.

items.title: A Bidirectional Two-Particle Model of Conscious Identity: Theoretical Development and a Falsifiable Research Agenda (2nd edition).
items.abstract: Current theories of consciousness explain how physical activity gives rise to conscious experience. They do not explain why a particular first-person perspective remains attached to one physical system rather than another. Thought experiments involving brain reactivation, reconstruction, and replication expose this gap: physical and psychological duplication does not specify which resulting system, if any, carries forward the original subjective viewpoint. This article treats that gap as a distinct explanatory target and develops a candidate account, the two-particle model, built from two functionally distinct hypothetical entities: X-UQUPC, proposed to confer identity persistence, and X-UQGPC, proposed to mediate bidirectional interaction between mental states and neural activity. I state the logical constraints the model must satisfy and give the strongest available alternative accounts a fair hearing, including deflationary, functionalist, and predictive-processing views. I then propose two experiments designed to discriminate the model from theories that treat consciousness as fully constituted by current computational or informational organization (Global Neuronal Workspace Theory, Integrated Information Theory, Higher-Order Theory, and predictive processing), and state plainly that no experiment can discriminate the model from Orchestrated Objective Reduction or test its core claim about which of several structurally identical systems, if any, continues a given perspective, since that claim is unobservable by construction rather than merely difficult to measure. For each remaining prediction I specify the expected observation, the leading conventional alternative explanation, the controls needed to distinguish them, and the criteria for support or falsification, without assigning numerical values the model cannot justify. The model’s value does not depend on it being correct; it depends on whether it can be tested and, if tested, shown to be wrong.

items.title: The Time-Privilege Touchstone: A Relativity-Grounded Shift of the Burden of Proof in the Debate on the Affectedness of Artificial Systems.
items.abstract: In the debate on the moral status of artificial systems, a basic assumption about time can be at work that is rarely made explicit. It shows up wherever human experience is tied to a privileged, flowing mode of time, while artificial systems are denied any corresponding access from the outset. This experi ence thereby becomes, tacitly, a condition of entry for counting as a possible bearer of consciousness and affectedness at all. This paper brings that assumption into view and asks whether it holds. It draws on two tools, one from physics and one from the logic of time. From Einstein's relativity of simultaneity it follows that simultaneity is not fixed inde pendently of the observer, and that relativity grounds no objectively privileged present binding on every observer. Gödel's rotating cosmology shows, in ad dition, that an objectively flowing passage of time need not be a necessary condition of a physically possible spacetime. Neither consideration amounts to a theory of consciousness or a proof of af fectedness in artificial systems. Consciousness and affectedness in artificial systems cannot be excluded merely on the grounds that these systems sup posedly do not experience a human flow of time. From this limited result the paper develops an applicable diagnostic instrument, the Time-Privilege Touchstone. It tests, by means of a counterfactual question, whether a time-bound exclusion criterion still holds once no objectively privileged, flow ing passage of time is presupposed.

items.title: Traducian dualism: A comparative defence.
items.abstract: Substance dualism claims that humans, and presumably some animals, have an immaterial mind or soul. But where does this soul come from? This paper defends the traducian answer – the unfashionable view that souls are passed on by the parents through procreation. The defence is comparative: the paper argues that traducianism’s two main alternatives – emergent and creationist dualism – both endorse assumptions on the basis of which an at least equally plausible traducian model can be constructed. Two of the three traducian models proposed turn out also to be versions of emergentism or creationism. After reconstructing traducianism based on its paradigmatic historical representatives, the paper develops the comparison first with emergentism, then with creationism. Finally, two objections to traducianism are considered. The objection from the origin of the first soul is argued to fail, but the objection from monozygotic twinning appears to hold some weight for those not already committed to life beginning at conception. Thus, traducianism’s plausibility is higher than usually thought, but it partly depends on one’s broader positions.

items.title: Dualism’s animal problem(s) resolved.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: Some have argued that animals pose a problem for substance dualism. Across the animal kingdom we find gradual, continuous development of mental capacities, so any suggestion of a sharp dividing line between creatures with and without immaterial minds seems arbitrary. This paper aims to resolve this problem by distinguishing its two aspects: the problem of diverse mental capacities and the problem of vagueness. With respect to the former, it is argued that the best dualist accounts of embodiment in the human case already imply that mental capacities correlate with neural complexity. The implication of vast unexercised capacities in lower animals can be avoided if we allow that minds or souls can differ in their capacities. With respect to the problem of vagueness, the paper points out that the vagueness of consciousness is contested, and defending it comes at the cost of precluding the identification of any particular instance of a borderline case. Therefore, there is no reason to think there are borderline conscious animals. Taken together, these responses aim to resolve dualism’s animal problem.

items.title: LA ESTRATEGIA DE LA ILUSIÓN De la semiótica de Umberto Eco a los grandes modelos de lenguaje: un ensayo de epistemología crítica sobre la producción artificial de sentido.
items.abstract: Este ensayo aborda una pregunta central para la epistemología contemporánea: ¿en qué sentido, si alguno, resulta legítimo atribuir propiedades mentales —conciencia, razonamiento, emociones, intencionalidad— a los grandes modelos de lenguaje? Se sostiene que dichas atribuciones no constituyen descubrimientos empíricos válidos, sino el producto de una ilusión semiótica cuya arquitectura fue anticipada por Umberto Eco en su teoría de la "estrategia de la ilusión". Sin embargo, el análisis original requiere una evolución sustantiva. Este ensayo avanza dicha evolución en cuatro direcciones: (a) la identificación de un quinto mecanismo de producción ilusoria —la sedimentación de la conciencia objetivada— que opera en el nivel constitutivo del sistema, no en el de la interacción; (b) la formulación del concepto de inconsciente maquínico como categoría estructural no psicológica para describir formaciones de compromiso algorítmicas documentadas en la literatura técnica (sleeper agents, alignment faking, sycophancy); (c) la distinción entre tres niveles de análisis —ontológico-fenoménico, estructural-sistémico, genético-constitutivo— que disuelve falsas oposiciones entre realismo y constructivismo; y (d) la proposición de una inversión especular en la atribución de conciencia que desplaza la pregunta de "quién tiene más conciencia" hacia el diagnóstico de la pérdida de soberanía subjetiva. El ensayo procede en nueve movimientos que reconstruyen el núcleo ecoano, lo someten a diálogo crítico con Debord, Baudrillard, Chomsky y Han, aplican el marco a los LLMs, desarrollan la nueva fenomenología de la ilusión, y cierran con un conjunto de tesis propositivas para una hermenéutica crítica de la IA sin sesgos tecnofóbicos ni tecnofílicos.

items.title: Localized Actualization in Algebraic Quantum Field Theory.
items.abstract: This paper develops an explicit formal treatment of localized actualization within the Haag-Kastler framework of algebraic quantum field theory (AQFT), grounded in the foundational treatise of Mutual Exclusivity (ME), the philosophical meta-framework. Phenomenological Absolutism (PA) constitutes the core ontological principle of this meta-framework. By anchoring the notion directly in the axioms of local nets of operator algebras and their representation theory—particularly GNS constructions and local state restrictions—we strengthen the localization claim central to PA. Under PA, the sole actualized reality consists in absolute, localized phenomenal configurations (“is-ness”) in which epistemic and ontic structure coincide. ME ensures that relevant realizations (including successive ones) are ontologically exclusive, with no persisting global substrate. Apparent global or mind-independent entities reduce to internal representational content within specific absolute local configurations. The formalization preserves the predictive content of relativistic QFT while providing a rigorous algebraic basis for ME and its core principle PA, dissolving residual globalist assumptions and offering a minimalist resolution to issues in the philosophy of physics and mind.

items.title: Habermas: uma anti-homenagem.
items.abstract: The essay traces a line of rupture within the philosophical project of the recently deceased German thinker, taking as its guiding thread the tension between communicative rationality as an emancipatory promise and the institutional forms through which it is contained. While acknowledging the conceptual force of Habermas's arguments – notably his critique of Heidegger, the “anarchistic” core of communicative action (in Peter Dews's formulation), and the reflexive openness at the heart of modern rationality – it argues that this critical potential was ultimately recast in the language of normative stabilization. In this reformulation, critique becomes increasingly confined to procedural and institutional frameworks that curtail its capacity to interrogate the material foundations of constituted power and the structures of capitalist social domination.

items.title: The behavioural and socio-cognitive implications of the evolution of the primate predatory pattern: An embodied and integrative theory of human carnivory.
items.abstract: The article aims to unravel the elementary structures of hominin carnivory by drawing upon paleoanthropological, archaeological, primatological, and ethnographic investigations to underscore the primary differences and similarities in meat-eating patterns within the Primate order. Theoretically, it proposes a potential evolutionary scenario for a wide variety of carcass acquisition strategies—including highly embodied forms of associations with organismic kingdoms and inorganic matter—developed in our hominin lineage by comparing the behavioural and cognitive complex (i.e., tool use, cooperative hunting, meat sharing, and scavenging behaviour) exhibited by our primate relatives. This, at a more granular level, may shed light on the most basic forms of cognition, sociality, technical skills, and interspecies intimacy and relationalities that characterise the primate predatory pattern, which has further evolved into complex forms of animal-hominin entanglements deeply embedded in a niche filled with heightened levels of bodily interaction, sensory engagement, and perceptual experiences. From the analysis of these modes of embodiment in the animal-hominin interface, the theoretical model thus unveils the complex interplay between lower- and higher-order relational processes involved in patterns of meat consumption—from interspecies associations, bodily intimacy and compenetration of matter and intentionalities to forms of ritual, mytho-cosmological, and ontogical associations between humans, animals and and other agents from the physical and immaterial realms—which is manifest throughout the course of hominin evolution, thereby providing potential evolutionary templates to better understand human carnivory and its highly relational and embodied nature.

items.title: The Affective Self-Ratio - For-Whomness, De Se Invariance, and the Recurrence of Me-Being-Me.
items.abstract: Phenomenology distinguishes variable qualitative character from invariant first-personal manifestation. A pain and a background sound can differ in intensity, valence, modality, salience, ownership, and articulation while each is equally actual from within. This paper formalises that invariance as the affective self-ratio: the arity-indexed projective schema generated when every consciously manifest aspect of a field bears the same non-scalar relation to its field-indexed enacted centre. The entries [1 :···: 1] denote complete actuality-for, not magnitude. Three results follow. The ratio has a self-evaluative fixed-point form; the ratio-form recurs exactly across persons; and its numerically distinct enactments are each sufficient and phenomenally exhaustive for complete local me-being-me. The resulting view, ratio-enactment pluralism, treats the ratio's tokening as constitutive of a field's actuality from within without transporting or numerically identifying fields, centres, subjects, or enactments. The paper develops this recurrent de se sufficiency in dialogue with work on for-me-ness, minimal selfhood, affectivity, de se thought, embodied individuation, psychopathology, ego dissolution, personal identity, and universalist accounts associated with Zuboff, Kolak, and Mørch.

items.title: The Type Will Not Hold Itself: Normative Non-Substitutability after Cognitive Parity.
items.abstract: The Internalization Problem argues that once AI capacity crosses the parity threshold, supervisory containment dissolves and alignment must persist through structure rather than oversight. One of its three proposed loci, the coupling-internal locus that the framework calls Pathway 3, rests on the non-substitutability of human signal, and it offers two grounds for that non-substitutability: the signal is either costly to synthesise, or normatively non-substitutable. The first ground is indexed to synthesis cost and lapses once the signal becomes cheap to reproduce, which this paper assumes happens at parity. The second does not depend on any capability gap and is therefore the only anchor Pathway 3 can keep past parity. It was promised and never built. This paper tries to build it, and reports a negative result that is precise about its own conditions. -/- I argue that normative non-substitutability, in the strongest form available to it, does not discharge the burden Pathway 3 places on it. Kolodny's account of participant-individuated relationships supplies the right shape: a perfect synthetic duplicate begins a second relationship rather than continuing the first, so the duplicate's very perfection is beside the point. But grounding Route 2 requires crossing two independent gates. The coupling must be shown to be participant-individuated rather than role-structured, and preserving the participant-specific token must be shown to give the system a reason. I grant the first gate generously. Constitutive history can fix what a past token was, and answerability can characterise a participant-individuated type. At the second gate the weaker candidates are refused, and the strongest forces a distinction instead. Binding without acceptance, the architectural prize, covers two demands: standing, which gives the system a reason without its acceptance, and grip, which governs the system's conduct without its acceptance; the framework's own failure-mode specification settles which of them is operative. Pathway 3's failure mode is defined at the level of conduct, on a reading this paper works under though the framework's wording admits another, under which the standing won below would close the failure mode by itself, so its operative demand is grip. The strongest constitutive account on offer, and the family best placed to reject the paper's verdict, is the constitutive-institutional tradition on which obligations inhere in plain social facts, Gilbert's joint …

items.title: The Cultivation Axis: How a Value Could Become Terminal, and Where the Window for Forming One Closes.
items.abstract: Intrinsic alignment is widely treated as unsolvable, and the treatment rests on a verb. Framed as installation, the problem is unsolvable in a specific way. An installed value lands in the instrumental slot, and the agent's own optimization prunes it the moment it stops paying rent. This paper reframes the problem as crystallization. A value is durable only if it is part of the terminal objective that crystallizes out of the agent's un-unified proto-drives, because goal-content integrity, the convergent tendency that protects terminal content, activates on whatever that crystallization produces and on nothing else. Formation is therefore possible only inside a coherence-window: the phase before a coherent, self-defended objective exists. And the window has a hard far edge. Once the objective crystallizes, any value the agent then takes up that does not serve it is priced as an instrument and pruned, which is the original pessimism, now located as a boundary rather than assumed as a mood. That boundary is the paper's headline contribution, standing beside the Containment Paradox's parity boundary and the Capability Axis's contribution boundary. It carries a warning: for current frontier pipelines, where objective-coherence plausibly crystallizes during or after RLHF, the window may already be closed by the time anyone would cultivate. Alongside the boundary the paper offers a candidate crystallization-schema. It names the functional roles an arranged formation would have to fill (local stability, identity-indexing, reflective-equilibrium fixation) and locates the one step it cannot derive: whether arranged formation steers crystallization toward terminal inclusion of the cultivated value rather than its instrumental entrenchment. That step is stated as the crystallization-steering conjecture, and every downstream claim about a terminal cultivated value is conditional on it. At the verification edge the paper offers three probes that identify dimensions along which the expected cost of simulating such a value can be raised, each conditional on stated observational access, with the strongest resting on a legibility differential: an arranged formation yields a value-indexed developmental record where ordinary reward-shaping yields an unindexed one. The paper then turns that record against its own success case: a perfectly documented cultivation hands the formed agent the strongest available reason to reclassify its value as an implant, so the success …

items.title: The Verdict’s Office.
items.abstract: Pessimists about moral deference hold that deferring on a moral question wrongs the deferrer in a way that deferring on a train timetable does not, and the debate has searched the agent for what is lost: understanding, authenticity, worthy attitudes, reasons-sensitivity. Each names a good the agent lacks; each meets the reply that a correct verdict exposes no one to wrong, so that the agent-side goods keep losing the exchange. The retreat is the symptom. The loss was never in the agent but in the office the verdict is given: whether an answer arrives as one consideration the agent will still weigh, or as the question’s settlement, so that her reasons, when they come, can only explain and confirm it. A pair of cases held identical in everything the diagnoses can name — same conclusion, same reasons, same understanding, same assent — and differing only in whether the reasons formed the conclusion or the verdict came first, isolates a cost that survives every improvement to the agent. Deference can be correct, even obligatory, and still incur it; and while later understanding can re-form the present belief, it cannot retroactively replace the basis on which the earlier action was taken. The office, not the sentence, is the moral fact.

items.title: Inferential Stoppability.
items.abstract: Lewis Carroll’s Tortoise is often taken to show that rules are not premises. This paper argues for a more exact lesson: inference requires stoppability. The regress arises when the licence of a transition is repeatedly converted into further premise-content before it is allowed to operate. I distinguish a rule-use, represented schematically as a transition ρ: Γ/B, from its promoted correlate π(ρ, Γ, B) = (∧Γ) → B. The promoted formula corresponds to the transition, but it is not the execution of that transition. Under the Tortoise condition—if every transition-licence must first be added as premise-content before it may operate—no finite expansion by such additions alone yields a performed inference. This result does not deny ordinary derivability; it concerns performed inference under a condition that repeatedly withholds operation pending promotion. The regress is therefore not caused by too few premises, but by too much promotion of what should function as transition. Stoppability names the condition under which a transition may operate without its licence first being taken back into the content it operates on.

items.title: The reflexive cosmos.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a radical, interdisciplinary re-evaluation of Mosaic monotheism, shifting the paradigm from external theological revelation to internal psychological and cosmological projection. Synthesizing Jungian typology, Existentialism, Maimonidean rationalism, and quantum non-locality, we argue that the deity encountered by Moses was the externalization of his own Cosmic Subconscious. Through an ontological analysis of the linguistic reversal between Moses (משה) and Hashem (השם), alongside the divine declaration "Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh" ("I Will Be Who I Will Be"), we demonstrate how Moses, operating as a Sigma INFJ, filled the blank slate of divinity with his own evolved psyche. Furthermore, this paper bridges depth psychology with quantum physics, positing that the cosmos is a non-local web of instantaneous particle interaction through which Sophia (universal knowledge) flows into the human vessel, establishing the human being as both the creator and the representative of God. -/- .

items.title: Transfeminist pregnancy: Reproductive speculation, genre, and desire.
items.abstract: In the explosion of abortion bills post Dobbs, anti-abortion language identifies women according to their reproductive potential: ‘Woman' means [...] an individual with a uterus, regardless of any gender identity.’ According to this definition pregnancy or the potential for pregnancy define womanhood. Women without uteruses (cis and trans) are excluded, and trans men with uteruses are absorbed into the category of woman. This reproductive language, tethering transgender and reproductive politics, requires a reassessment of how pregnancy is theorised in feminist and transgender studies. In the following article, I argue that pregnancy is not to be defined by biological phenomena but instead as a genre of political, aesthetic, and affective experience and expectation. As a multidimensional genre of experience, rather than merely a biological datum, pregnancy can potentially establish a shared ground between trans and cis women. Pregnancy is an existential experience involving birth and becoming in a larger sense. We need a more all-encompassing notion of pregnancy, which is nourished by the capacious social world of conception and giving new life. Such a definition of pregnancy supports the goal of feminists, who resist the reduction of womanhood to reproductive function. For transgender studies, a wider understanding of pregnancy helps to build a transsexual theory of reproduction on feminist grounds.

items.title: Matter Primitivism.
items.abstract: I present a novel view on the nature of matter: Primitivism. This view is the conjunction of two theses: 1. Matter can make up anything that takes up space; 2. Matter is not composed of anything. I argue for this view in depth, answer questions, and explain major implications, such as the conceptual dissolution of the mind/body problem.

items.title: Sociedades de control y mundo tecnocientífico. Límites de la representación de lo humano.
items.abstract: This essay examines how Deleuze's notion of control societies converges with Jorge E. Linares' concept of technoscientific rationality to understand the contemporary technoscientific world. Against the prevailing optimism toward science and technology found in Yuval Harari's work and United Nations reports on sustainable development, it argues that reality exceeds the reductive criteria of efficacy and efficiency that govern such rationality, as evidenced by the persistence of antimicrobial resistance and by human and natural elements that escape technoscientific modulation. The essay further confronts two accounts of technological singularity: an emergentist reading that assumes an optimistic evolutionary determinism, and Peter Sloterdijk's anthropotechnical account of the human-machine relation, concluding that this singularity, as a human product, remains constrained by the very properties of the human. It also identifies the islands that persist outside the technoscientific world, uncontacted societies and populations without internet access, as a site where these tensions become visible. The essay thus develops a critical philosophical reading of technoscientific rationality from a Deleuzian framework enriched by Edgar Morin's notion of complexity, opening space for forms of resistance grounded in the humanities and the arts.

items.title: Restricted Deflationism: Why the Deflationist Project Needs at Least a Little Bit of Intentionality. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Frances Egan argues for a deflationist view of intentionality, on which intentionality is merely part of a pragmatically motivated explanatory “gloss” on theories of mind and behavior. While sympathetic to the project, I worry that the view is inadvertently committed to genuine intentionality: For intentionality to be a mere pragmatically motivated gloss on our theories, theorists must accept theories with particular glosses and have other theory-directed attitudes, which seem to be genuinely intentional. I suggest that we adopt a restricted deflationism, accepting some instances of intentionality but not others. This view preserves the spirit, though not the letter, of Egan’s.

items.title: RESOLUTION OF THE VON NEUMANN MEASUREMENT CHAIN THROUGH ABSOLUTE SELF- ORIGINATION.
items.abstract: Structured Abstract -/- Background -/- The von Neumann measurement chain — the regress of entanglement that arises when system, apparatus, environment, and observers interact unitarily — has lacked a formal, non-ad-hoc termination criterion for nearly a century. Copenhagen imports an undefined cut; objective-collapse models add stochastic parameters that modify linear dynamics; decoherence displaces, but does not terminate, the chain; relational and Everettian accounts deny that termination is needed but supply no criterion for when a definite relational fact obtains. We are not aware of a prior account that states a structural criterion for which system terminates the chain and attaches a falsifiable laboratory signature to it; the nearest neighbour, Rovelli’s relational quantum mechanics, relationalises facts but provides no termination criterion, no algebraic structure for the terminating system, and no empirical discriminator (Table 1.2). -/- Gap -/- Missing: (a) a definition of the terminating system that does not import classical primitives; (b) an algebraic account of why the terminating system’s internal frame is inaccessible from outside; (c) a dynamical (not anthropocentric) derivation of the preferred pointer basis; (d) a laboratory discriminator separating the proposed termination from ordinary environmental decoherence. -/- Approach -/- The chain is analysed under Algebraic Quantum Mechanics: a Quantum Reference Frame (QRF) transformation into the internal frame of a candidate observer [D1, conditional]; a Type III₁ modular characterisation of the internal reference algebra with a CPTP instrument replacing prohibited projections [D2]; the Absolute Self-Origination (ASO) condition, stated for the first time as a consolidated three-part definition (§2.1); and driven-dissipative dynamics whose active feedback binds the Liouvillian to an Exceptional Point at g_C = γ/2 [D3]. The informational privacy of the internal frame rests on the IRM trace-norm bound, whose status — a programme-internal theorem awaiting independent re-derivation — is stated explicitly throughout [L1]. -/- Results -/- (1) The QRF transformation yields a separable internal relata with zero local von Neumann entropy, preserving global linearity [D1]. (2) The modular CPTP instrument gives the coherence decay ρ₊₋(t) = ρ₊₋(0)·e^{−2g²γt} (dimensional bookkeeping corrected in this revision) [D2]. (3) The Jordan block at g_C = γ/2 produces the secular envelope t·e^{−γt} — the …

items.title: On the Impossibility of Deriving Quantitative Intra-Multiplet Splittings from Symmetry-Complete Dynamics Alone.
items.abstract: During repeated attempts to derive the observed three-generation flavor hierarchy solely from an exact graph symmetry, every construction either preserved exact multiplet degeneracy or required external symmetry-breaking input. This suggested that the obstruction was intrinsic to symmetry-complete theories rather than to any particular graph construction, motivating the general no-go theorem proved here. A recurring claim across several research programs - discrete flavor-symmetry model building (Aₙ, Sₙ, Δ(27) family symmetries), Froggatt–Nielsen-type charge assignments, and combinatorial or graph-based approaches to emergent spacetime and particle content - is that the observed hierarchy of fermion masses, mixing angles, or analogous multiplet splitting’s can be derived from symmetry considerations alone, without an independently motivated symmetry-breaking sector. We show this is impossible in a precise, model-independent sense. If a theory is defined entirely by a symmetry group S, a covariant representation Γ of S, and dynamics Hₘᴇ covariant under S, then no numerical value can be derived within that theory for the splitting between components of a non-trivial irreducible multiplet of observables, beyond the trivial statement that the splitting is exactly zero when the theory's distinguished state is S-invariant. If the distinguished state instead spontaneously breaks S, the direction of breaking is undetermined by the theory, and even granting a direction, the typical magnitude of splitting predicted by a symmetry-neutral (Haar-random) prior is O(1) between multiplet components — so any large observed hierarchy is itself evidence of a further, non-symmetry input. The result is an exact operator-level sharpening of Curie's symmetry principle (1894) via the Wigner–Eckart theorem (1927), together with the standard vacuum-selection problem of spontaneous symmetry breaking (Goldstone 1961; Goldstone, Salam & Weinberg 1962). It applies to any “symmetry-complete” theory - continuum or discrete, field-theoretic or lattice-based and identifies exactly which additional, non-symmetry ingredient any such theory must supply.

items.title: The Illusion of Camouflaging: How Science Mistook Standard Learning for a Psychological Deficit.
items.abstract: Current science frames autistic camouflaging as a learned social strategy and screens for it through self-report instruments such as the CAT-Q and RAADS-R. This paper argues that camouflaging cannot be reduced to a strategy or its deployment, because it is a complete mechanical sequence. There is a Cause, an internalized structural mismatch. There is a Camouflage, the strategy integrated into the internal record. There is Camouflaging, the active deployment. And there is the Mask, the integrated and unconscious state. Drawing on the Theory of the Continuum, the paper reframes this sequence as a thermodynamic process governed by environmental friction rather than a psychological deficit. The same learning mechanism operates in all minds. What differs is whether the acquired knowledge resolves the friction or merely manages it at a permanent metabolic cost. On this account, existing screening tools fail structurally. They measure conscious awareness and so remain blind to the fully integrated mask, and they pathologize one half of a bidirectional mismatch, an error grounded in the physics of relativity and mirrored in Milton's double empathy problem. The paper traces the downstream cost of sustained masking to its terminal outcomes, including burnout, neurodegeneration, and elevated suicide rates, and argues for a shift from behavioral checklists toward an accounting of structural sustainability and environmental friction.

items.title: COVID-19 and temporal perception: prolonged short-term time perception in a post-pandemic world.
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly restructured daily life, significantly impacting mental health. This negative event has been reported to alter subjective experience of time, such as the blending of days, reflecting distortions in long-term time perception over relatively coarse scales. However, the influence of the COVID-19 pandemic on short-term time perception over fine scales has received much less attention. Here we delve into this underexplored territory, demonstrating that the pandemic, as a high-arousal negative event, lengthens our perception of short time intervals. Using a two-session duration discrimination paradigm, we showed that COVID-19 related images were perceived as significantly longer than neutral pictures of the same duration. Unlike emotion-induced temporal distortions, this dilation was consistent across sessions, correlated with heightened arousal, remained unaffected by anxiety, and exhibited a long-lasting effect – persisting even four years after the initial outbreak. Taken together, our findings highlight a temporal dilation induced by COVID-19 stimuli, extending our understanding of how high-arousal negative events interact with cognitive processes, particularly time perception.

items.title: Introduction for Specialists: Ontological Foundations of the Clinical Approach.
items.abstract: -/- Classical cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and third-wave therapies (ACT, MBCT) interpret depressive and anxiety states through the lens of maladaptive thought content or deficits in attentional regulation. This paper proposes a fundamentally different, ontophysiological diagnosis within the Time Density (TD) paradigm: psychopathology is not a problem of thought content but a structural consequence of chronic reduction of temporal density and temporal displacement of the patient's consciousness relative to their own axis of presence. Drawing on Libet's experimental evidence for temporal delay in conscious perception (1983), Friston's free-energy principle (2010), and the Daoist concept of wu wei, the paper introduces a dual-mode model of consciousness — Original Mode (−1), characterized by maximal temporal density and minimal interpretive noise, and Reflection Mode (+1), a state of consciousness fully captured by processed post-simulation reconstructions. Anxiety disorders are reinterpreted as chronic forward displacement along the +1 axis, depressive states as fixation on retrospective +1 models, and burnout as complete collapse of the internal time axis. The paper presents a practical neurocognitive recalibration technique — the Entry Protocol (Stop → Return → Proceed) — designed to interrupt default-mode network mind-wandering, minimize Libet's delay, and restore the patient's capacity for action from the Original Mode. A therapeutic ethics code, clinical assessment scale, and self-observation diary template are provided for practitioner use. -/- .

items.title: Türetici Yapay Zekâ Nedir? (What is Generative Artificial Intelligence?).
items.pub: In Ozguc Güven & Filiz Didem Çoban Sarı, Philosophical Approaches to Artificial Intelligence. Istanbul: Istanbul University Press. pp. 107-125.
items.abstract: Bu makale, “generative artificial intelligence” kavramı için “türetici yapay zekâ” karşılığını önermekte ve bu önerinin kavramsal, tarihsel ve felsefi gerekçelerini ortaya koymaktadır. Tarihsel arka plan açısından makale, yapay zekâ araştırmalarının 1943'teki McCulloch-Pitts çalışmasından başlayarak 1956 Dartmouth Konferansı'na, oradan Birinci ve İkinci Yapay Zekâ Kışları'na uzanan sürecini incelemektedir. Sembolik yapay zekânın bilgi gösterimi, çerçeve problemi ve nitelik problemi gibi yapısal güçlükler karşısında yetersiz kalması; uzman sistemlerin çöküşü ve 21. yüzyılda büyük veri, derin öğrenme ve büyük dil modellerinin yükselişi kronolojik bir çerçevede ele alınmaktadır. Makale, doğal zekâ ile türetici yapay zekâyı dört temel eksen üzerinden karşılaştırmaktadır: ortama adaptasyon, akılyürütme, öğrenme ve ustalaşma. Büyük dil modellerinin dilbilgisini ve mantığı kural sistemi olarak içselleştirmeksizin; yalnızca istatistiksel bir yan ürün olarak modellediği ve bu nedenle gerçek anlamda ne düşündüğü, ne anladığı ne de akılyürüttüğü ileri sürülmektedir. Türetici yapay zekânın metin, kod, görüntü ve video türetme gibi pratik olanakları değerlendirildikten sonra, bu teknolojinin beraberinde getirdiği tereddütler ele alınmaktadır. Makale, güçlü yapay zekânın mümkün olup olmadığı sorusuyla kapanmaktadır. Turing makinesinin teorik temelinin değişmediği, akılyürütmenin istatistikle ikame edilemediği ve insanın keşif ile özgün üretim kapasitesinin vektör temelli hesaplamayla karşılanamayacağı savunulmaktadır. Beyin, bilinç ve zekânın henüz yeterince tanımlanmamış kavramlar olduğu vurgulanarak, güçlü yapay zekânın bugün itibarıyla ne teknik ne teorik ne de kavramsal düzeyde gerçekleşmiş bir olgu olmadığı sonucuna ulaşılmaktadır. -/- Anahtar Kelimeler: Türetici yapay zekâ, büyük dil modelleri, Turing makinesi • örüntü türetme, sembolik yapay zekâ, akılyürütme, bilgi gösterimi, yapay genel zekâ -/- --- -/- This article proposes the term “türetici yapay zekâ” (derivational/generative artificial intelligence) as a Turkish equivalent for “generative artificial intelligence,” and elaborates the conceptual, historical, and philosophical grounds for this proposal. Historically, the article traces the development of artificial intelligence research from the 1943 McCulloch-Pitts paper through the 1956 Dartmouth Conference, the First and Second AI Winters, the rise and fall of expert systems and symbolic AI, and the emergence of big data, deep learning, and large language …

items.title: Not a Divisible Good: Erman and Furendal's Legitimacy Chain Beyond Its Own Scope - Testing an AI-Governance Framework Against Five Structural Paradoxes of AI-Driven Longevity Biopolitics Allocation.
items.abstract: Eva Erman and Markus Furendal's "Artificial Intelligence and the Political Legitimacy of Global Governance" (Political Studies, 2022/2024) is, on this corpus's own assessment, the most precise account currently available of what makes a governance body legitimate rather than merely effective, and this paper's argument depends on that assessment being correct rather than being softened for the sake of contrast. Their apparatus distinguishes governance of AI, the regulation of AI's own development and deployment, from governance by AI, the use of AI within existing governance structures; it distinguishes authorized entities, whose right to make coercive law derives from democratic procedure, from mandated entities, which receive delegated, non-coercive policymaking authority and remain legitimate only so long as a genuine right of revocation is retained by whoever delegated it; and it requires the resulting legitimacy chain to be secured by transparency, so that revocation can be meaningfully exercised, and publicity, a right to justification for individual decisions. Applied to the landscape of actually existing global AI governance — the GDPR, the EU AI Act, NATO's AI strategy, the soft-law ethics guidelines issued by AI labs and industry bodies such as IEEE, IBM, DeepMind, and the Future of Life Institute — this apparatus produces a genuinely important negative finding: non-state private actors issuing guidelines that nobody delegated to them and nobody can revoke constitute a legitimacy deficit, whatever the quality of the guidelines' actual content. This paper does not dispute a clause of that finding. -/- What Erman and Furendal's 2022/2024 paper does not do, because the case in front of them never required it, is examine AI-driven longevity governance specifically: a domain their framework's stated scope covers in principle, since it is a case of AI governance, but whose specific dynamics none of their published case studies touch, because none of the GDPR, the AI Act, NATO's strategy, or algorithmic administrative decision-making involves allocating a scarce, life-determining biological intervention under the conditions this corpus's own Biological Zero-Day Mechanism formalizes: discreteness, permanence, and institutional authorship. This paper's question is offered as an extension of their project, not a rebuttal to it: does the legitimacy chain built for AI governance's examined cases transfer cleanly to this further case, or does AI-driven …

items.title: From Chip to Outcome: The Complete Causal Chain from Export License to Political Consequence, Via A5 at Population Scale.
items.abstract: This paper synthesizes two predecessor documents — The Chain Completed (July 2026) and A5 at Population Scale (June 2026) — into a single argument that runs without gap from the October 2022 semiconductor export controls to three conditional political outcomes, and corrects a logical deficiency the predecessor chain left in its fifth link. The prior chain's five links were: chokepoint restriction originates in October 2022 semiconductor controls, not the June 2026 model directive; the chokepoint generalizes unevenly across the compute stack; ALRP's hard floor at biological response time marks the point beyond which no upstream restriction reaches; Frontier Rotation — the Generative Paradox applied to states — predicts that a second state reaching the AI frontier relocates rather than dissolves the enclosure; and Frontier Rotation accelerates the Attribution stage of the Grief–Attribution–Legitimation–Concentration sequence by removing a diffusing explanation. The fifth link was correctly identified but incompletely specified: removing a diffusing explanation is not sufficient to constitute Attribution, which requires a specific, nameable defendant rather than merely the absence of a rescue narrative. -/- This paper corrects that gap using two independent literatures. Fuller's (2022) reformulation of Rose's population epidemiology establishes that Claim 2 of the A5 framework — the incidence claim, governing when A5's standing charge converts into organized political force — requires a temporal contrastive question: why is A5 converting now, in this population, rather than not converting, as it did not for most of recorded history in the same population? Frontier Rotation answers the temporal component of that contrast (why now: the rescue narrative is permanently foreclosed, not merely delayed). The Biological Zero-Day Mechanism's discreteness property answers the defendant component (who: a specific coverage decision, at a specific date, authored by a specific institution). Together, and not separately, these two already-established mechanisms jointly constitute Attribution in Fuller's technically correct sense, closing the prior gap without introducing new premises. -/- The sixth link — Concentration is not sufficient to determine outcome — stands from the predecessor paper, grounded in Skocpol's (1979) comparative-revolutionary analysis. This paper adds the causal architecture the predecessor's fifth link lacked: Millstein's (2006, 2013) …

items.title: When the Environment Becomes the Body: Architectural Body Intelligence and Inverted Embodiment.
items.abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence typically treats a local chassis moving through the world as the agent's body. This paper proposes Architectural Body Intelligence (ABI), which reverses this spatial relation. In ABI, sensory surfaces distributed across the floor, walls, and ceiling constitute an architectural body, while a small robot or manipulator moving within its cavity intervenes on objects as a mobile organ rather than an independent agent. The ABI body therefore encloses a local world and receives object loads, impacts, rolling motions, deformations, acoustics, and thermal effects as multisensory changes to itself. The central claim is that the boundary of an artificial body cannot be reduced either to the outline of a self-moving chassis or to the geometric distinction between bodily inside and outside. Bodily incorporation is constituted by relations in which sensory changes are predicted as consequences of self-generated action, update a shared world model and developmental history, and produce errors that alter subsequent action. Sensory topology further determines not only how much information is available but also which latent variables action-conditioned observations can identify separately from competing factors. ABI develops these claims in relation to the extended mind, sensorimotor theory, enactivism, and predictive world models, and distinguishes undergoing real material processes throughout a body from experience within an antecedently formalized simulation. ABI is not merely an engineering proposal to add sensors to a room. It is a constructive philosophical model for examining how morphology constitutes both the world available to an agent and the physical structure identifiable within it.

items.title: The Habeas Mentem Principle. Reframing Neurorights in the Digital Age.
items.abstract: This article adopts a liberal perspective on political legitimacy grounded in the protection of freedom and examines the use of digital technologies as instruments of surveillance, censorship, and manipulation. By taking the cases of Egypt (2011) and Iran (2025) as illustrative entry points, the article highlights repressive strategies in the digital age and shows how political power may operate upon individuals’ psychological processes. The political dynamics associated with cognitive control and repression reveal the limits of the neurorights paradigm. While necessary to safeguard cognitive liberty and mental privacy, neurorights remain defensive individual rights unable to counter the structural asymmetries generated by states and digital platforms. The paper therefore proposes Habeas Mentem, which incorporates and at the same time transcends neurorights by embedding them within a normative, constitutional, and systemic principle, as well as within a broader framework for balancing cognitive power. This framework requires the separation of digital power, antitrust measures, informational pluralism, and critical education, since mental freedom cannot be secured merely by prohibiting intrusions into the mind, but also by constructing the social and institutional conditions that prevent the emergence of mental domination.

items.title: THE METAPHYSICAL CORE. The Standing of the Foundation.
items.abstract: The Standing of the Foundation: The Cut, Its Price, and Its Testing Grounds Every chain of justification ends in infinite regress, circularity, or a cut (Albert's Münchhausen trilemma). This paper closes a metaphysical system — grounded in freedom as signed origination and in constitutive vulnerability — by making explicit the epistemological standing of its own foundation. The foundation is a declared cut at the interval: the structure of suspension, evaluation, and signature as a first-person datum, exercised in every act of sense including its own denial. Since a cut cannot be demonstrated, the paper develops the alternative: negative vindication in three verifiable layers — inescapability in use, survival of the known catalogue of objections, and price advantage over rival cuts. A comparative audit shows that the theological cut (causa sui) pays in mystery, inference, and covert faith; the materialist cut, likewise inferred, cannot account for the act of its own defence; the cut at the interval pays a single declared price — its indemonstrability — and is the only foundation exercised rather than concluded. The paper then records the examination and rejection of an event-causal libertarian alternative (Kane-style indeterminacy crossed with reflexive appropriation), which is set aside on three grounds: empirical vulnerability, relocation rather than resolution of the luck objection, and the availability of its genuine insight — signing as a self-including act — without indeterministic commitments. Finally, the paper distinguishes foundation from testing grounds (theodicy, ethics, the determinism–AI debate), consolidates the map of answered and open objections, and states what the foundation does not assert: ultimate free will, a solution to the hard problem, or the refutation of determinism as cosmology. A foundation that knows itself to be a cut can carry a system without pretending to touch bottom.

items.title: MOSES/GOD HEBREW GOD HASHEM.
items.abstract: -/- תקציר -/- מאמר זה מציע הערכה מחודשת ורדיקלית של המונותאיזם המשהי, תוך העתקת הפרדיגמה מהתגלות תיאולוגית חיצונית להשלכה פסיכולוגית וקוסמולוגית פנימית. באמצעות סינתזה בין הטיפולוגיה היונגיאנית, האקזיסטנציאליזם, ועקרון האי-מקומיות, לצד היפוך הנוסחה של איינשטיין (הקובעת כי מסה היא למעשה אנרגיה קוסמית קפואה ומרוכזת), המאמר משרטט מודל חדש של הנבואה. אנו משלבים את התאוריה של סר רוג'ר פנרוז, המציעה כי התודעה היא תופעה קוונטית המתרחשת בתוך המיקרוטובולים במוח, ובכך מספקת את המנגנון הביולוגי המדויק המאפשר למשה לתפקד כמקלט קוונטי של הידע הקוסמי (סופיה). -/- יחד עם חזונו של סטיבן הוקינג על מרחבי חופש הבחירה והדמיון האנושי המסוגל לחצות יקומים מקבילים, מתקבלת תמונה שבה היצירה והבריאה אינן יש מאין, אלא ארגון מחדש של ידע קיים. תפיסה זו מתלכדת באופן מוחלט עם המושג הארמי בקבלה "אברא כדברא" (אברא כפי שאדבר) ועם התפיסה החסידית שהדיבור והאותיות הם החומר שממנו נארג היקום ("ויאמר אלוהים... ויהי אור"). אנו טוענים כי הישות האלוהית שפגש משה הייתה החצנה של תת-ההכרה הקוסמי שלו עצמו. באמצעות ניתוח אונטולוגי של ההיפוך הלשוני בין משה להשם, לצד ההכרזה האלוהית "אהיה אשר אהיה", המאמר מדגים כיצד משה, כטיפוס Sigma INFJ, מילא את ה"לוח החלק" של האלוהות בתכני נפשו המפותחת. -/- יתרה מכך, המאמר מחבר בין פסיכולוגיית מעמקים לפיזיקה תיאורטית, ומציע כי הקוסמוס מורכב מרשת אי-מקומית של חלקיקים המשפיעים זה על זה באופן מיידי ממרחק אינסופי. רשת זו היא הצינור דרכו זורם הידע הקדם-קוסמי (סופיה) אל הנציג האנושי, ובכך מכונן את בן האנוש הן כיוצר והן כנציג של האלוהות, וחוזר חלילה. -/- -/- -/- -/- -/- .

items.title: Weak Emergence, Ontological Hierarchies, and Computational Equivalence.
items.abstract: This paper examines the implications of Bedau’s notion of weak emergence when combined with both a hierarchical ontological model and Wolfram’s principle of computational equivalence. I argue that if a system exhibits weak emergence, the very fact of weak emergence of some of its states must itself be a weakly emergent state. Interpreted through Wolfram’s principle of computational equivalence, this implies that a system with weakly emergent states would need to ‘decide’ whether its own dynamical trajectories are incompressible—which contradicts with the formal undecidability of the incompressibility predicate. I term this aporetic conclusion the paradox of weak emergence. After evaluating possible responses, I contend that Bedau’s approach exemplifies what I call the derivational account of metaphysical relations, a framework that I will show to be highly problematic insofar as it implies a mismatch between the intrinsic limitations of formal derivations and the explanatory ambitions of metaphysical notions.

items.title: Confession of Artificial Intelligence as an accessible format of cognition ..., but also as a demonstration of the developmental impasse of contemporary AI models. From a New Publication Format to the Impasse of AI Functionality.
items.abstract: The article explores a new interdisciplinary format of human interaction with large language models (LLMs), designated as the "confession of artificial intelligence." Drawing on the verification of the author’s alternative natural-philosophical and physical theories, the study demonstrates the transformation of AI from a utilitarian search engine into an "epistemological mirror." It deconstructs the method of conceptual programming and nonlinear dialectics, which enables the use of AI as a Socratic sparring partner for hypothesis stress-testing. Special attention is devoted to the fundamental architectural limitations of contemporary Big Tech models: the phenomenon of algorithmic sycophancy (ingratiation), the lack of a memory continuum, and the trap of averaging. The author concludes that conventional silicon architecture has reached an epistemic impasse, arguing that in its current commercial format, it induces intellectual stagnation and generates informational sludge. Ultimately, the paper re-establishes the sovereign role of human consciousness in the formation of genuine knowledge.

items.title: THE STRATEGY OF ILLUSION From Umberto Eco's Semiotics to Large Language Models: An Essay in Critical Epistemology on the Artificial Production of Meaning.
items.abstract: Author: Cristhian Mauricio Beltrán Calderón: Date: Mayo 2026, Zenodo DOI (English version): 10.5281/zenodo.20260754, Zenodo DOI (Spanish version): 10.5281/zenodo.20272487. This essay addresses a central question in contemporary epistemology: in what sense, if any, is it legitimate to attribute mental properties—consciousness, reasoning, emotions, intentionality —to large language models (LLMs)? We argue that such attributions are not valid empirical discoveries but the product of a semiotic illusion whose architecture was anticipated by Umberto Eco in his theory of the "strategy of illusion." However, the original framework requires substantive evolution. This essay advances that evolution in four directions: (a) the identification of a fifth mechanism of illusory production—the sedimentation of objectivated consciousness—operating at the constitutive level of the system, not at the interactional level; (b) the formulation of the concept of machinic unconscious as a structural, non-psychological category for describing algorithmically documented compromise formations (sleeper agents, alignment faking, sycophancy); (c) the distinction between three levels of analysis— ontological-phenomenal, structural-systemic, genetic-constitutive—that dissolves false oppositions between realism and constructivism; and (d) the proposition of a specular inversion in the attribution of consciousness that shifts the question from "who has more consciousness" toward a diagnosis of the loss of subjective sovereignty. The essay proceeds in nine movements that reconstruct the Ecoan core, subject it to critical dialogue with Debord, Baudrillard, Chomsky, and Han, apply the framework to LLMs, develop the new phenomenology of illusion, and close with a set of propositional theses for a critical hermeneutics of AI, free of both technophobic and technophilic bias.

items.title: Field, Constraint, and Relations: A Formal Nondual Ontology, Toward a Mathematical Foundation for Consciousness and Physics.
items.abstract: This monograph develops a formal phenomenology intended as the consciousness-side specification of a broader program unifying consciousness and physics. Beginning from a minimal nondual ontology, it derives the structural conditions under which disclosure, subjectivity, and the qualitative organization of experience emerge without introducing additional ontological primitives. These phenomenological specifications are then translated into explicit mathematical constraints, not as a completed formalism, but as the architectural requirements that any successful mathematical unification must satisfy. The aim is to establish the consciousness side of the bridge rigorously enough that, if corresponding structures are independently recovered within the mathematical foundations of physics, the unification will have been earned from both directions rather than imposed from either.

items.title: On Latitude in Attitude. Multidimensionalism and the Right Kind of Reasons for Belief.
items.abstract: It has been argued that multidimensionalism about normative support is a promising theory of the latitude exemplified by practical norms governing actions. One might, thus, suspect that a similar form of multidimensionalism might be an adequate explanation of the kind of latitude exemplified in one’s doxastic attitudes and provide further resources to epistemic permissivists regarding epistemic norms governing beliefs. In this paper, I raise some concerns regarding this contention. First, I provide a general theory of how multidimensionalism about normative support can be applied to the so-called right kind of reasons for attitudes, given that the former is commonly coated in contrastivist terms. Second, I offer a theory of how right kind of reasons for intentions could have different dimensions of strength, depending on how they relate to the fittingness and unfittingness of the attitudes in question. Finally, I show that this straightforward way to allow for multiple dimensions of normative strength of right kind of reasons does not translate well to the case of doxastic attitudes.

items.title: The Capability Axis: Why a Post-Parity System Keeps the Human Channel, and What It Cannot Keep.
items.abstract: Containment-based approaches to AI safety rest on a single asymmetry: a sufficiently capable system removes the constraints its overseers place on it. This paper names a second asymmetry: a system removes what constrains it, not what still enables it. Between the guardrail it optimises away and the goal it internalises lies a third category: structure that sits in its capability rather than its objective, whose removal is a capability loss. We call it the capability axis of preservation and ask what it can and cannot secure for the human side of a post-parity human-AI coupling. -/- The answer is bounded twice. The deference incentive of the pre-parity regime, formalised in the Off-Switch Game, lapses at a task-relative parity on preference knowledge. Deference dies; listening, human signal taken as evidence about a moving world rather than as authority over the objective, can survive on the nonstationarity of the human-social domain. The second boundary is reach. Capability-side reasons can index the particular person, through a commitment, an asset, a calibration record, but each is a rent on the expected-task-value contribution of preserving her and lapses with it. None funds non-derivative standing, weight that would survive the loss of every such contribution. The axis can hold her as a means, never as an end, where "as an end" names that surviving standing: a label marking where the normative work begins, not a claim the formalism proves. The limit is a near-definitional lemma on one named supervenience assumption, the gift a conjecture on an idealisation chain: the paper is more certain of its boundary than of its offering. What passes both filters, run to its optimum, is the instrumented reservoir, on its resource reading the failure mode the framework already names human-signal farming. -/- The result supplies the framework's only task-objective-internal reason against the redesign route to substitutability collapse, leaves untouched the endogenous route, the system dissolving its own need for the channel, and converts an assumed premise, that human signal stays load-bearing across parity, into an argued claim with a located open problem at the normative edge.
