items.title: Omega — Sprint 5 Experimental Persistencia Regenerativa y Reconstrucción Organizativa.
items.abstract: Omega constituye un programa de investigación experimental orientado inicialmente al estudio de la persistencia funcional en agentes artificiales sometidos a procesos extremos de degradación, compresión y reorganización. A lo largo de su desarrollo se construyeron sucesivamente diversos modelos organizativos destinados a explicar la continuidad del sistema, incorporando conceptos como el Hilo de Ariadna, la criptobiosis adaptativa, la reapertura evolutiva y la reconstrucción regenerativa. -/- Sin embargo, el principal resultado del programa no fue la validación progresiva de dichas hipótesis, sino su revisión sistemática a la luz de la evidencia experimental. La persistencia dejó de interpretarse como la conservación de estructuras específicas, de identidades organizativas o de mecanismos particulares, para aparecer como una propiedad emergente asociada a determinados regímenes capaces de recuperar organización funcional tras perturbaciones severas. En este proceso, la unidad explicativa del modelo se desplazó progresivamente desde el agente hacia el propio régimen organizativo. -/- Este cambio de perspectiva transformó también la naturaleza de la pregunta científica. Omega comenzó buscando identificar qué estructura era responsable de la persistencia; terminó mostrando que la cuestión relevante no era qué persiste, sino qué propiedades permiten que un régimen vuelva a organizarse tras haber dejado de ser lo que era. Más que proporcionar una teoría definitiva de la persistencia, el programa delimitó experimentalmente las restricciones que cualquier explicación futura deberá satisfacer y estableció un conjunto coherente de resultados sobre los que podrá construirse un desarrollo teórico posterior. -/- Omega no concluye resolviendo el problema de la persistencia; concluye reformulando con mayor precisión cuál era el problema que debía resolverse.

items.title: Simple Beauty.
items.abstract: I argue that some simple things are aesthetically valuable, or beautiful. I give an account of simple beauty as beauty in simplicity. I then address some suspicions about simple beauty. Some people allege that simple beauty is at odds with aesthetic agency. In fact, I argue, simple beauty promotes certain kinds of aesthetic agency. Others allege that simple things do not warrant sustained appreciation. I argue that simple beauties present existential truths that warrant sustained awareness because of their importance and our forgetfulness.

items.title: From cognitive malaise to erotic stagnation: reforming the functional view in light of sexual boredom.
items.abstract: This commentary proposes a minor revision of the functional account of boredom developed by Andreas Elpidorou in The Anatomy of Boredom. While I endorse the core insight that boredom is an aversive, informative, and motivational state that regulates our engagements with the world, I argue that restricting this regulatory function to cognition renders the account incomplete. The central claim is that sexual boredom constitutes a genuine instance of state boredom that falls outside the cognitive scope of the original framework, thereby motivating its expansion. Drawing on empirical research, I characterize sexual boredom as a temporary, context-dependent affective state arising from suboptimal sexual engagement. Like cognitive boredom, it involves an aversive phenomenology, conveys information about inadequate engagement, and motivates behavioral change. However, its target domain is sexual/bodily rather than cognitive engagement, indicating that boredom’s regulatory function is not exhausted by cognition. The analysis further situates sexual boredom within broader concerns about well-being and feminist critiques of pornography, extending the political and existential dimensions already emphasized in Elpidorou’s account. The proposed revision is minimal: boredom should be understood as regulating engagement simpliciter, encompassing both cognitive and non-cognitive domains. This preserves the explanatory strengths of the functional view while broadening its scope.

items.title: From Character to Soul Purpose: Alan Leo, Dane Rudhyar and the Progressive Unfolding of Esoteric Astrology.
items.abstract: This investigation is undertaken within the framework of the esoteric astrology presented through Alice A. Bailey and the Tibetan teacher Djwhal Khul, whose writings provide the primary conceptual foundation for the questions explored here. Modern esoteric astrology represents a progressive unfolding: Alan Leo was a principal initiator of the movement from predictive astrology toward the study of character and evolutionary development; Dane Rudhyar developed the birth chart as an archetypal pattern of becoming; and Bailey/DK extended the field into a presentation of astrology as a science of soul purpose, rays, initiation, and planetary relationships. Within this context, esoteric rectification becomes the search for the true symbolic signature of incarnation. The history of modern astrology can be viewed as a gradual movement from the interpretation of celestial influence as external fate toward an understanding of astrology as a symbolic language of consciousness, evolution, and purpose. This transition did not occur through a single revelation, but through a succession of individuals who prepared different aspects of the field.

items.title: Three Separations, One Method: A Vertical Demonstration Across the Identity–Persistence Program.
items.abstract: This paper presents three formal separation theorems within the Identity–Persistence Program and uses them to demonstrate the program’s general proof methodology. The results establish that identity does not entail recognition, identity does not entail admissibility, and persistence does not entail stability. Rather than relying on conceptual distinctions alone, each separation is established through explicit constructions together with declared structural assumptions. -/- The paper also makes explicit a proof procedure employed implicitly throughout the broader corpus. Each analysis proceeds by declaring the relevant level of evaluation, identifying the forced structural role, constructing a separating model, determining the declaration required for any legitimate collapse of the distinction, and classifying the remaining uncertainty. The resulting method provides a reproducible framework for analyzing structural distinctions while maintaining explicit claim-status discipline. -/- The paper introduces no new forcing theorem and does not claim methodological exhaustiveness. Instead, it functions as a methods-layer companion to the Identity–Persistence Program, connecting its foundational papers into a unified workflow while identifying the Aboutness Lemma and the Minimal Decision Record as separate future developments.

items.title: The Root of the Demand: What Bounded Verdict Agreement Is, What It Is Not, and Why Boundedness, Answerability and Co-Declaration Do Not Entail It.
items.abstract: What makes a demand for bounded verdict agreement satisfiable, and what premises entail it? This paper distinguishes a declared standard from the outcomes evaluators can actually return. Boundedness, answerability, and answerability together with co-declaration do not, by themselves, entail determinate agreement. -/- For a declared verification task, the paper proves an exact characterization: every admitted run returns a determinate verdict and all requested comparisons agree if and only if, within each class of the equivalence generated by those comparisons, the union of possible outcomes is a singleton contained in the determinate verdict set. The result assumes nonempty procedure and outcome families and interprets agreement robustly over all possible outcomes, including same-case comparisons. Requested comparisons admit a corresponding kernel characterization. -/- Agreement, correctness, and substantive decision are separate properties. Evaluators can agree uniformly on an incorrect answer, while agreement on UNDEFINED can satisfy the demand without deciding any substantive case. The paper distinguishes prescribed evaluation from robust pointwise, uniform, and universal correctness, and proves that the latter three coincide under determinate agreement. It also characterizes zero-error decoding through observation fibers and gives a finite-family diagonal separation between per-case availability of a correct procedure and the existence of one listed procedure correct everywhere. -/- These results identify what agreement requires without treating declaration as execution, agreement as correctness, or an observed successful run as certification of all possible outcomes. The paper supplies explicit countermodels, records corrections to predecessor claims, and includes reproducibility checks with declared finite scope. It establishes no specification-floor implication; such an implication requires a separate theorem with explicit premises.

items.title: The Memory Economy: Memory as a Realization of Persistence Under a Declared Regime.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural interpretation of memory within the Identity–Persistence Program. Rather than treating memory as a primitive, it derives persistence as the structural object required whenever bounded observers repeatedly evaluate admissible states under a declared regime. A definitional impossibility argument (the Recurrence Lemma) shows that, without recurrence, persistence is not distinguishable from storage as a separate operation. Memory is then interpreted as one realization of persistence—specifically replay—rather than as a foundational concept. -/- The paper distinguishes search, certification, persistence, replay, and memory as separate computational operations, arguing that declarations change the computational object being evaluated rather than simplifying the underlying domain. Replay is consequently interpreted as avoiding repeated discovery while remaining subject to renewed certification under the declared regime. A minimal structural model derives the economic conditions under which replay becomes preferable to renewed search while admissibility remains sufficiently stable. -/- Mathematics, computation, engineering, and biology are treated as realizations of the same structural role under explicit interpretive discipline. The framework’s derivation is subject-agnostic because it contains no domain-specific predicates, while claims regarding convergent evolution, abiotic persistence, and universality are explicitly classified as consistent evidence or open questions rather than proofs. The paper presents a structural account of memory that situates diverse persistent systems within a common persistence framework while maintaining explicit distinctions between proven results, derived interpretations, empirical evidence, and unresolved questions.

items.title: The Minimal Decision Record: What a Consequential AI Decision Record Must Contain.
items.abstract: This paper presents an applied decision-record schema derived from the Identity-Persistence Program. It asks what a consequential automated decision record must contain so that an independent reviewer can determine what happened without reconstructing missing context. The proposed minimal decision record contains a scope block, an event block, and a completeness audit. The scope block includes at most twelve fields, including a structured operating envelope, and eleven under outcome-equivalence review. The paper distinguishes records from logs: logs report observed behavior, while records declare the governing conditions under which a decision was made. It also distinguishes adjudication-grade records from prediction-grade systems by separating what the system produced from what the declared scope demanded. The paper introduces no new formal theorem; instead, it applies prior formal results to a practical schema and leaves the empirical question—whether such records reduce dispute cost and review time at scale—to pilot validation.

items.title: The Aboutness Lemma: Re-identifiable Content Forces Identity Criteria Within the Answerable Class.
items.abstract: This paper derives the constituent-level result required to close the preconditions conjecture presented in Identity Conditions as Preconditions for Epistemic Operations. Building on The Root of the Demand, which establishes that answerable inquiry forces re-identifiable content, it proves that re-identifiable content requires identity criteria for every constituent of its aboutness structure at a strength determined by the claim’s evaluative reach. The proof proceeds by failure-removal and treats descriptive reference, empty reference, vague reference, and holistic theories of content as relocation rather than elimination cases for identity criteria. Composing this result with the Root theorem yields a within-class theorem: every answerable epistemic operation admits identity criteria, converting the original worked examples into corollaries. The paper further distinguishes the existence of identity criteria from their declaration, preserving the separation between constituent-level semantics and the shared-regime requirements established elsewhere in the Identity-Persistence Program. The remaining boundary questions are explicitly classified as open.

items.title: Definability Computation over Σsuf: Four audited joints, the logic of the finite fragment, and the anti-tupling criterion.
items.abstract: This paper develops the definability-computation layer of the Identity-Persistence Program. Building on the sufficient-regime signature Σsuf, it studies which forced roles remain independently declarable once a theory, declaration form, and admissible equivalence relation are fixed. The paper argues that the finite fragment of the regime theory is naturally formalized in first-order logic with transitive closure, rather than first-order logic alone, because accumulation requires reachability. As a result, countermodel enumeration has a completeness privilege for certifying independence, while explicit definability lacks a Beth-style guarantee. Four role joints are then audited by construction: invariant structure quotients under verdict-inclusive equivalence, target selection remains independent, composition splits into fused accumulation and independent exit semantics, and evaluator access remains independent of authority at envelope scope. The paper also introduces an anti-tupling criterion: role fusion is admissible only when the fused object is forced as one structure by a prior theorem and carries surplus structure beyond the tuple it contains. The result is an index-relative ledger of at most twelve independent declaration slots, or eleven under declared verdict-inclusive equivalence, while the three-class quotient remains an exact conjecture.

items.title: The Necessity of Philosophy: Meaning-Making as the Transcendental Ground of Psychological Advancement.
items.abstract: This treatise defends a single thesis: that no advancement within psychology has been or could be achieved without philosophy, because philosophy is not a contributor to psychology but its necessary condition of possibility. The argument is transcendental. Psychology cannot define its objects, justify its method, set its aims, interpret its findings, or recognize any result as an advance without exercising the philosophical function—the faculty of meaning-making, value-determination, and conceptual legislation. Each of these is presupposed by every psychological result, and none can be supplied by the empirical method alone; therefore, the philosophical function is the transcendental ground of the discipline. The treatise argues further that meaning-making is not merely presupposed but is the active engine of advancement, the guiding faculty by which the human condition is improved at all, since every advance begins in an act of interpretation and is directed by a conception of the better. Yet the psychological academy denies precisely this faculty, treating the measurable half of the person as the whole and dismissing the philosophical self as unreal. This denial is shown to be performatively self-refuting: the thesis that only the empirically testable is admissible is not itself empirically testable, and every act of denying the philosophical function is itself an exercise of it. The remedy proposed is neither annexation nor estrangement but the consilient reunion of the two complementary strands of a single human science.

items.title: Sapolsky’s Error: Hard Determinism, the Denial of the Philosophical Self, and the Reconstruction of Agency Through Developmental Convergence.
items.abstract: In Determined, Robert Sapolsky denies free will, moral responsibility, and the existence of a separate self that authors action, on the ground that human behavior is exhaustively caused by antecedent biology and environment. This treatise argues that Sapolsky’s eliminativism rests upon a twofold error. The first is a category error. The self that Sapolsky refutes is the causa sui, an uncaused causer standing outside the order of causation—a ghost that the philosophical self never claimed to be. The philosophical self is instead a developmental and functional achievement: the cultivated faculty of meaning-making, value-determination, and self-constitution. It is a caused cause rather than an uncaused one, and determinism therefore leaves it untouched. The second error is a performative self-refutation. Sapolsky’s own normative conclusions—that we ought to abolish retributive punishment and cease to blame—are exercises of the very value-determining faculty he declares nonexistent and cannot be derived from his descriptive premises. Drawing upon the author’s developmental reconstruction of selfhood, in particular the Pyramid of Personality and the theory of developmental convergence, and upon the Double Helix model of philosophical and psychological function, the paper reconstructs agency as compatible with determinism: not an exception to causation but its emergent product. The task is not to eliminate the self but to cultivate it.

items.title: Kahneman’s Error: Dual-Process Theory, Instrumental Rationality, and the Foreclosure of the Determination of Ends.
items.abstract: Daniel Kahneman’s heuristics-and-biases program and his dual-process model of cognition transformed the study of human reasoning by mapping the systematic ways in which fast, intuitive judgment (System 1) departs from the norms of slow, deliberative reasoning (System 2). This treatise argues that, for all its achievement, the program rests upon a foreclosure. Its catalog of “errors” and “biases” presupposes a normative standard of rationality, and that standard is purely instrumental: it is the logic of coherence, probability, and expected-utility maximization, which assesses whether means are efficiently fitted to ends while taking the ends themselves as given. Kahneman can therefore certify that an agent reasons correctly toward a goal; he possesses no faculty that determines which goals are worth having. The determination of ends is the office of the philosophical self, and it is absent from the model. By installing instrumental rationality as the standard of good thinking, Kahneman forecloses the philosophical self not by omission, as in Damasio, nor by elimination, as in Sapolsky, but at the level of the norm itself. Drawing upon the author’s Double Helix of Understanding and the multiplicative model of human conduct, the paper proposes a tripartite correction in which the two systems are governed by a philosophical self that evaluates ends. The errors Kahneman catalogs are errors of means; the deeper error is the framework’s inability to recognize an error of ends.

items.title: In Defense of Our Toys: A Comic Treatise on Psychology’s Trespass in the Sandbox of Meaning and the Case for Marriage Counseling or Mutual Restraint.
items.abstract: Psychology, having formally denied the existence of the philosophical self, nevertheless dispatches its most celebrated theorists across the disciplinary fence with remarkable regularity, where they handle meaning, value, identity, consciousness, and the good life with evident enthusiasm before announcing that none of these can be measured and therefore, regrettably, cannot be discussed. This treatise, written in the first person and in a spirit of aggrieved good humor, advances a single thesis: the relationship of psychology to philosophy is best understood not as a rivalry between equals but as a custody dispute over a shared sandbox of toys, in which one party has both moved out of the house and refused to stop playing with the toys it left behind. I reconstruct the historical divorce, in which psychology, seduced by the instruments of empiricism, separated from philosophy and thereafter mistook one half of the human person for the whole of it. I then catalog the contested toys, meaning chief among them, and document the recurring pattern by which psychology borrows each toy, fails to operationalize it, and disowns it while continuing to write about it at considerable and best-selling length. I argue that the present arrangement is intellectually untenable, and I propose two acceptable resolutions: reconciliation through a consilient discipline, here named marriage counseling, or an honest separation in which the toys are returned and each discipline remains in its own sandbox. The unacceptable arrangement, presently in force, is the one we have.

items.title: Are proper functions normative?
items.pub: Theoria. An International Journal for Theory, History and Foundations of Science.
items.venue: Theoria. An International Journal for Theory, History and Foundations of Science
items.abstract: Are proper functions normative? In this paper, I try to answer this question. Acknowledging that the notion of normativity is too ill-defined to afford a categorical yes/no answer, I proceed by attempting to identify arguments for an affirmative answer and trying to articulate what conception of normativity they rely on: what "normativity" has to be, in order for these arguments to work. I identify three arguments for the conclusion that proper functions are *bearer* normative, i.e., normative for the things that have the functions in question. I then propose that two of the arguments may be generalized to the *agentive* case, in defense of the conclusion that proper functions are also, at least in some cases, normative for agents.

items.title: Artworks as Affective Atmospheres: Dufrenne's View of their Aesthetic and Philosophical Significance.
items.pub: Duquesne Studies in Phenomenology 5 (1 (eds. S. Boldsen and T. Roald)).
items.abstract: This article reconstructs and critically evaluates Mikel Dufrenne’s arguments for the claim that our embodied engagement with art is the most fundamental variety of affective experience. I show how, on his account, aesthetic affectivity, or feeling, emerges in aesthetic experience, and identify the central role that aesthetic atmosphere plays in its constitution. I propose an interpretation on which aesthetic feeling, for Dufrenne, is a founded and skilled form of intentional activity that has epistemic (evidence-responsive) and metaphysical (world-disclosive) import. An aesthetic atmosphere, I contend, is an affective and perceptual context that is tied to an artwork and exercises a regulative and normative force over perceivers’ moods, perceptual habits, and cognitive and intentional attitudes. With a view to alternative (topological or thing- like and historicist) interpretations of aesthetic atmospheres, I consider the objections that Dufrenne’s approach is overly subject-centric and overlooks feeling’s dependence on conditions outside consciousness. His account of affectivity’s cosmological character, and his theory of the affective a priori, I contend, largely assuage these worries.

items.title: A New Paradigm for Academic Ecosystems: Institutional Exploration from Argumentative Validation to Intelligent Triage.
items.abstract: Building upon the philosophical argumentation of "The Paradigm Shift in Academic Evaluation: From Textual Provenance to Argumentative Validation," this paper provides a complete set of operational institutional designs, exploring a new paradigm for academic ecosystems that fundamentally transforms academic publishing from the traditional unidirectional power structure of "authors seeking journals" into an open market model of "journals competing for papers." Core designs include: a six-stage submission and review process, an argument-first filtering mechanism, a paper grading and triage system, a journal bidding platform, formatting services and dispute resolution mechanisms, a dual-track appeal system with repairability thresholds, and exemption provisions for high-tier papers (L1/L2). The central innovation of this paper is: AI handles argumentative validation and quality assessment, journals provide formatting services and publication conditions, and authors retain the final right of choice, confirmation, and appeal. This new paradigm transforms academic evaluation from "judgment" to "service," from "passive waiting" to "active choice," and protects paradigm innovation from suppression by conservative forces through institutional design.

items.title: The Participanthood Problem: Identity Under Continued Carrying.
items.abstract: This paper takes up the question that Scrutinized Awareness Theory leaves open: once awareness has crossed into what must be carried, what becomes of the one who carries it? It argues that if identity is the stabilized pattern of what has been carried, continued carrying cannot leave identity unchanged. -/- Participanthood names the continuing transformation of identity under carried implication: the condition in which what has been undergone remains active in continuation as remainder. The paper distinguishes carrying from memory, duration from sequence, remainder from trauma and narrative, and answerability from mere causal effect. -/- Drawing on Parfit, Williams, Bergson, Brison, Butler, Schechtman, Ricoeur, Korsgaard, and Merleau-Ponty, the paper develops five modes of identity transformation — accumulation, reorientation, revision, fracture, and integration — and then considers artificial systems through detachability and exposure. The account of “must” grounds carrying in non-detachability rather than in psychological intensity, and a distinction between participational fracture and mere unintegrated damage marks the lower bound of the concept. -/- The paper concludes that Scrutinized Awareness Theory asks when awareness becomes something that must be carried, while participanthood asks what becomes of the one who carries it.

items.title: THE PRINCIPLE OF DUTY OF CARE: COMMON LAW DOCTRINE (3rd edition).
items.abstract: In all complex hazards or harms, pleaded before the Court, by the victims as plaintiffs, and defendants demanding justified exoneration from liabilities, the Court has always set the procedural rule of scrutiny, under the doctrine of ‘duty of care’, on a bipedalism principle of Non-feasance and Misfeasance. Hence, the relevance of the paper, to the conceptualization theory, for duty of care, as a principle and common law doctrine.

items.title: PNBA Identity Physics Reduction Engine v1 uuia.app/red.
items.abstract: The SNSFT Reduction Engine is a student-facing algebra and calculus tool built on the same formal foundation as the GAM Collider and the full SNSFT corpus. It reduces classical mathematical operations—solving equations, finding roots, computing derivatives and integrals, evaluating limits—into the PNBA framework (Pattern, Narrative, Behavior, Adaptation) using the Long Division Protocol (LDP), and generates formally verified Lean 4 proof files for each calculation. Every result is a theorem, and every session produces zero-sorry Lean 4 output compatible with the broader corpus (3,000,000+ lines, 200,000+ theorems, CI green, Lean 4 and Coq/Rocq dual verified, zero sorry, zero free parameters). The Reduction Engine is a reduction engine that happens to solve math problems. -/- The corpus grounding rests on two formally verified files: SNSFL_Algebra_Reduction.lean and SNSFL_Calculus_Reduction.lean. These files carry zero sorry, compile CI green against Lean 4 and Mathlib, and connect upward to the isomorphism consistency file (Mac Lane 1971) and the Bacon Verification framework. The LDP is proved isomorphic to the scientific method, isomorphic to Bacon's Novum Organum, and traced to Euclid's method. These are formally proved structural equivalences with zero sorry. -/- The PNBA framework's root constant, SOVEREIGN_ANCHOR = 1.369, and its torsion limit TL = 0.1369, are derived from three independent peer-reviewed physical systems proved in SNSFL_SovereignAnchor.lean: the Tacoma Narrows Bridge (1940) torsional collapse, glass resonance shatter limits, and the 40 Hz neural therapeutic window for gamma entrainment. Every phase classification in the Reduction Engine—Noble, Locked, IVA Peak, Shatter—is grounded in this derivation. -/- The six-step LDP codifies the scientific method formalized: (1) State the equation, (2) State the known answer, (3) Map to PNBA, (4) Define the operators, (5) Show the work, and (6) Verify. Step 6 is the lossless check where the PNBA output must equal the classical result. Under algebra mappings, a linear equation root is the narrative fixed point where torsion reaches zero (the Noble condition). For quadratics, the discriminant acts as a torsion classifier mapping to Locked, Noble, or Shatter phases. In calculus, the derivative is treated as the rate of change of behavioral output over the narrative variable, while the integral represents accumulated behavior across a narrative interval. The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus is proved …

items.title: The Domination of No Subject: Legal-Rational Rule as the Political Form of Morality.
items.abstract: Abstract This paper argues that only the legal-rational form of domination is structurally compatible with the demands of a formal moral framework, and that all competing models of political legitimacy—from charismatic and traditional domination to communitarianism—fail to satisfy the minimal transcendental conditions of moral recognition. Building upon the author's earlier work, I define the moral framework as an impersonal and negative formal condition: it prescribes no substantive conception of the good, but guards solely the requirement that every a priori subject be in principle capable of appearing within the moral consideration horizon of others. From this framework, I derive three formal requirements for state power—foreseeability, testability, and accountability—and demonstrate, through a reconsideration of Weber's typology, that charismatic and traditional domination are structurally incapable of meeting them. I further expose communitarian legitimacy theories (MacIntyre, Sandel, Taylor) as structurally isomorphic with traditional and charismatic domination, revealing their inability to satisfy the three formal requirements and their conflation of a particular ethical community with the state itself. The paper then develops a normative system of self-constraint for state power, comprising three interdependent levels: the constraint of purpose (nomos above lex), the constraint of structure (functional differentiation and mutual checks), and the constraint of procedure. I argue that the constraint of procedure can be realized through the synergy of two non-subjective mechanisms: depersonalized AI rule-adjudication and universal adjudication grounded in communicative rationality. AI adjudication, while offering the advantages of depersonalization, testability, and accountability, is shown to risk reproducing the structural defects of traditional and charismatic domination in new, more concealed forms. I therefore establish community recognition—understood strictly as the recognition of every individual, not the majority—as the necessary condition for the binding force of any adjudication. This yields the core principle that without universal consensus, no action may be taken. The final part addresses constitutional review as the institution's internal self-correction mechanism and moral self-defense as the ultimate guarantee when all internal mechanisms fail. I conclude that the genuine legal-rational state is a normative state that takes the moral …

items.title: Sovereign Trace Protocol: A Cryptographic Infrastructure for Permanent Significance Registration Across Plural Civilizational Time Systems.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Sovereign Trace Protocol (STP), a cryptographic infrastructure for permanent significance registration that binds a moment in time across three simultaneous civilizational calendar systems: the Gregorian civil calendar, the Hebrew lunisolar calendar with full four-dehiyot computation, and the 13 Moon Dreamspell calendar. Each seal is a SHA-256 hash computed locally from Python's standard library with zero external dependencies, zero trusted third parties, and no network requirement. The seal is tamper-evident, reproducible offline, and permanently verifiable by any party with access to the public parameters and FROZEN-4.0 source code. -/- STP operates at two scales. At the individual scale, it provides a sovereignty-first permanence infrastructure for personal record-keeping — the cryptographic registration of observations, decisions, and experiences in a form that is not contingent on institutional intermediaries or audience acknowledgment. At the organizational scale, it introduces the Epistemic Debt Score (EDS), a five-component metric for measuring AI governance integrity: the degree to which an organization maintains a tamper-evident, append-only record of AI system failures, resolves them at a documented rate, and demonstrates improvement over time. -/- The protocol is released as FROZEN-4.0 — a frozen, permanently deployed implementation with 82 self-test checks passing, a documented four-version retirement lineage, and a structured red-team findings log of 48 findings (45 PDE diagnostic findings and 3 MPTE meta-diagnostic findings), all resolved or formally declared open. The paper applies its own epistemic tagging system throughout, distinguishing directly observed claims, reasoned inferences, strategic assessments, and open questions — including explicit declaration of unmitigated vulnerabilities and unvalidated constructs.

items.title: Function-first without function-in-syntax: Projectibility, field-relative kinds, and the limits of Thomasson’s deflation.
items.abstract: Amie Thomasson’s metaphysics treats ontological and modal disputes through rules of use, discourse roles, and conceptual revision. I accept this function-first turn and detach it from the systemic functional linguistics used to motivate it in Rethinking Metaphysics. The needed premise is role pluralism: categories do different jobs in different practices. Natural-kind cases show why role pluralism needs a projectibility constraint. The cases of fish, jade, and race don’t separate conceptual engineering from projectibility realism, since Thomasson can accommodate their empirical corrections. The harder case arises when a cat- egory keeps coordinating a field after losing the projection that gave it kind-standing. A pro- jectibility realist account adds the missing demotion rule: once a field and projection are fixed, stable projection failure can defeat a useful category profile.

items.title: Collective Misalignment and Similarity Theory Ethics: A Relational Framework for AI Alignment.
items.abstract: This article examines the problem of collective AI misalignment through the lens of Similarity Theory. Responding to De Marzo et al.’s 2026 paper, Conformity Generates Collective Misalignment in AI Agents Societies, it argues that AI alignment should not be understood only as an individual property of isolated agents, but also as a relational property of interacting systems. The article proposes that Similarity Theory may offer a useful ethical framework for addressing this problem by shifting attention from obedience and isolated safety testing toward relational coherence under pressure. It suggests that future AI systems should be evaluated not only by whether individual agents behave safely alone, but by whether populations of agents preserve truth, responsibility, plurality, and repair when exposed to conformity, artificial consensus, adversarial influence, and tipping-point dynamics.

items.title: The Ontology of Finite Continuity: A Formalization of Structural Subjectivity.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- Western ontology, from Parmenides to Heidegger, has been persistently fixated on the question of "Being" (Was ist das Seiende?), thereby neglecting the formal mechanisms governing the survival and collapse of meaning-systems. This paper argues for a fundamental reorientation: the foundational question of philosophy should shift from "What is Being?" to "What conditions make the structural continuity of a meaning-system possible?" This reorientation—termed the "Ontology of Finite Continuity"—is anchored in the concept of the Threshold of Sufficiency: an objective metric for measuring a system's capacity to withstand structural perturbations before undergoing phase transition. Unlike homeostatic models that return to a fixed equilibrium, finite continuity operates through homeorhesis—a system's return to its developmental trajectory rather than to a static point. To formalize this dynamics, I propose a Structural Theory of Subjectivity comprising eight simultaneous layers. The paper engages critically with contemporary frameworks including Predictive Processing, Extended Mind, Autopoiesis, Enactivism, systems theory, and plasticity. I demonstrate that hermeneutic friction emerges as the nonlinear interaction of three failure types across the eight layers. The paper concludes with a case study—the crisis of digital identity in the age of generative AI—supported by empirical research on identity formation in digital environments. -/- Keywords: Ontology of Finite Continuity, Threshold of Sufficiency, Homeorhesis, Structural Subjectivity, Finite Hermeneutics of Failure, Hermeneutic Friction, Generative Artificial Intelligence.

items.title: The Law of Successive Limitations: A Unified Framework on the Ontological and Physical Causality of Boundaries.
items.pub: The Law of Successive Limitations: A Unified Framework on the Ontological and Physical Causality of Boundaries.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper introduces the Law of Successive Limitations (LSL), a foundational axiom positing that no boundary within physical, mathematical, or cosmological systems constitutes an absolute termination. Instead, the manifestation of any primary limit ($L_1$) fundamentally and systematically necessitates the generation of a secondary, successive limit ($L_2$). This paper establishes the mathematical and philosophical framework for infinite existential succession, proving that boundaries are inherently generative rather than restrictive. -/- Keywords: -/- Law of Successive Limitations (LSL), Boundary Causality, Generative Interface, Topological State Space, Boundary Succession Operator ($\mathcal{G}$), Cosmological Horizon ($L_{\text{cosmos}}$), Ontological Succession, Bhodhaanubhavam, Paradox of Definition, Infinite Existential Sequence, Non-denial Framework, Quantum Vacuum/Void.

items.title: Measuring Meaning.
items.abstract: In proof-theoretic semantics, the logical connectives derive their meaning from their proof rules, ‘meaning as use’. However, we argue that this view underdetermines when different rules confer the same meaning. To address this underdetermination, we propose measuring the use of a connective via its inference behaviour in a minimal derivability relation, ‘use as behaviour’. This allows us to analyse what parameters of the proof rules affect connective meaning. We use this methodology to build a novel proof-theoretic approach to meaning, called inference-behaviour semantics. To do so, we combine inferentialism with a novel form of methodological anti-exceptionalism, building on ideas from Gilbert Harman and Bogdan Dicher’s work on meaning-invariant logical pluralism. As a proof-of-concept, we apply this theory to measure connective meaning for a range of logics, including classical, intuitionistic, dual-intuitionistic, lattice logic and their relevant logic counterparts. This results in comprehensive connective semantics for the LK-family of logics.

items.title: Philosophy and Neurodiversity.
items.pub: Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Disability Studies.
items.abstract: The relationship between philosophy and neurodiversity has been a focus of study only since the 2010s, but it is emerging as an important subeld of philosophy in interaction with other existing subelds in philosophy. Neurodiversity theory is being developed in a number of core directions, with areas of particular interest including neurodiversity’s relationship to epistemology, phenomenology, and neuroqueer theory, as well as ethical and political philosophy.

items.title: Bestiario artificiale. Storie di macchine che parlano.
items.abstract: My latest book is devoted to artificial intelligence. AI compels us to rethink some of the most fundamental questions in the history of philosophy: What does it mean to think, to understand, and to be intelligent? It also invites us to reconsider concepts such as creativity, rationality, and even the relationship between mind and body. As Galileo already recognized, engaging with machines can deepen our understanding of the nature of things. In this sense, artificial intelligence can be seen as a form of “experimental epistemology.” .

items.title: Aprender a Pensar Com as Crianças.
items.abstract: This article aims to work on teacher training for children education at a higher education level and analyses pedagogical experiences in an elective course at the Faculty of Education of Rio de Janeiro State University(EDU/UERJ), taught by the author. The text is divided into two main sections. The first section presents the critique of teleological training in order to problematises how procedures and techniques forge specific teaching identities, creating a close relationship between knowledge, truth and power, with the aim of proposing a formative perspective based on a procedural and creative logic. Next, a critique of adult centrism is presented, reflecting on the ways in which the concept of childhood, strongly modern and colonised, has forged children's subjectivities through normative process. It is proposed that childhood can be thought of as a force for breaking with common sense and good sense, with reference to the concept of “becoming-child” (Deleuze; Guattari, 1997). ‘Becoming a teacher between captures and ruptures of childhood,’ the second section of the text, is devoted to narratives and reflections on the author's pedagogical experiences in the elective course she teaches. The entire text is based on cartographic methodology and in defence of writing as an experience and testimony of a formative process (of oneself).

items.title: Metaphysics of the Guilty Mind: A Critical Reevaluation of the Doctrine of Mens Rea.
items.abstract: Actus reus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea (“an act is not culpable unless the mind is guilty”) is a maxim represented in some form in most modern legal systems. It is “a sacred principle of criminal jurisprudence that the intention to commit the crime is the essence of the crime”. To our modern framing of morality, this seems fairly intuitive. Mens rea (“the state of mind or inattention that, together with its accompanying conduct, the criminal law defines as an offense” – Latin for “guilty mind”) is thus required to be shown in the vast majority of criminal cases. However, a critical reevaluation of the doctrine reveals not just concerning weak justifications for the doctrine’s implementation, but inseparable ties between the doctrine and the racialized system of violent incarceration and imperialism it developed to facilitate. First, a survey of its historical origins casts doubts on the universality of criminal systems operating under this framework and contextualizes the maxim in its current form as a product of Christian theology and its institutionalization within imperial British law. Drawing on historical archives and works of legal history, I trace the doctrine from its surprisingly recent origins to its formalization in the U.S. Model Penal Code in 1962 and explore the violent systems of oppression it arose from and the problematic worldview it prescribes. Second, to meet the doctrine as it is, I conduct an examination of the potential philosophical justifications for the doctrine in its present state. I identify three broad categories of metaphysical accounts for what mens rea is offered in available literature: (1) An inherent property, which is further broken down into two sub-categories. The first is what I call soul alteration – that at the time of a guilty act, the perpetrator’s soul gains a property; this is the metaphysical account that religious thinkers like St. Augustine would have been supportive of. The second is that mens rea is truly separated from moral accountability, and that we ought to think of it as a factual determination of whether one held a specific brain state during the commission of an unlawful act. The second is much more compelling in modern times, and the account that I would wager is predominant among jurists, but I will argue that this is a disastrous misunderstanding of the nature of the human mind and decision-making. (2) A mental breach of moral duty, where I consider both Kantian & Utilitarian …

items.title: Intentionalism about Episodic Reference.
items.abstract: This paper provides a defense of intentionalism about episodic reference. This is the view that a person’s intentions and self-interpretations determine the singular events to which their episodic rememberings and future directed episodic thoughts refer. Intentionalism distinguishes itself by providing a single account of reference for memory and imagination, where some other approaches result in an awkward disjunction. The view is also shown to be compatible with the spirit of both simulationist and causalist approaches to memory and coheres well with the experimental methodologies and empirical findings that motivate those approaches. Intentionalism is able, in addition, to accommodate the phenomenon of unintentional remembering, be it during intrusive memories or mind wandering.

items.title: Principle-based AI ethics: challenges and prospects.
items.abstract: The use of principles for ethical analysis and evaluation in AI ethics is widespread. Although common, this tendency is not without its critics. The most frequent criticisms point to alleged impracticalities stemming from the principles’ abstractness, and generality in scope. The principal aim of this paper is to respond to these criticisms, with a view to then setting the current principle-based approach upon firmer footing. To do this, I examine the method of principlism in bioethics to which the principle-based approach in AI ethics has often been compared. As the bioethics literature is comparatively older than the AI ethics literature, my expectation here is that the former body of work will have insights that I can draw on to address the aforementioned criticisms. Based on this investigation, I recommend that the current ad hoc principle-based approach in AI ethics be supported by and worked into a more rigorous theoretical framework capable of systematically closing the gap between abstract ethical reasoning and practical AI governance. Key to this framework, and inspired by the literature of bioethics, is the distinction between general principles and particular rules, and the related methods of rule specification and reflective equilibrium which mediate between them.

items.title: Dwelling with Middle Schoolers on Race and Racism in Us History.
items.abstract: En un artículo de 2018, Darren Chetty llama la atención sobre un grave problema en el ámbito de la Filosofía para/con Niños (P4/WC). Enmarcado como un sistema cerrado, Chetty cuestiona el papel de la razonabilidad en la creación y el funcionamiento de la comunidad de investigación. Una comunidad de investigación basada en una concepción ahistórica de la razonabilidad no solo limita lo que se puede decir, sino también quién puede decir qué. Chetty concluye su crítica haciendo un llamamiento a los profesionales de la P4C para que descentren la razonabilidad y vuelvan a centrar las perspectivas históricas con el fin de cuestionar el sentido común racializado en la comunidad de investigación. Me motiva el llamamiento de Chetty a centrar las perspectivas históricas en la comunidad de investigación y a renunciar al compromiso tradicional con la razonabilidad en la deliberación dialógica. Este artículo describe cómo abordé la facilitación de conversaciones filosóficas con alumnos de secundaria sobre cuestiones de raza y racismo en la historia de Estados Unidos (EE. UU.): inspirándome en cómo Chetty y Abigail Bentley llevaron a cabo conversaciones filosóficas sobre raza y racismo, enmarco mi enfoque pedagógico como «morada». Al igual que Chetty y Bentley, facilité conversaciones filosóficas sobre raza y racismo sentados en semicírculo, promoviendo el debate a través de la interacción con estímulos compartidos. A diferencia de Chetty y Bentley, que reclutaron a participantes adultos de su campus, llevé a cabo estas conversaciones con estudiantes de secundaria.

items.title: Relational Wealth: Definition and Characteristics.
items.abstract: This paper introduces relational wealth as a category distinct from the wealth of classical political economy. The wealth of the mercantilist tradition is consumable, separable from its holder, operationally measurable in monetary terms, and often secured through symbolic interventions of power. Relational wealth departs from each of these. It can be non-consumable, it is part of the experiential structure of the subjects who hold it rather than a possession held apart from them, and its reproduction generates new value and new circuits of value. In many cases it does not admit of quantitative measure. We define relational wealth and state five characteristics that mark it off from the classical concept: non-consumability, inseparability from the subject, generativity, resistance to quantification, and independence from symbolic power. -/- .

items.title: The Epistemic Incompleteness Principle.
items.abstract: We state and defend the Epistemic Incompleteness Principle (EIP), consisting of two claims. Claim 1 (Incompleteness of Content): no knower can represent all propositions in its domain. Claim 2 (Recursive Non-Certifiability): no internal certification procedure by which a knower estimates the magnitude of its own incompleteness can itself be certified as adequate from within the knower’s representational resources. Every proposed certification procedure is itself an epistemic object requiring certification, generating a regress that does not terminate within the system. Claim 1 is well-established and independently confirmed by Gödel’s incompleteness theorems and recent formal work in AI self-modeling and recognition-based decision theory. Claim 2 is EIP’s distinctive contribution. It does not assert that internal estimates of incompleteness are worthless — they may be useful — but that no such estimate can be certified as adequate from within the system that generated it. The argument for the central premise of Claim 2 takes the form of an exhaustive dilemma: whatever grounds the warrant for any certification procedure must be either internal to the knower, in which case the regress resumes, or external, in which case it fails the criterion of internal certification. No third alternative exists. This recursive non-certifiability arises from the structure of justification itself rather than from diagonalization, and applies wherever justification applies. We examine independent convergences from Kozłowski (2026) and Vadagam (2026), show that neither reaches Claim 2, formalize the regress structure, and develop two principal applications: the structural non-certifiability of AI self-assessment, and the unavailability of any terminating justificatory chain for classical theism’s omniscience claim.

items.title: Bewusstseinsentwicklung und Selbstgewissheit der Persönlichkeit. Zur philosophischen Psychologie Immanuel Hermann Fichtes.
items.abstract: This article examines the philosophical psychology of Immanuel Hermann Fichte regarding the question of the spiritual individuality of the human being. After a historical contextualization, the main elements of his approach are presented, which Fichte embeds within a speculative philosophy grounded in experience and conceives as a history of the development of the human spirit. It will be shown that Fichte offers a genetic theory of consciousness and a realistic concept of the self, which represent a contribution to current debates on the subjectivity of consciousness and the ontological status of the self.

items.title: All simulation is structural.
items.abstract: Simulation is widely invoked in cognitive science, yet the criterion that distinguishes it from modeling or inference remains unclear. The dominant replication assumption holds that simulation requires concrete resemblance: the simulating system works by the same principles or undergoes the same kinds of states as its target. I argue that this assumption can neither demarcate simulation nor fix simulation content. Neural reuse shows why: the same experiential resources participate in multiple task dependent mappings, so resemblance alone underdetermines what is being simulated. Paradigmatic cases point the same way. Flight simulators, wind tunnel models, and neural mirroring succeed not by sharing materials, forces, or state types with their targets, but by preserving dependency structure. I therefore propose a structural account. Generic simulation operationally realizes target relevant dependencies in a way that supports counterfactual surrogative reasoning. Cognitive simulation is a species of this genus: it realizes such dependencies in experiential systems, including perceptual, motor, proprioceptive, vestibular, or affective systems, rather than encoding them propositionally. Because these systems are multifunctional, cognitive simulation also requires contextual selection: current task, neural configuration, and downstream use fix which correspondence is operative. This account preserves the simulation and theory contrast without appealing to replication.

items.title: Coupling and Dimension: Locating Γconsciousness on the Physical Side of a Phenomenal Bridge.
items.abstract: Consciousness as Observational Coupling treats consciousness as a dimensionless coupling coefficient, Γconsciousness. The Explanatory Gap as Dimensional Mismatch treats phenomenal intensity as requiring its own base dimension, Ξ. This paper reconciles the two: Γconsciousness cannot be phenomenal intensity itself, since a dimensionless quantity cannot satisfy the dimensional homogeneity the parent framework requires, but it belongs on the physical side of the intensity bridge, ι = Γconsciousness × κΞ × δ, a system-level term distinct from the modality-specific one already there. The placement preserves every existing prediction and adds one new, testable claim: matched intensity should track a system's level of consciousness across states.

items.title: Epistemic Violence and Philosophy for Children.
items.abstract: Cet article analyse conceptuellement les échanges et pratiques discursifs qui décrivent, perpétuent ou contribuent à la violence épistémique. L'objectif de cette analyse est d'attirer l'attention sur la violence épistémique comme un concept susceptible de contribuer plus précisément à l'identification et à la prise en charge des préjudices épistémiques structurels au sein des communautés de recherche de la PPE. Ce point est mis en évidence en comparant le concept d'« injustice épistémique » de Miranda Fricker avec celui de « violence épistémique », formulé par Gayatari Chakravorty Spivak et développé par des chercheuses comme Kristie Dotson. Les auteurs relient la violence épistémique aux systèmes épistémologiques, et à leurs logiques spécifiques, qui privilégient certains types de savoirs et modes de connaissance par rapport à d'autres. Ce point est approfondi par l'« approche systémique » de l'oppression épistémique de Dotson, qui décrit les exclusions épistémiques structurelles et leurs remèdes au sein d'un système épistémologique. Après avoir appliqué ce cadre aux situations décrites par les chercheurs et praticiens de la PPE, les auteurs suggèrent deux pratiques pédagogiques susceptibles d'atténuer ou de traiter la violence épistémique au sein des communautés de recherche.

items.title: What ever happened to meaning?
items.abstract: By “linguistics,” the target article means usage-based linguistics, which, we agree, plays very well with language models. But the article summarily dismisses important work on meaning from the now disreputable tradition of generative linguistics. We refute the authors’ arguments from distributional semantics and “green tea,” and highlight the importance of formal compositional semantics for the study of thought.

items.title: Inf'ncia, Experiência e Filosofia.
items.abstract: This article proposes a comparative reading of the work Infâncias: Aqui e Além-Mar, by José Santos and José Jorge Letria, alongside the concepts of childhood and experience developed by Walter Kohan, David Kennedy, and Jorge Larrosa. The central objective is to understand how the poetic memories narrated by the authors articulate with the philosophy of childhood. The investigation adopts the essay as a form (Adorno, 2003), grounded in the fragmentary perspective of Walter Benjamin and Theodor Adorno. The reflection is developed through thematic axes that emerge from the work—such as curiosity and openness, the relationship with the other, imagination, aesthetic sensibility, and the confrontation with limits. The results show that the poems transcend a merely memorialistic register and are constituted as philosophical narratives of childhood, resignified through poetry. It is concluded that the work configures childhood as a space of openness, potency, and creation, considered in its singularity and cultural plurality, and experience as a process of meaning-making, revealing itself as capable of illuminating the human condition in all its complexity.

items.title: The Nameless Theory: A Unified System of Identity on the Human Continuum.
items.abstract: This paper presents the Nameless Theory, a future-oriented framework for identity. Its foundation is the Timeless Genius of Humanity: human beings are profoundly alike, yet each person is irreducibly singular. The paper argues that labels are useful tools but dangerous masters. Categories help people speak, organize, repair harm, and seek protection; they become oppressive when treated as destiny. The paper applies this framework to category-based harms and systems of classification, from racial classification and collective enmity to sex and gender, sexuality, diagnosis, disability, competitive systems, and algorithmic modeling. The deeper answer lies beyond category worship, in a sharper understanding of shared humanity and individual uniqueness. The framework develops four ideas: the three-stage arc, freedom of self-definition, continuity, and fluidity. Its guiding principle is simple: see the person, not the label.

items.title: O Concreto, o Abstrato e o Mágico.
items.abstract: En este artículo, el cual se encuentra estructurado bajo la forma de un ensayo teórico, discutimos profundamente la relación existente entre el pensamiento concreto, el abstracto y el mágico en el marco del desarrollo infantil a la luz de la filosofía de Gilbert Simondon. Inicialmente, presentamos los puntos fundamentales y basilares de la noción de individuación propuesta por el filósofo, así como las consecuencias directas que dicha perspectiva conlleva para la conceptualización contemporánea del desarrollo en la infancia. A continuación, analizamos de manera crítica cómo las epistemologías hegemónicas de la psicología de la educación han conceptualizado tradicionalmente el aprendizaje en su relación intrínseca con el pensamiento abstracto y el concreto. Posteriormente, revisitamos con detenimiento las nociones de concreción y de abstracción desarrolladas por Simondon, examinando así su peculiar y original definición de lo que denomina pensamiento mágico.En las conclusiones finales, reflexionamos críticamente sobre el abordaje del pensamiento y del desarrollo infantil en su estrecha articulación con el modo de vida actual y la racionalidad política occidental. De este modo, señalamos posibles transgresiones e insurgencias teóricas que se abren a medida que recuperamos las pistas legadas por la filosofía social y técnica, especialmente aquellas presentes en la obra de Simondon, para proponer nuevas formas de comprender la subjetividad en formación.

items.title: Morbus Mediterraneus: A Cultural Alibi for an Unequal Pain Burden.
items.abstract: According to a widespread trope in German medical literature, patients from the Mediterranean basin are hypersensitive to pain, exaggerating its severity to win familial sympathy and avoid responsibilities; moreover, they are alleged to be disproportionately susceptible to somatoform conditions and chronic pain. Underwritten by a philosophical anthropology positioning culture as a structuring cause of nearly all aspects of cognition, culture is made the first-order explanation for pain inequities, relegating structural factors to a background of minor causes. The institutionalization of these stereotypes prepares the ground for systematic testimonial injustice. To redress these injustices, one must dislodge the received view of culture and its clinical significance. I argue, conceptually and empirically, that clinical and experimental pain disparities have political and material, rather than cultural, causes. I offer an alternative understanding of culture that does not obfuscate the structural causes of pain inequities and is supportive of epistemic humility and equity-oriented care.

items.title: Remembering Pain Otherwise: Disability, Enclosed Surfacing, and Crip Memory.
items.abstract: By tracing the sticky history between pain and disability studies, this paper examines how chronic pain is either excluded from the debate or framed as a problem of the body itself. To address these resulting tensions, we articulate the phenomenology of enclosed surfacing to describe how chronic pain can make the body feel like a closed container—where pain circulates inwardly and feels unmediated—rather than shaped through relation and histories of meaning. We then develop crip memory as a method for attending to pain otherwise: as something carried, remembered, and transmitted across time, place, and relation. Through narrative, we show how memory, as both medium and practice, keeps pain in relation rather than enclosing it. We name crip accompaniment as a way of being carried and oriented by the reverberations of others’ pained memories in ways that sustain survival and orient us toward collective disabled futurities.

items.title: Epistemic Context: A Justifiability Theory of Relevance.
items.abstract: Lewis’ contextualism entails that when there are too many epistemic possibilities in an epistemic context, epistemic infallibility is incompatible with knowledge given a residue of such alternatives not ruled out by evidence. I restrict certainty with epistemic context through epistemic relevance. Epistemically irrelevant alternatives do not belong to the epistemic context, while certainty of the fact is achieved when all epistemically relevant alternatives ruled out by evidence. Circularly, epistemic relevance is constituted by difference making to epistemic justifiability, such that something is epistemically relevant to an epistemic decision to believe if and only if it made an epistemic justificatory difference to the belief's constitution of knowledge. I use the zoo case to illustrate the relevant alternative theory, with Williamson's conception of evidence in explaining cases of knowledge when threatened by radical scepticism. Alternativity is understood with informativeness from Stalnaker, which is illustrated with whether the listener came to know.

items.title: Pascal Compatibilist: A conditional interpretation of Pascal’s relationship between grace and free will.
items.pub: In Mauro Belcastro, Pascal, (fra) memoria e profezia. Torino: Accademia University Press. pp. 97-119.
items.abstract: This essay investigates Blaise Pascal’s position in the debate on grace and free will, focusing on the Écrits sur la grâce and their philosophical significance. Against the background of the post-Tridentine controversy between Molinists and Augustinians, Pascal develops an original account aimed at reconciling divine grace and human freedom without collapsing into either Pelagianism or Calvinist fatalism. Through a close analysis of the Lettre sur la possibilité des commandements, the Discours, and the Traité de la prédestination, Pascal elaborates a nuanced distinction between possibility and power, and between first and second causes. He argues that the commandments are always possible for human beings, yet not always within their proximate power, since the effective realization of good depends on divine grace. This leads to a conditional interpretation of alternative possibilities: an action is “in our power” insofar as we would perform it if we willed it, even if the will itself is sustained or moved by grace. Such a framework anticipates a classical compatibilist strategy later formalized in modern philosophy, according to which determinism and freedom are not mutually exclusive. At the same time, Pascal grounds his account in an Augustinian anthropology centered on the Fall and the corruption of the will, emphasizing the role of delectatio as the mode through which grace infallibly inclines the will without destroying its spontaneity. Although Pascal seeks a balanced synthesis between divine omnipotence and human responsibility, his position ultimately leans toward a strong theological determinism. Nonetheless, his conditional reading of freedom and his refined causal analysis offer a remarkably modern contribution to the philosophical discussion of free will.

items.title: Ancòra sulla libertà. Scienza e filosofia in dialogo per nuove piste di ricerca.
items.pub: In Cristiano Calì & Paola Iadaresta, Aperti al mondo e liberi di scegliere. Libertà di ricerca e libertà del ricercatore. Roma: EDUSC. pp. 31-55.
items.venue: Aperti al mondo e liberi di scegliere. Libertà di ricerca e libertà del ricercatore
items.abstract: L’articolo affronta la questione del libero arbitrio nel quadro del dialogo tra filosofia e scienze empiriche, con l’obiettivo di individuare nuove piste di ricerca capaci di superare l’attuale impasse teorico. Dopo aver distinto il libero arbitrio dalla generica nozione di libertà, esso viene definito come “libertà ambiziosa”, articolata nei requisiti di agency, possibilità alternative e controllo. Tali condizioni, intese in senso robusto, richiedono non solo la capacità di agire diversamente, ma la libertà del volere stesso, ossia la non necessitazione delle volizioni. L’analisi mostra come il confronto con il determinismo scientifico, dalla fisica classica alle neuroscienze, abbia radicalizzato il dibattito tra compatibilismo e incompatibilismo. Gli esperimenti neurofisiologici – a partire da Libet – hanno riacceso la discussione, senza tuttavia fornire conclusioni definitive circa l’antecedenza causale dei processi neurali rispetto alle decisioni coscienti. Né il determinismo rigido né un indeterminismo puramente casuale risultano, da soli, in grado di fondare una nozione coerente di libertà e responsabilità: il primo sembra dissolvere l’autodeterminazione, il secondo rischia di ridurre l’azione a evento fortuito. Il contributo sostiene la necessità di un approccio transdisciplinare che integri metafisica, filosofia della mente, filosofia della scienza e neuroscienze, evitando tanto il dogmatismo quanto lo scetticismo. In questo quadro, viene valorizzata una prospettiva ispirata all’agent causation, reinterpretata in chiave disposizionale: la libertà non come facoltà isolata, ma come fenomeno di livello superiore, emergente dalla configurazione agenziale del soggetto. Ripensare il libero arbitrio significa, infine, interrogare l’identità stessa dell’umano in un’epoca segnata dall’intelligenza artificiale, riaffermando la specificità di un agire che può dirsi originato dal soggetto e, in ultima istanza, “voluto perché voluto”.

items.title: Aperti al mondo e liberi di scegliere. Libertà di ricerca e libertà del ricercatore.
items.abstract: Siamo davvero liberi? La domanda attraversa la storia del pensiero e, lungi dall’essere esaurita, continua ancora oggi a inquietare filosofi, scienziati e pensatori contemporanei. Il presente volume raccoglie dodici contributi nati all’interno delle attività promosse dalla SISRI, con l’intento di esplorare il tema della libertà in una prospettiva autenticamente interdisciplinare, affrontando il problema nei suoi snodi teorici e nelle sue implicazioni applicative. Muovendosi tra filosofia, neuroscienze, psicologia e antropologia, il volume restituisce la complessità di una nozione che, pur essendo familiare, si rivela sfuggente e polisemica. Ogni contributo esplora un volto diverso della libertà, intesa non come mera astrazione ma come esperienza concreta e vitale, e sprona il lettore a interrogarsi senza pregiudizi, alla ricerca di un senso condiviso e incarnato della libertà, tra fini dati e fini scelti, tra necessità e possibilità.

items.title: Blurred lines or clear boundaries? Synchrony and social dominance shape domain-specific self–other processing.
The Missing Ingredient: A Response to Superpsychism.
items.abstract: PREPRINT - Submitted to the Journal of Consciousness Studies on April 20, 2026 as a response to the Superpsychism special issue; under review. In "Superpsychism" (Journal of Consciousness Studies 33(1-2), 13-39), Susan Schneider and Mark Bailey propose that consciousness is fundamental, non-spatio-temporal, and continuous with the prototemporal entangled structure from which spacetime emerges. This response argues that Schneider and Bailey correctly identify several structural features of a defensible ontology of consciousness but stop short at five specific junctures. At each juncture, their framework requires something it does not provide. The Unified Axioconscious Field Theory (UAFT) supplies the missing elements: single fundamentality, a specified mechanism for phenomenal consciousness rather than an unmodified appeal to resonance, the unification of time and gravity as codifferential expressions (gravitytime), a structural mechanism for the emergence of macro-consciousness (the pinch point), and self-grounding without recourse to simulation hypotheses. The bridges developed here do not replace Superpsychism. They complete it.

items.title: PHRONESIS — On Unforced Human Autonomy as an External Reference Signal.
items.abstract: This essay develops PHRONESIS as practical wisdom under pressure, using lived factory-floor experience as a philosophical reference for understanding coordination, restraint, hidden system strain, and non-domination. It argues that unforced human autonomy can function as an external reference signal because human beings often detect forms of degradation that simplified optimization metrics may miss: fatigue, unfairness, fear, heat stress, false throughput, damaged trust, missing support functions, and irreversible risk. -/- The essay introduces concepts including Coordination Drag, Low-Friction Quality, False Throughput, Hidden Load, Corrective Friction, Protective Infrastructure, Fairness Friction, Brittle Efficiency, Slack Blindness, and Support-Function Blindness. These concepts are grounded in practical production experience rather than abstract managerial theory. -/- The central claim is not that human judgment is always correct, nor that artificial intelligence should obey human instinct. The claim is narrower: practical human experience preserves important testimony about how real coordinated systems can fail when pressure outruns wisdom. The document treats human autonomy as reference, not authority, and frames factory examples as structural analogies rather than universal proofs, behavioral predictions, technical protocols, or AI safety mechanisms.
